title: Dual Rate Surveillance Technician/Operator
description:
This is a dual rate position with responsibilities both as a Surveillance Technician and Surveillance Operator. Will provide support to the Surveillance Technician Supervisor for projects along with Surveillance Operator duties.

Surveillance Technician is responsible for the design, installation, configuration, testing, and maintenance of Surveillance IP CCTV systems and related computer/network infrastructure for Black Hawk Horseshoe and Lady Luck. This role requires advanced technical skills in computer systems, networking, and software integration to ensure compliance, security, and operational efficiency.

Surveillance Operator uses video technology to support safe, secure, and well‑run casino and property operations, helping protect our guests, team members, and company assets.

Surveillance Technician is $30.00/hr.

Surveillance Operator is $24.00/hr.

Surveillance Technician

  • Perform systems analysis to evaluate surveillance technology needs and recommend solutions for hardware, software, and network integration.

  • Design and implement computer-based surveillance systems, including configuration of servers, storage devices, and network components.

  • Develop and maintain software configurations for video management systems, encoders, and matrix switching units.

  • Apply basic programming and scripting for network and system automation tasks.

  • Install, configure, and maintain:

Pan, tilt, and zoom motorized mechanisms.

IP Video cameras, including PTZ, fixed, multi-sensor, 360 degree “fisheye”.

Matrix switching units.

Computers, servers, and network infrastructure supporting surveillance systems.

  • Perform network programming and troubleshooting, including IP addressing, VLAN configuration, and connectivity testing.

  • Conduct system testing and performance analysis to ensure optimal functionality and compliance with regulatory standards.

  • Maintain detailed technical documentation, including system diagrams, configuration logs, and maintenance records.

  • Research emerging technologies and recommend upgrades or new solutions to enhance surveillance capabilities.

  • Manage procurement of hardware/software, including seeking bids and ordering parts.

  • Ensure adherence to Colorado Division of Gaming regulations, Caesars Internal Controls, Surveillance Department Operational Manual, and company policies.

  • Provide technical support and respond to system malfunctions promptly.

  • Perform additional technical projects as assigned.

Surveillance Operator

  • Observe casino and property operations using video surveillance technology to help maintain a safe, secure, and well‑regulated environment for guests, team members, and company assets.

  • After completing required training, demonstrate knowledge and proficiency in monitoring all table games and gaming activities.

  • Monitor slot operations to identify irregular activity, ensure compliance with procedures, and protect company assets.

  • Observe cage, vault, and count room activities to support accuracy, security, and regulatory compliance.

  • Monitor non‑gaming areas of the property, including public spaces and back‑of‑house areas, to promote safety and security.

  • Complete accurate written logs detailing surveillance observations and activities during each shift.

  • Prepare clear, timely written reports documenting observations, incidents, and potential policy or procedural violations.

  • Perform all other duties as assigned in support of the Surveillance department and property operations.

  • Minimum of two years’ experience in computer systems, networking, or electronic surveillance technology.

  • Strong knowledge of computer hardware, operating systems, and network protocols.

  • Familiarity with video management software and IP-based surveillance systems.

  • Ability to apply systems analysis techniques and troubleshoot complex technical issues.

  • Experience with basic programming or scripting preferred.

  • Must be at least 21 years of age.

  • Must be able to obtain and maintain Colorado Support Gaming License

  • Strong verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to clearly convey information and observations.

  • Ability to write neat, clear, and legible reports and maintain accurate written logs.

  • Ability to remain seated for extended periods of time while working in close proximity to other team members and effectively multitask in a monitoring environment.

  • Ability to maintain confidentiality and handle sensitive information with discretion and professionalism.

  • Willingness and ability to work flexible schedules, including nights, weekends, holidays, and overtime as required.

  • Ability to follow company policies, procedures, and regulatory requirements at all times.

  • Ability to work independently while also collaborating effectively with a team.

  • Prior military, security, or law enforcement experience is preferred; computer handling experience is helpful.

title: Project & Policy Analyst III
description:
Senior Clinical Research Coordinators independently coordinate and are accountable for the overall administration of one or more clinical studies, typically requiring advanced-level knowledge and skills. They may provide leadership to lower-level clinical research coordinators and/or other support personnel.

The position is responsible for, and critically important to the overall operational management of clinical research activities. It has direct responsibility for implementing a diverse portfolio of research activities for one or more studies which may include multicenter clinical trials (both NIH and industry-sponsored), local investigator-initiated clinical trials, and/or programmatic clinical research activities, such as a clinical database and biorepository. Positions at this level may perform expert and efficient integration of multiple complex programmatic activities, applying a sophisticated medical knowledge base, substantial leadership skills, effectively working with a variety of people and organizations at UCSF (clinicians, investigators, clinical staff, administration, Committee on Human Research, human resources, contracts and grants) and elsewhere (industry sponsors, coordinating centers, FDA, NIH), exhiting an in-depth knowledge of specific programs.

Reporting to a Principal Investigator (PI) or Director, the incumbent may have central responsibility for ensuring CHR approval and compliance, contract generation, negotiation and approval, subject recruitment, appropriate study testing, and adequate enrollment of multicenter clinical trials, longitudinal cohort studies, local investigator-initiated studies, and biorepository efforts; exercise strong administration and management leadership of clinical research, strong research coordination, and may lead experienced personnel to ensure optimal systems for efficiency, compliance, safety, financial oversight, and contractual expertise in negotiations and execution, as well as create and implement quality improvement processes. This is a position of leadership whose main purpose is to ensure that clinical research commitments are met and that the programs maintain a reputation for excellence in all activities.

The Human Research Program Manager independently manages the day-to-day human research operations of the Bodansky Laboratory and the CHAMP program. Using broad knowledge of clinical research operations, the incumbent coordinates clinical research coordinators (CRCs), prospective participant identification and enrollment workflows, biospecimen collection and transfer, the CHAMP biorepository, regulatory documentation, data and specimen quality, and communication among clinical and laboratory teams. The incumbent translates scientific priorities into reliable operational plans, develops and improves standard operating procedures, tracks deliverables and risks, and resolves diverse operational problems with substantial independence. The role requires excellent organization, judgment, discretion, and interpersonal skill in a sensitive pediatric clinical environment.

Department Overview

The Bodansky Laboratory is part of the UCSF Department of Pediatrics, Division of Pediatric Critical Care Medicine. The laboratory studies pediatric critical illness, immune dysregulation, autoimmunity, and enigmatic pediatric disease by connecting bedside observation, prospective human biospecimen collection, and advanced immune profiling. The lab's human research portfolio includes the CHAMP (Child Health Advanced Molecular Phenotyping) program, a clinical research and biorepository infrastructure designed to learn from children with rare, severe, or incompletely understood inflammatory or immune-mediated illnesses.

The team works closely with patients and families, clinical research coordinators, physicians, nurses, laboratory staff, institutional research offices, and collaborators across UCSF and other institutions. We value scientific rigor, reliable execution, thoughtful stewardship of human biospecimens and data, clear communication, humility, and a deep commitment to improving outcomes for critically ill children.

Research Operations Management

  • Develop project plans, interview key sponsors, and deliver tangible project results.
  • Provide periodic status reports to project executives and coordinate documentation and archiving of project deliverables.
  • Design and perform ad-hoc performance analysis of the projects and the project staff.
  • Build flexible pricing and cost models to test recommended solutions against a range of outcomes/scenarios within the clinic trials and research projects.
  • Perform business process review, operational reviews and design and implement workflow and controls.
  • Develop project-related presentation material for study.
  • Monitor key operating potential for risk to clinics, physicians, staff, and the University (e.g., inappropriate marketing, poor hiring practices, etc.).

HR Management/Administration

  • Assist department with recruit and train clinical research coordinators in collaboration with leadership.
  • Provide guidance to clinical research coordinators and assistants, and help them successfully perform functions including recruitment, scheduling, visit management, subject characterization, and data entry.
  • Train others in federal and local research laws and guidelines.
  • Help manage personnel needs as needed.
  • Independently manages daily operations for the Bodansky Lab human research portfolio and CHAMP program.
  • Builds and maintains work plans, coordinates CRC coverage and priorities, assigns and follows up on operational tasks, leads team huddles, and ensures that participant identification, approach, consent, enrollment, clinical data collection, and follow-up activities occur accurately and on time.
  • Develops and maintains program management and quality systems, including enrollment and specimen trackers, dashboards, issue logs, document-control processes, data-quality checks, staff onboarding tools, and audit-ready files.
  • Analyzes workflow and performance data, identifies gaps, and implements practical process improvements.

Clinical Trials Management

  • Determine interest of groups in trial participation, assess ability to execute protocol safely and properly (analysis of infrastructure, staff, funding needs), negotiate pre-trial agreement and budget, work with Research Services Analyst and Industry Contracts to execute agreement, set up ancillary departments, train staff, assign tasks, create documentation, and ensure local and federal research law compliance.
  • Provide ongoing staff training, ensure continued compliance, coordinate amendment updates, maintain study files, ensure audit readiness, recruit patients, and track enrollment; lead staff to ensure proper close-out of studies, discuss subjects’ options, and ensure that documentation and storage of study files meets legal requirements.
  • Ensure optimal systems are in place to ensure compliance with regulatory requirements for the safe conduct of clinical research. Ensure all CHR documents are up to date.
  • Oversee preparation of new CHR applications; arrange paperwork for renewal of existing protocols; respond to CHR requests for revisions; and coordinate protocol changes with study sponsors.
  • Ensure reporting of protocol violations to study sponsors and reporting of adverse events to the CHR in a timely manner.
  • Respond to requests and reviews of studies from sponsors, study monitors, FDA, and other entities, including complex audits of study performance.

Biorepository and Biospecimen Management

  • Coordinates the CHAMP biorepository and end-to-end biospecimen workflows.
  • Maintains collection plans and SOPs; coordinates collection, labeling, processing handoffs, storage, inventory, retrieval, and shipment.
  • Reconciles specimens with source documentation; monitors chain of custody and freezer/inventory records; and resolves discrepancies with clinical and laboratory partners.
  • Serves as the primary operational liaison among patients and families, CRCs, clinical teams, laboratory personnel, investigators, and internal and external collaborators.
  • Communicates complex research workflows clearly and respectfully, anticipates handoff failures, facilitates meetings, documents decisions, and sustains trusted working relationships in time-sensitive and emotionally sensitive settings.

Risk Management and Regulatory Compliance

  • Protect the University from non-compliance and potential litigation by ensuring contract compliance, meeting local and federal laws, and ensuring compliance with hiring and supervision laws; implement safeguards and proper compliance with federal and local regulations to ensure audit prevention and success.
  • Act as regulatory authority and advisor by training and educating employees and advising leadership and PI’s.
  • Manage audits.
  • Help institute and maintain a Quality Improvement Process.
  • Manages research regulatory and compliance operations in collaboration with the Principal Investigator and UCSF research offices.
  • Prepares and tracks IRB submissions, amendments, renewals, reliance documentation, consent materials, delegation and training records, and required reports.
  • Monitors adherence to approved protocols, privacy requirements, and institutional policies and escalates reportable events appropriately.

Financial Management and Program Support

  • Oversee budgets, invoices, and reimbursements.
  • Ensure billing is appropriate and accurate to avoid improper billing of Medicare, private insurance, or patients.
  • Guide subjects through financial process (private vs. federal trials and their relationship to insurance reimbursement) to ensure accurate payments are made and subject not held responsible.
  • Review budget reports on a monthly basis.
  • Along with the PI, create and maintain the annual study budget, monitoring all items posted on ledgers, and ensuring that future budget projections are consistent with remaining funds.
  • Responsible for ensuring that the use of research funding is in compliance with funding agency protocols.
  • Assist PI in grant development, focusing on budget development.
  • Supports program reporting, study start-up, resource planning, grant and progress-report content, collaboration agreements, and special projects.
  • Prepares concise summaries, presentations, and recommendations for the Principal Investigator and program stakeholders.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in related area and sufficient experience and demonstrated skills to successfully perform the assigned duties and responsibilities and/or equivalent experience/training.
  • Demonstrated ability to develop recruitment strategies in complex environments and differing patient pools, independently identifying recruitment leads, implementing new strategies, and continually adjusting strategies to meet current recruitment goals.
  • In-depth knowledge of clinical research contracts and grants, clinical trials, protocols, FDA regulations, and complex visit structures.
  • Project management skills to oversee the administrative operations of the clinical trials program; knowledge of strategies for recruiting human subjects.
  • Exceptional analytical skills to evaluate the importance and urgency of problems; excellent demonstrated interpersonal, verbal and written communication skills.
  • Ability to analyze complex and non-routine issues requiring innovative solutions.
  • Ability to operate effectively in a changing organizational and technological environment.
  • Ability to assess and respond to audit risk; ability to develop project plans/schedules and motivate team to meet deadlines.
  • Ability to interpret and apply policies and regulations.
  • Financial analysis skills; demonstrated skills in preparing and presenting financial and quantitative analyses, including financial projections and budgets.
  • Significant project and clinical trial management experience or progressively responsible experience in a related position including regulatory and compliance responsibilities.
  • Experience using database software, such as MS Access or FileMaker Pro.

Required Licenses and/or Certifications

  • Ability to obtain certification by the Society of Clinical Research Associates or the Association of Clinical Research Professionals within one year of date of hire.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Fluency in spreadsheet software; ability to develop complex spreadsheets independently; demonstrated skills in audit preparation, execution, and follow-up.
  • Experience in risk management regarding study subjects, federal and non-federal sponsors and regulating bodies.
  • Experience with grant application procedures, personnel documentation, contract generation and subcontracting, preferably at UCSF.
  • Certification by the Society of Clinical Research Associates or the Association of Clinical Research Professionals.

title: Assistant Vice President, Data, Reporting & Platform Enablement
description:
Assistant Vice President, Data, Reporting & Platform Enablement

Global | Permanent or 12-month rotational assignment

About Citco

Citco is a global leader in fund services, corporate governance and related asset services with staff across 50 office locations worldwide. With more than $1.8 trillion in assets under administration, we deliver end-to-end solutions and exceptional service to meet our clients’ needs.

For more information about Citco, please visit www.citco.com

About the Team & Business Line

Fund Administration is Citco’s core business, and our alternative asset and accounting service is one of the industry’s most respected. Our continuous investment in learning and technology solutions means our people are equipped to deliver a seamless client experience.

Strategic Operations is a dedicated function within Private Assets. It brings transformation delivery, project execution, business analysis, operational initiatives and implementation support into one team, reducing the delivery burden on BAU Operations and maintaining ownership from design through adoption.

The group will be split across three distinct focus areas, aligned under two individual leaders:

Operating Model, Product & Client Solutions: led by the Operating Model & Product leader, this area will define how services should run end to end, shape scalable products and solutions, support complex client implementations, and ensure client commitments are operationally deliverable.

Data, Reporting & Platform Enablement: led by the Technology, Data & Delivery leader, this area will define Operations requirements for data, reporting and platforms, strengthen data quality and lineage, and carry solutions through testing, deployment and adoption.

Digital Workflow, Automation & AI: also led by the Technology, Data & Delivery leader, this area will identify and deliver workflow, automation and AI opportunities, establish appropriate controls, and measure whether the expected benefits are realised.

The group works in close partnership with Operations, the Transformation Office, IT, Tactical Operations and Marquee Client teams. Roles may be permanent or approximately 12-month rotational assignments anchored in strategic locations. Rotational colleagues will join from the business, help shape and deliver change, and return to the line with broader project experience.

Your Role

You will support data, reporting and platform delivery, with hands-on ownership of analysis, reporting build and testing.

  • Gather and document data and reporting requirements from Operations teams.

  • Build, test and maintain reporting outputs and analysis used to evidence problems and measure benefits.

  • Investigate data quality issues and trace them back to source.

  • Build and execute test scripts for platform and reporting change, and track defects through to resolution.

  • Support platform implementation tasks across fund structures, new client setups and transitions.

  • Prepare user guidance and support Operations teams through go-live.

  • Maintain project documentation, trackers and status reporting.

About You

You have 4+ years’ experience in private assets accounting or operations, with exposure to reporting or data work.

  • Solid technical knowledge of private assets processes and the data they produce.

  • Hands-on experience building or maintaining reporting, or a clear appetite to develop in that direction.

  • Comfortable working with technology partners and asking the questions needed to get to a root cause.

  • Strong analytical skills, with the ability to interrogate data and evidence a recommendation.

  • Attention to detail and a proven ability to manage several pieces of work at once.

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.

  • Advanced computer skills (Microsoft Excel); exposure to reporting, workflow or automation tooling an advantage.

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Accounting, Finance or Economics; working towards a professional accounting designation an advantage.

What We Expect of the Strategic Operations Team

Regardless of role or focus area, everyone in Strategic Operations is expected to demonstrate the following:

  • Deep technical and operational knowledge — genuine depth in how our processes, data and platforms actually work — the detail that only comes from having run the work.

  • Curiosity — the instinct to ask why a process looks the way it does, to challenge the answer, and to keep asking whether there is a better way.

  • A transformational mindset — comfortable redesigning end to end rather than patching, and prepared to see change through past go-live to the point where it is genuinely adopted.

  • Ownership through to adoption — accountability does not end at delivery; success is measured by whether the change sticks in the business.

  • Commercial and client awareness — an understanding of what we can genuinely run, so that what we commit to a client is deliverable.

  • Global mindset — working across regions, jurisdictions and time zones, and designing solutions that scale beyond a single desk, client or location.

  • Ambition to shape Citco’s future — an appetite to help build the operating model we will run for years, and to be measured on whether it works.

Our Benefits

Your well-being is of paramount importance to us, and central to our success. We provide a range of benefits, training and education support, and flexible working arrangements to help you achieve success in your career while balancing personal needs. Ask us about specific benefits in your location.

We embrace diversity, prioritizing the hiring of people from diverse backgrounds. Our inclusive culture is a source of pride and strength, fostering innovation and mutual respect.

Citco welcomes and encourages applications from people with disabilities. Accommodations are available upon request for candidates taking part in all aspects of the selection process

title: Project Controls Specialist
description:
This Opportunity

WSP is seeking a Project Controls Specialist to join their Project Controls team in Cleveland, OH.

Your Impact

  • Monitor project schedules, identifying cost and scheduling issues and recommending resolutions to the Program Manager.
  • Prepare cost estimates, budgets, forecasts, cash flows, and financial projections; support earned value management (EVM) tracking and reporting.
  • Track and control project costs, including change management, cost coding, commitments, and accruals across active projects.
  • Monitor schedule performance, critical path changes, and float, coordinating with contractors and consultants to resolve variances.
  • Administer cost management/PMIS platforms (EcoSys, Autodesk Forma, or similar); track acquisition packages for reimbursement and support invoice review and processing.

  • Support vendor selection, contractor progress tracking, change order management, and project close-out reporting.

Who You Are

Minimum Requirements:

  • Bachelor's degree in Business, Finance, Accounting, Engineering, Construction Management, or equivalent.

  • 5-7 years of experience in cost controls and scheduling on large-scale capital projects.

  • Strong working knowledge of earned value management (EVM), cost forecasting, and schedule management practices.

  • PMIS/Scheduling: Experience with PMIS platforms such as e-Builder, Procore EcoSys, Autodesk Forma, or Autodesk Construction Cloud, and Primavera P6 or Microsoft Project.

  • Familiarity with Power BI and data reporting concepts sufficient to collaborate with reporting/BI teams and ensure accurate data integration.

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with keen attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate cost and schedule data into clear updates for project teams and stakeholders.

title: Building Technology Systems - Assistant Vice President
description:
This Opportunity

WSP, an award‑winning and innovative multi‑disciplinary engineering consulting firm, is looking for a Building Technology Systems - Assistant Vice President with background in Healthcare Building Technology Systems design for our Denver Office. WSP works closely with architects and owners from around the world on large, complex projects with a focus on sustainability and energy performance of the built environment.

About the Job

Our Engineers work on high quality, high-profile, national and international projects. You will actively participate in leading our department from business development throughout the full project cycle, from the design phase through final construction close-out and commissioning. WSP offers excellent growth opportunities, mentoring junior staff is a key part of this role: Many of our senior leaders started out as young engineers in our firm and we believe in a “promote from within” culture.

Your Impact

  • Project management of large projects and projects for key clients.
  • Project manager on projects involving multiple service lines.
  • Demonstrates understanding and management of client’s expectations for project goals, budget and schedules
  • Responsibility for project accounting including budget monitoring, profitability, contract negotiations and timely resolution with clients.
  • Has full responsibility and accountability for maintaining a portfolio of clients.
  • Develops objectives to increase business with selected clients.
  • Client networking, follow-up on leads, follow-up participation in marketing meetings, strategy sessions, etc.
  • Promotes all WSP service offerings when interacting with clients or potential clients.
  • Prepares proposals and responses to RFP’s and participates at proposal presentations and pursuit interviews.
  • Has full responsibility and accountability for client satisfaction and maintaining a steady level of repeat business.
  • Delegates work properly to senior and non-senior staff; manages and coordinates the work.
  • Ability to mentor staff on a project basis and assure continued advancement of staff from project to project. Identifying and mentoring future Project Leaders.
  • Takes active role in industry events and in professional organizations.
  • Lead designs for building technology systems
  • Coordination and integration of building technology systems with other intelligent building systems

Who You Are

Required Qualifications

  • Possess a four-year Engineering or other higher education degree or equivalent combination of education/training and related work experience in Building Technology Systems design in the following disciplines (Structured Cabling Systems/ AV/Electronic Safety and Security systems)
  • 10+ years’ experience designing high end Building Technology Systems for the Architectural and Electrical consulting industry.
  • At least 5 years’ experience in a supervisory and project management capacity.
  • Experience in various types and sizes of projects including healthcare, science and technology, federal, high rise commercial office, hospitality, educational, data center design and outside plant infrastructure.
  • Design experience of integrated intelligent building systems for Smart Buildings.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with an emphasis on the ability to organize and present design information to clients.
  • AutoCAD and Revit experience desired.
  • Highly proficient in the use of Microsoft Office software.
  • Extensive experience in working directly with clients.
  • Extensive portfolio of medium-to-large healthcare projects.
  • Industry Certifications are preferred BICSI RCDD, CTS-D, CPP, PMP, etc.

WSP provides a comprehensive suite of benefits focused on a providing health and financial stability throughout the employee’s career. title: AI Enablement Lead
description:
Fully remote | Complete engagement job

Founded in Palo Alto by Dr. Andrew Ng and Israel Niezen, Factored helps U.S. companies build and scale world-class AI, ML, and Data teams, powered by the top 1% of LATAM talent, with a defining purpose: To empower brilliant humans, unleash their potential, and amplify their impact in the world.

At Factored, you’ll be part of a community that values learning, ownership, and authenticity, where your growth is personal and your ideas matter. We’re transparent, curious, and collaborative. We strive for excellence, celebrate diversity, encourage curiosity, and build an environment where you can truly thrive.

We are looking for a strategic, client-facing AI Enablement Lead to own the end-to-end enablement lifecycle for our clients adopting Claude and Anthropic technologies. In this role you will lead engagements with enterprise clients, design tailored training proposals, manage the operational delivery of enablement programs, and define and track the KPIs that prove impact. You will also be a capable facilitator who can step into the room for introductory sessions when needed. This is an ideal role for someone who combines consultative instincts, program management rigor, practical AI fluency, and good facilitation skills to lead AI enablement sessions, but whose primary value is in architecting and running programs that drive measurable adoption at scale.

Functional Responsibilities:

  • Lead needs analysis with enterprise clients, understanding their roles, AI maturity, and priorities and translating findings into a clear enablement scope and structured training proposal (objectives, audiences, formats, timeline, and success metrics).
  • Standardizing and tailor existing enablement frameworks and content to each client’s context, adjusting examples, exercises, and depth without rebuilding from scratch.
  • Own the operational delivery of enablement programs end-to-end: scheduling cohorts, coordinating trainers, managing rollout roadmaps, and keeping client stakeholders aligned from kickoff through hand-off.
  • Define, track, and report KPIs: adoption rates, tool usage, satisfaction, business outcomes and use data to iterate on program design and demonstrate ROI.
  • Capture insights across sessions: common questions, content gaps, what works and feed them back to improve activation packages and programs.
  • Facilitate introductory sessions directly when needed, and ensure quality and consistency across all sessions delivered by trainers in the program.
  • Maintain strong, practical fluency with Claude and the Anthropic ecosystem so you can demo live, answer real questions, and translate capabilities into relevant outcomes.

Qualifications:

  • 6–10 years of experience in enablement, technical training, learning & development, customer education, sales engineering, consulting, or a comparable client-facing role, ideally in a technology, SaaS, or AI/ML context, with at least 2–3 years leading enablement programs end-to-end (not only delivering sessions).
  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience; instructional design, adult-learning, program management, or relevant technical certifications are a plus.
  • Proven experience conducting needs analysis or discovery with enterprise clients, translating business context into structured learning programs.
  • Strong ability to design training proposals: defining learning objectives, audience segmentation, session architecture, timelines, and success metrics.
  • Demonstrated experience managing the operational delivery of structured programs or rollouts schedules, cohorts, stakeholders, trainers, and adoption outcomes across an organization.
  • Track record of defining and tracking KPIs for enablement or adoption programs, and using data to iterate and report impact to stakeholders.
  • Strong, hands-on practical fluency with LLMs and AI tools (experience with Claude or the Anthropic ecosystem is a significant plus) comfortable prompting, demoing live, and designing practical workflows.
  • Solid facilitation and presentation skills, with a proven ability to teach and engage mixed audiences, from technical practitioners to business users to executives, even if facilitation is not your primary function.
  • The ability to translate technical capabilities into clear, relevant value for non-technical audiences, and to hold credibility with technical ones.
  • High emotional intelligence, executive presence, and consultative instincts, comfortable navigating client relationships, surfacing challenges, and driving alignment.
  • A genuine passion for teaching and for staying current in a fast-moving field, you actively relearn as the technology evolves.
  • Willingness to travel and deliver on-site with enterprise clients across the US as needed.
  • Excellent English (C1-C2) written and verbal communication skills.

Our Benefits:

  • Ownership through equity participation.
  • Annual company retreat.
  • Education bonus for continuous learning.
  • Company-wide winter break.
  • Paid time off.
  • Optional in-person events and meetups.
  • Tailored career roadmaps.
  • High-performance culture.

At Factored, we believe that passionate, smart people expect honesty and transparency, as well as the freedom to do the best work of their lives while learning and growing as much as possible. Great people enjoy working with other passionate, smart people, so we believe in hiring right, and are very selective about who joins our team. Once we hire you, we will invest in you and support your career and professional growth in many meaningful ways. We hire people who are supremely intelligent and talented, but we recognize that intelligence is not enough. Perhaps more importantly, we look for those who are also passionate about our mission and are honest, diligent, collaborative, kind to others, and fun to be around. Life is too short to work with people who don’t inspire you.
We are a transparent workplace, where EVERYBODY has a voice in building OUR company, and where learning and growth are available to everyone based on their merits, not just on stamps on their resume. As impressive as some of the stamps on our resumes are, we recognize that human talent and passion exist everywhere, and come from many backgrounds, so stamps matter much less than results. All of us are dedicated doers and are highly energetic, focusing vehemently on execution because we know that the best learning happens by doing. We recognize that we are creating OUR COMPANY TOGETHER, which is not only a high-performing fast-growing business but is changing the way the world perceives the quality of technical talent in Latin America. We are fueled by the great positive impact we are making in the places where we do business and are committed to accelerating careers and investing in hundreds (and hopefully thousands) of highly talented data science engineers and data analysts.
In short, our business is about people, so we hire the best people and invest as much as possible in making them fall in love with their work, their learning, and their mission. When not nerding out on data science, we love to make music together, play sports, play games, dance salsa, cook delicious food, brew the best coffee, throw the best parties, and generally have a great time with each other.

title: Front Office Supervisor (m/w/d)
description:

You will be responsible for the performance of tasks associated with emergency response (emergency spill cleanup), hazardous waste clean-up, site-remediation (tank and pit cleaning), equipment decontamination and handling of hazardous materials.

title: Sognepræst i Hune Pastorat, Jammerbugt Provsti, Aalborg Stift
description:
Stillingen som tjenestemandsansat sognepræst i Hune Pastorat, Jammerbugt Provsti er ledig til besættelse den 1. december eller snarest derefter.

Til stillingen er knyttet en forpligtelse som kirkebogsfører og begravelsesmyndighed.

Stilling er på 100 % af fuldtidsbeskæftigelse med en bistandsforpligtelse svarende til 25 % af fuldtidsbeskæftigelse til Jammerbugt Provsti.

Stillingen er en fuldtidsstilling.

Som ny sognepræst får du et introduktionsforløb, hvor du får en mentor, der guider dig igennem i den første tid i embedet og sætter dig nærmere ind i de forskellige arbejdsopgaver, der er for en præst.

I embedsbeskrivelsen fra menighedsrådet kan du læse om sognet og hvilke tanker, menighedsrådet gør sig om det ledige embede. Embedsbeskrivelsen kan læses på Aalborg Stifts hjemmeside .

Har du lyst til at læse mere om sognet og hvordan kirkelivet m.v. er i sognet, kan du også orientere dig på sognets hjemmeside: .

Stillingen er omfattet af Bekendtgørelse af lov om ansættelse i stillinger i folkekirken m.v. (LBK nr. 676 af 13/7/2026)

Stillingen aflønnes efter løngruppe 1 i aftale om aflønning af tjenestemandsansatte præster i folkekirken.

Ud over selve lønnen ydes et rådighedstillæg med et afrundet grundbeløb pr. 31. marts 2012 for en fuldtidsstilling på kr. 43.000,00 årligt. Ved deltidsansættelse vil der ske beregning af tillægget i forhold til ansættelseskvoten.

Stillingen er omfattet af reglerne om Ny Løn, hvorfor det er muligt at ønske en lønforhandling.

Der er knyttet tjenestebolig til stillingen. Tjenesteboligen ligger på adressen Kirkevej 9, 9492 Blokhus.

Boligbidraget for tjenesteboligen excl. udgifter til el, vand og varme udgør på nuværende tidspunkt kr. 5.798,58.

Det forudsættes, at ansøgere har kørekort til almindelig bil (B) og er villig til at bruge egen bil i jobbet.

Er du endnu ikke ordineret, bedes du sende kopi af eksamenspapirer og attest fra Pastoralseminariet sammen med din ansøgning.

Hvis du indstilles til stillingen, vil der blive indhentet børneattest.

Alle kvalificerede ansøgere uanset køn opfordres til at søge stillingen.

Er du interesseret i stillingen og ønsker at sende en ansøgning, bedes du kontakte både menighedsråd og provst for at aftale et tidspunkt for et besøg og en samtale, inden ansøgningsfristen udløber.

Er det første gang du søger embede, bedes du kontakte biskoppens sekretær for at aftale et tidspunkt for en samtale med biskop Thomas Reinholdt Rasmussen, ligeledes inden ansøgningsfristen udløber.

Ansøgningen skal stiles til Kirkeministeriet, men skal sendes til biskoppen over Aalborg Stift pr. mail til: KMAAL-ANSOEGNING@KM.DK og ansøgningen skal være biskoppen i hænde senest opslagets udløbsdato kl. 15.00.

title: Assistant Vice President, Operating Model, Product & Client Solutions
description:
Assistant Vice President, Operating Model, Product & Client Solutions

Global | Permanent or 12-month rotational assignment

About Citco

Citco is a global leader in fund services, corporate governance and related asset services with staff across 50 office locations worldwide. With more than $1.8 trillion in assets under administration, we deliver end-to-end solutions and exceptional service to meet our clients’ needs.

For more information about Citco, please visit www.citco.com

About the Team & Business Line

Fund Administration is Citco’s core business, and our alternative asset and accounting service is one of the industry’s most respected. Our continuous investment in learning and technology solutions means our people are equipped to deliver a seamless client experience.

Strategic Operations is a dedicated function within Private Assets. It brings transformation delivery, project execution, business analysis, operational initiatives and implementation support into one team, reducing the delivery burden on BAU Operations and maintaining ownership from design through adoption.

The group will be split across three distinct focus areas, aligned under two individual leaders:

Operating Model, Product & Client Solutions: led by the Operating Model & Product leader, this area will define how services should run end to end, shape scalable products and solutions, support complex client implementations, and ensure client commitments are operationally deliverable.

Data, Reporting & Platform Enablement: led by the Technology, Data & Delivery leader, this area will define Operations requirements for data, reporting and platforms, strengthen data quality and lineage, and carry solutions through testing, deployment and adoption.

Digital Workflow, Automation & AI: also led by the Technology, Data & Delivery leader, this area will identify and deliver workflow, automation and AI opportunities, establish appropriate controls, and measure whether the expected benefits are realised.

The group works in close partnership with Operations, the Transformation Office, IT, Tactical Operations and Marquee Client teams. Roles may be permanent or approximately 12-month rotational assignments anchored in strategic locations. Rotational colleagues will join from the business, help shape and deliver change, and return to the line with broader project experience.

Your Role

You will support the redesign and delivery of operating model and product change, with hands-on ownership of analysis, testing and implementation tasks.

  • Map current state processes, gather data and evidence where the friction and cost actually sit.

  • Support the design of target state processes, controls and handoffs.

  • Draft business requirements and supporting documentation for review with IT and the Transformation Office.

  • Build and execute test scripts, run UAT cycles and track defects through to resolution.

  • Document client-specific processes and requirements, and evidence where they differ from our standard model.

  • Prepare analysis and materials to support client pitches, POCs and solution design.

  • Support implementation of fund structures, new client setups, onboarding and transitions on our accounting platforms.

  • Maintain the reuse inventory — what was built, for whom, and who else could benefit.

  • Prepare training material and support Operations teams through go-live and into adoption.

  • Maintain project documentation, trackers and status reporting.

About You

You have 4+ years’ experience in private assets accounting or operations, at a fund administrator, fund manager or comparable environment.

  • Solid technical knowledge of private assets processes — general ledger, capital activity, fee calculations, financial statements and investor reporting.

  • Exposure to process improvement, system testing or project work, or a clear appetite to move in that direction.

  • Comfortable engaging both operational teams and technology partners.

  • Strong analytical skills, with the ability to interrogate data and evidence a recommendation.

  • Attention to detail and a proven ability to manage several pieces of work at once.

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.

  • Advanced computer skills (Microsoft Excel); exposure to reporting, workflow or automation tooling an advantage.

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Accounting, Finance or Economics; working towards a professional accounting designation an advantage.

What We Expect of the Strategic Operations Team

Regardless of role or focus area, everyone in Strategic Operations is expected to demonstrate the following:

  • Deep technical and operational knowledge — genuine depth in how our processes, data and platforms actually work — the detail that only comes from having run the work.

  • Curiosity — the instinct to ask why a process looks the way it does, to challenge the answer, and to keep asking whether there is a better way.

  • A transformational mindset — comfortable redesigning end to end rather than patching, and prepared to see change through past go-live to the point where it is genuinely adopted.

  • Ownership through to adoption — accountability does not end at delivery; success is measured by whether the change sticks in the business.

  • Commercial and client awareness — an understanding of what we can genuinely run, so that what we commit to a client is deliverable.

  • Global mindset — working across regions, jurisdictions and time zones, and designing solutions that scale beyond a single desk, client or location.

  • Ambition to shape Citco’s future — an appetite to help build the operating model we will run for years, and to be measured on whether it works.

Our Benefits

Your well-being is of paramount importance to us, and central to our success. We provide a range of benefits, training and education support, and flexible working arrangements to help you achieve success in your career while balancing personal needs. Ask us about specific benefits in your location.

We embrace diversity, prioritizing the hiring of people from diverse backgrounds. Our inclusive culture is a source of pride and strength, fostering innovation and mutual respect.

Citco welcomes and encourages applications from people with disabilities. Accommodations are available upon request for candidates taking part in all aspects of the selection process.

title: Community Health Worker - Inpatient Psychiatry
description:
The Community Health Worker (CHW) is a vital member of the care team who supports patients throughout the care continuum. They provide responsive support, education, advocacy, and care coordination to individuals and families who may be experiencing socioeconomic, mental health, substance use, and/or other related social challenges. This role focuses on improving access to services, strengthening community connections, and supporting individuals in adopting healthier behaviors through client-centered and trauma-informed practices.
CHWs work closely with healthcare providers, social service agencies, school districts and community partners to address social determinants of health and promote health equity within the communities they serve.

  • Collaborate with healthcare providers and community partners
  • Referring patients to providers who can assist them
  • Advocating for patients attempting to make use of public health and government programs
  • Explaining health information in a culturally sensitive, easy-to-understand manner
  • Maintaining accurate records of all patient contacts
  • Protecting patient confidentiality
  • Build trusting relationships with individuals, families, and community members.
  • Provide outreach, education, and support related to mental health, trauma, substance use, and overall well-being.
  • Assist clients in navigating behavioral healthcare and social service systems.
  • Conduct resource referrals and care coordination.
  • Support crisis intervention efforts and safety planning as appropriate.
  • Advocate for clients and promote self-advocacy skills.

Travel Requirements

  • Must be able to travel between various system facilities and off-site locations as needed. - Required

Skills and Abilities

Essential Technical/Motor Skills

  • Hand/eye coordination; speaks clearly; good hearing, ability to use computers, printers and telephone equipment.


Interpersonal Skills

  • Ability to work as member of team and develop trusting relationship quickly.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills including sensitivity to other cultures and ethnicities.


Essential Physical Requirements

Essential Mental Abilities

  • Problem solving skills and ability to interpret data

title: Project Manager
description:
Project Managers provide oversight and direction to their assigned projects. The Project Manager is accountable for planning, managing, and monitoring the project lifecycle to ensure projects are executed within their scope, schedule, budget, quality level, and targeted benefit realization — the project lifecycle includes, from the requirement phase through project retirement closeout. Posted position does not provide visa sponsorship or relocation.

Essential Responsibilities

  • Drive positive customer experience during project execution
  • Provides consultation on proposal development as required
  • Ensures integration of the project activities to meet project cost, schedule, deliverables, and manages scope changes to achieve customer requirements
  • Acts as meeting chair for internal/external Kick-Off meetings
  • Flows down contract requirements to the project team to ensure each team member is aware of his/her obligations
  • Develops and manages the project schedule with input from various departments to ensure alignment with both internal and contractual delivery commitments
  • Conducts project-specific meetings with project stakeholders
  • Responsible for project commercial and contract management
  • Effectively work within a multi-organizational/divisional project environment.
  • Develops and manages Project Management Plans
  • Proactively manages risk (threats and opportunities) and regularly communicates to stakeholders
  • The key point of contact for all communications between the customer and Powell
  • Responsible for the Management of the project’s financials, including revenue budgets, cost budgets and forecasts to ensure the project’s P&L objectives are realized
  • Responsible for progress reporting
  • Ensures project alignment between customer requirements and company objectives to maximize benefit realization
  • Effectively communicate with project stakeholder to ensure timely and transparent information flow
  • Make sound decisions and provide project direction that is well thought out to achieve predictable outcomes
  • Lead and or participate in continuous improvement initiatives
  • Responsible for the adherence to project and company quality levels

Qualifications

  • Bachelor Degree in business, engineering or other related fields from an accredited institution or be a certified Project Management Professional (PMP) or have a management level certification from the Association of Project Management (APM)

Effective abilities with project management, engineering, and accounting software (Primavera, MS Project, ERP system, Agile)

  • Expected Competencies to include:
    • Business Acumen (Business Strategy, Contract Management)
    • Leadership (Inclusiveness, Critical Thinking)
    • Technical Project Management (Professional Execution within a formal framework)
    • Demonstrated ability to lead and influence a matrix-organized team through the lifecycle of a project
    • Strong interpersonal skills with the ability to effectively communicate with all stakeholders
    • Detail-oriented and results-driven
    • Demonstrated ability to make decisions based on limited information
    • Established ability to negotiate with and influence customers, subcontractors and other key stakeholders
    • Strong focus on customer satisfaction
    • Technically astute

Required Experience Is Proportionate With the Selected Job Level

  • The Project Manager I level requires:
    • Bachelor Degree in business, engineering or other related fields from an accredited institution or be a certified Project Management Professional (PMP) or have a management level certification from the Association of Project Management (APM)
    • One (1) year in a titled project management position in the construction, manufacturing, oil & gas and/or power distribution industry, or similarly complex projects
  • The Project Manager II level requires:
    • Bachelor Degree in business, engineering or other related fields from an accredited institution or be a certified Project Management Professional (PMP) or have a management level certification from the Association of Project Management (APM)
    • Three (3) years in a titled project management position in the construction, manufacturing, oil & gas and/or power distribution industry, or similarly complex projects

    • Bachelor Degree in business, engineering or other related fields from an accredited institution
    • Be a certified Project Management Professional (PMP) or have a management level certification from the Association of Project Management (APM)

Working Conditions

The employee typically performs duties in a normal office environment. There may be some work in a manufacturing environment and exposure to the elements of our factory. Additionally, there may be some work performed in the field with exposure to construction sites or active customer facilities.

It is the policy of Powell Industries to promote safe working conditions for ALL employees, to make available where necessary special equipment to protect employees against specific hazards, to reduce accidents through prevention programs, and to establish rules that are designed for the safety of all. It is the responsibility of each employee to adhere to this policy, as well as to observe all safety practices and exercise every precaution for the safety of accidents.

This position is expected to travel approximately 5-10% of the time and must be able to travel with short notice and/or for extended periods.

Physical Requirements

  • Regularly required to use hands to touch, hold, handle, or feel.

This is a 20 bed, mixed Geriatric/Psychiatric co-ed unit which focuses on the treatment of older adults, many of whom are 55 and older, with primary psychiatric diagnoses.

About University of Cincinnati Medical Center

As part of the Clifton Campus of UC Health, Greater Cincinnati’s academic health system, University of Cincinnati Medical Center has served Greater Cincinnati and Northern Kentucky for nearly 200 years. Each year, hundreds of thousands of patients receive care from our world-renowned clinicians and care team. Our experts utilize the most advanced medical knowledge and technology available, providing a level of specialty and subspecialty medical care that is not available anywhere else in Greater Cincinnati.

UC Medical Center is also home to medical breakthroughs- our physician experts conduct basic, translational and clinical research, leading to new therapies and care protocols, and connecting patients to the latest and most advanced treatments. UC Medical Center houses Greater Cincinnati’s only Level I adult trauma center, which includes the right mix of specialist and medical resources available at a moment’s notice for a wide variety of the most complex medical conditions and injuries.

Become part of the only Psychiatric Unit in Southwest Ohio where you can gain exposure to a variety of diagnosis in behavioral health. You will also have the opportunity to see things you won’t see anywhere else and the chance to treat patients that other institutions don’t accept.

The Psychiatric Therapeutic Program Worker (TPW), in collaboration with other members of the healthcare team, is responsible for maintaining a therapeutic milieu and a safe environment for all psychiatric patients on the unit. As a member of the patient care team, the TPW performs selected duties under the direction of the Registered Nurse, to ensure quality patient care.

title: Lead P&C Technician Field Services
description:
WSP is currently initiating a search for a POWER Testing and Energization (PTE) Lead P&C Technician Field Services based in Wisconsin or Minnesota. Successful applicants will be involved in projects with our PTE Team and be a part of a growing organization that is solving problems and supporting client needs in electrical testing and commissioning in utility substations, industrial, and bulk electrical power systems.

This Opportunity

  • Leads field operations for complex construction, environmental, and infrastructure projects by providing expert technical guidance, hands-on execution, and oversight of day‑to‑day site activities
  • Applies extensive field experience and specialized knowledge to support day-to-day site activities, troubleshoot technical challenges, and uphold quality and safety standards while ensuring escalations are made to project leadership for issues involving contractual, schedule, or major scope impacts
  • Coordinates with engineers, scientists, and subcontractors to ensure field tasks are delivered efficiently and in compliance with regulatory and client requirements
  • Supports project delivery by mentoring technicians, managing site logistics, and facilitating effective communication between field crews and project leadership
  • As one of the world’s leading professional services firms, WSP now brings world-class expertise in power delivery, power generation, and project management with the recent acquisition of POWER Engineers, Inc. Our vision is to be the preeminent pure-play global consulting firm for the world’s energy transition—and we need your help.

Your Impact

  • Perform testing and commissioning of Protection and Control systems on high voltage substations
  • Perform on-site hands-on protective relay testing using relay test sets such as Omicron CMC 256/356 or Doble F6150. Examples of relays to be tested are SEL-311L, SEL-387, SEL-487, SEL-421, SEL-351S, GE L90, GE D60 among others
  • Independently execute and validate advanced protection and control testing sequences, ensuring alignment with test plans, applicable standards, and client specifications
  • Follow safety protocols and participate in daily safety briefings and job hazard assessments
  • Use field forms, digital data tools, and mobile applications to document site activities
  • Perform equipment cleaning, inventory control, and calibration as directed
  • Act as a primary field liaison with clients, contractors, vendors, and project managers to communicate progress, risks, and technical concerns
  • Apply expert knowledge of field instrumentation and troubleshoot technical issues with minimal supervision
  • Lead field implementation of site-specific health and safety protocols, job hazard analyses, and quality control procedures
  • Lead field crews, assigning tasks, monitoring performance, and ensuring consistency across work streams
  • Mentor junior and mid-level technicians in technical procedures, safety practices, and proper documentation
  • Support corrective actions by troubleshooting equipment or procedural issues and identifying practical solutions
  • Monitor contractor compliance with site safety plans, environmental controls, and work quality expectations
  • Lead field readiness planning, including tool inspection, site access coordination, utility marking, and weather contingency measures
  • Participate in pre-construction meetings, regulatory inspections, and client walkthroughs as the senior field representative
  • Ensure accurate data collection, reporting, and integration with project systems and internal databases
  • Maintain oversight of fleet vehicles, tools, materials, and inventory to support site productivity
  • Contribute expert technical expertise to incident response, root cause analysis, and continuous improvement initiatives across projects
  • Maintain a strong safety culture and encourage proactive hazard recognition and reporting
  • Exercise responsible and ethical decision-making regarding company funds, resources, and conduct, and adhere to WSP’s Code of Conduct and related policies and procedures
  • Perform additional responsibilities as required by business needs

Who You Are

Required Qualifications

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Minimum of 11 years of experience in the electrical testing industry, including experience in medium and high voltage circuit breakers, power transformers, instrument transformers, and substation protection and controls testing
  • Demonstrable expertise on transmission, generation, or distribution relays (SEL, Basler, Beckwith, and GE families) and protective schemes
  • Advanced technical skills related to protective relays, including relay calibration utilizing test sets/measuring devices such as Omicron CMC 256/356 and Doble F6150, control scheme testing, testing of the sensing CT/PT circuits, ability to upload settings to microprocessor relays, and static & dynamic testing of microprocessor-based protective relays
  • Proven experience with electrical field testing standards, practices, and procedures, such as NETA, IEEE, and NFPA applicable standards
  • Expert knowledge of testing electrical distribution, generation, and transmission projects with voltage levels ranging from 15 kV to 500 kV, including protective relays and circuit breakers
  • Strong understanding of technical software used for testing purposes and data review: ProTesT, Protection Suite, ENOSERV RTS, Omicron Test Universe, and AcSELerator Quickset
  • Demonstrable ability to identify and respond to field challenges and equipment malfunctions
  • Advanced skill in preparing field logs, sketches, and digital reports
  • Physical stamina to work in outdoor and physically demanding conditions.
  • Significant experience collaborating with contractors, technicians, and engineers
  • Demonstrated commitment to field safety, quality, and regulatory compliance
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills for field team collaboration
  • Capability to support a wide variety of tasks in dynamic or changing environments
  • Ability to follow procedures, meet deadlines, and maintain accountability in the field
  • Commitment to continued learning and development in technical field services
  • Understanding of confidentiality and ethical behavior in technical environments
  • Reliable, punctual, and detail-oriented with the ability to work independently or with a team
  • Proven track record of upholding workplace safety and ability to abide by WSP’s health, safety, drug/alcohol, and harassment policies
  • Willingness and physical ability to lift up to 35 pounds individually, and up to 100 pounds with assistance
  • Valid driver’s license and clean driving record
  • Must be willing to travel (up to 80%)

Preferred Qualifications

  • Bachelor of Science in Electrical Engineering or Technology degree in a similar discipline
  • Experience in testing and troubleshooting electromechanical relays
  • Experience in testing and commissioning electrical equipment on high voltage substations such as CTs, CCVTs, PLC systems, and DC systems, including batteries and battery chargers
  • Current OSHA 30-hour or 40-hour HAZWOPER certification

title: Deputy/Assistant Director, AI Development (NAIC Secretariat) (3-year Contract)
description:
What the role is

Artificial intelligence is creating new opportunities to transform businesses, public services and the way people work. Singapore's national AI agenda brings together public-sector agencies, industry, research institutions and other ecosystem partners to strengthen Singapore's AI capabilities, accelerate responsible adoption and deliver meaningful economic and societal outcomes.

Within MAS, the Financial Infrastructure & Artificial Intelligence Office (FIA) leads initiatives that strengthen the foundations for AI innovation in financial services. This includes ecosystem development, strategic partnerships, data and digital infrastructure, industry capability building, and national-level initiatives that support the safe, trusted and effective use of AI across the financial sector.

What you will be working on

This role serves as MAS’ secretariat for all matters relating to the National AI Council (NAIC). You will coordinate MAS' participation in NAIC and related inter-agency platforms, support senior management engagements, drive follow-up on national AI priorities, and ensure that MAS delivers effectively on its commitments under Singapore's national AI agenda. Working closely with internal and external stakeholders, you will help shape MAS' contributions to AI policy, ecosystem development and strategic national initiatives.

This role focuses on shaping and coordinating strategic AI initiatives that support Singapore's national AI priorities for the financial sector. You will work closely with stakeholders across government, industry, academia and technology providers to develop and advance initiatives that strengthen AI adoption, capability development and innovation in financial services. You will help align stakeholders, drive implementation of strategic priorities, and ensure that AI policy, ecosystem development and industry transformation are effectively translated into outcomes.

Your responsibilities will include:

  • National AI Initiatives: Support the development and implementation of strategic AI initiatives that advance Singapore’s national AI priorities for the financial sector, including coordinating stakeholders, tracking milestones and monitoring outcomes

  • Cross-agency Collaboration: Coordinate MAS' participation in strategic AI initiatives involving multiple government agencies and stakeholders

  • Stakeholder engagement: Work closely with government agencies, financial institutions, technology firms, AI companies, research institutions and ecosystem partners to align priorities and drive collective action

  • Programme Coordination: Develop workplans to support MAS' AI related priorities, monitor progress across workstreams and facilitate resolution of implementation issues

  • Secretariat Support: Coordinate inputs, track deliverables, prepare briefing materials and support senior management engagements relating to strategic AI initiatives

What we are looking for

  • At least 5 years of relevant experience in strategy, policy development, programme management, consulting, technology, economic development or the public sector

  • Demonstrated ability to coordinate complex, multi-stakeholder initiatives and translate strategic priorities into executable workplans and outcomes

  • Strong programme and project management capabilities, including experience managing timelines, interdependencies, risks and reporting across multiple workstreams

  • Strong writing and presentation skills, with experience preparing policy papers, senior management briefs, meeting materials and executive-level presentations

  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced environment, manage competing priorities and deliver high-quality work within tight timelines

  • Self-motivated individual with sound judgement, initiative, adaptability and a strong desire to deliver meaningful national impact

You will be working in a fast-paced environment that would require the ability to manage multiple priorities and needs of stakeholders, as well as the agility to respond to changes and developments.

This is a 3-year contract. As part of the shortlisting process for this role, you may be required to complete a medical declaration and/or undergo further assessment.

All applicants will be notified on whether they are shortlisted or not within 4 weeks of the closing date of this job posting.

title: Sognepræst i Mørkhøj Pastorat, Gladsaxe-Herlev Provsti, Helsingør Stift
description:
En stilling som tjenestemandsansat sognepræst i Mørkhøj Pastorat, Gladsaxe-Herlev Provsti, er ledig til besættelse den 1. januar 2027 eller snarest derefter.

Stillingen er en fuldtidsstilling.

Som ny sognepræst får du et introduktionsforløb, hvor du får en mentor, der guider dig igennem i den første tid i embedet og sætter dig nærmere ind i de forskellige arbejdsopgaver, der er for en præst.

På stiftets hjemmeside under ledige stillinger kan du læse embedsbeskrivelsen fra menighedsrådet. Her kan du læse om pastoratet og om, hvilke tanker menighedsrådet gør sig om det ledige embede.

Har du lyst til at læse mere om Mørkhøj Pastorat og hvordan kirkelivet m.v. er i sognet, anbefales det, at du orienterer dig på sognets hjemmeside: Velkommen | Mørkhøj Sogn

Stillingen er omfattet af Bekendtgørelse om menighedsråds medvirken ved ansættelse i præste- og provstestillinger m.m. (BEK nr. 1815 af 29/12/2025)

Stillingen aflønnes efter løngruppe 1 i aftale om aflønning af tjenestemandsansatte præster i Folkekirken.

Ud over selve lønnen ydes et rådighedstillæg med et afrundet grundbeløb pr. 31. marts 2012 for en fuldtidsstilling på kr. 43.000,00 årligt.

Stillingen er omfattet af reglerne om Ny Løn, hvorfor det er muligt at ønske en lønforhandling.

Der er knyttet tjenestebolig til stillingen. Tjenesteboligen ligger på adressen Mørkhøjvej 177 A, 2860 Søborg.

Er du endnu ikke ordineret, bedes du sende kopi af eksamenspapirer og attest fra Pastoralseminariet sammen med din ansøgning.

Hvis du indstilles til stillingen, vil der blive indhentet børneattest.

Alle kvalificerede ansøgere uanset køn opfordres til at søge stillingen.

Er du interesseret i stillingen og ønsker at sende en ansøgning, bedes du kontakte både menighedsråd og provst for at aftale et tidspunkt for et besøg og en samtale, inden ansøgningsfristen udløber.

Er det første gang du søger embede, bedes du kontakte Helsingør Stiftsadministration for at aftale et tidspunkt for en samtale med biskoppen.

Ansøgningen skal stiles til Sundheds- og Kirkeministeriet, men skal sendes til Biskoppen over Helsingør Stift pr. mail til: kmhel@km.dk, og ansøgningen skal være biskoppen i hænde senest opslagets udløbsdato kl. 15.00.
