title: National Account Director
description:
Company Overview

Join us for an enriching journey with Outset, a trailblazing medical device company that is revolutionizing the field of dialysis. Our focus is to create one high performing team, obsessed with progress, in an atmosphere that is brimming with transformative opportunities. The heart of our mission is pioneering a groundbreaking technology that redefines the landscape of dialysis, streamlining complexity and cost, because patients deserve “better” now, not some day.

At Outset we’re revolutionizing an industry and changing lives. We’re impacting what the future of dialysis looks like by creating a first-of-its-kind technology in order to reduce the cost and complexity of dialysis. FDA cleared for use across care settings, from the hospital to the clinic to the home, the Tablo® Hemodialysis System harnesses modern technology for a new holistic approach to dialysis care. We’re giving providers time back to focus on patient care. And we’re giving patients the power to take control of their life and get back to enjoying the things they love.

Position Overview

The National Accounts Director owns the enterprise growth strategy for assigned national health systems, converting contract access into system-wide adoption of Tablo across acute-care settings. This role serves as the quarterback for complex accounts: building executive alignment, establishing clear expansion priorities, removing barriers to facility-level engagement, and coordinating execution across regions and sites.

Success requires equal strength in strategy and follow-through. You'll create top-down and bottom-up account plans, lead C-suite and system-level relationships, and partner with Area Sales Managers and cross-functional teams to translate enterprise opportunity into measurable penetration, predictable revenue, and long-term customer value.

Own the Enterprise Account Strategy

National account growth begins with a clear view of how Outset creates the greatest system-wide value.

  • Develop and own strategic account plans for assigned national health systems, including facility targets, sequencing, growth milestones, and executive engagement priorities.
  • Assess system-level opportunity, installed-base performance, treatment pull-through, whitespace, competitive dynamics, and barriers to adoption.
  • Translate enterprise priorities into coordinated action plans for regions, facilities, and internal partners.
  • Maintain a clear view of account progress, risks, forecast, and next-best actions.

Create Access and Drive System-Wide Penetration

The opportunity is not simply to secure a contract; it is to convert enterprise access into sustained adoption across the system.

  • Build trusted relationships with C-suite, clinical, financial, operational, supply chain, and other system-level stakeholders.
  • Establish and maintain national agreements and remove procurement, contracting, and access barriers that prevent facility-level engagement.
  • Identify opportunities to expand Tablo into additional hospitals, service lines, and acute-care applications within assigned accounts.
  • Lead regular executive business reviews to assess performance, unlock new opportunities, and advance the relationship.
  • Track system-level penetration, treatment pull-through, expansion milestones, and progress against the account plan.

Quarterback Cross-Functional Execution

National accounts require one enterprise strategy and coordinated execution across many teams and geographies.

  • Align ASMs and field leadership on account priorities, facility sequencing, stakeholder engagement, and ownership.
  • Partner with Clinical Sales, Marketing, Finance, Legal, and Operations to support product launches, pricing, demonstrations, implementation, and expansion.
  • Provide field teams with clear account context, tools, resources, and executive air cover while maintaining ownership of the enterprise relationship and strategy.
  • Create scalable practices, references, and expansion approaches that apply across systems.

Build the Value Case and Negotiate

Complex health-system decisions require a compelling case for change and agreements that support durable growth.

  • Lead consultative discovery to understand system priorities, economics, decision dynamics, and adoption requirements.
  • Develop and present business cases, ROI models, and executive recommendations that demonstrate the value of Tablo.
  • Lead complex negotiations involving capital equipment, pricing, software, IT, cybersecurity, compliance, and long-term commercial terms.
  • Secure agreements and annual commitments that support predictable, mutually valuable growth.

Deliver Results

Strong national-account leadership is measured by both enterprise outcomes and disciplined execution.

  • Meet or exceed quarterly and annual sales objectives for assigned accounts.
  • Provide leadership with clear, actionable account plans, forecasts, risks, and progress updates.
  • Represent Outset with executive presence, integrity, sound judgment, and strong follow-through.
  • Comply with all company quality and commercial policies.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience.
  • Ten or more years of successful MedTech or complex healthcare sales experience, including at least five years in capital sales.
  • Demonstrated success growing large health-system or integrated delivery network accounts across multiple sites or regions.
  • Strong consultative-selling, contracting, negotiation, and executive-presentation capability.
  • Experience building alignment across C-suite, clinical, operational, financial, and procurement stakeholders while leading cross-functional work without direct authority.
  • Ability to travel up to 75%.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience leading national or enterprise account strategy in hospitals, health systems, or integrated delivery networks.
  • Experience introducing disruptive technology and scaling adoption across multiple facilities.
  • Experience with software, analytics, EMR integration, or healthcare IT solutions.
  • Experience in dialysis, kidney care, or another complex capital-equipment market.
National Salary Range
National Salary Range (Remote)
$150,000—$150,000 USD

Company Culture

At Outset, we believe every person matters. Every Outsetter, every patient, every caregiver. Because we are here to create a revolution, and we believe in doing that by innovating everywhere with intelligent speed. Our team expects nothing less than our best display of strengths and skills, and we find joy in working together for a common goal. At Outset, we believe that curiosity, ingenuity and conviction in the power of technology will transform the lives of dialysis patients and providers.

We are fueled by the opportunity to give people their lives back. And we believe that it begins with YOU, our future Outsetter. At Outset, we’ve designed a professional world that our employees are honored and impassioned to belong to, one that offers challenge, the ability to collaborate with great people, and opportunities to build skill and expertise in a fulfilling career.

An opportunity at Outset Medical won’t just be about finding a job. Our culture revolves around the principles of moving farther, faster, together, so working here feels like a masterclass in peak performance, for individuals and teams.

title: Sr Transmission Project Manager
description:
This Opportunity

WSP is seeking a Sr Transmission Project Manager for our Power & Energy Program Management Team in St. Louis, MO or Collinsville, IL. The successful candidate will be responsible for managing technical, schedules, quality, and financial aspects of Power and Energy Transmission Line and Substation projects, managing and developing client relationships. This position may be offered remotely from a mutually acceptable WSP office. You must have the ability to travel to a WSP and/or Client office for periodic face-to-face meetings.

Provides project management leadership for the development, execution, management, control, and monitoring of Power Delivery projects, including electric transmission, distribution, and substation infrastructure. Ensures responsibilities across the full project lifecycle—proposal development, planning and project startup, project execution, reporting, and project closeout—are delivered, governed, and audited in alignment with corporate standards and client expectations.

This position is accountable for technical execution, schedules (CPM), financial performance, quality, safety, and client satisfaction on projects of moderate size, complexity, and regional scope. This role applies established project management practices to deliver consistent project outcomes while supporting company, regional, and business line objectives within a dynamic utility and Power Delivery environment.

Your Impact

  • Lead the planning, execution, monitoring, and closeout of multiple concurrent transmission line and substation projects of significant size, complexity, and strategic importance.
  • Provide senior-level project management oversight for scope, schedule, budget, quality, safety, risk, procurement, construction readiness, commissioning, and project closeout activities.
  • Serve as the primary point of accountability for project delivery, proactively identifying issues, driving decisions, escalating risks, and ensuring alignment with client expectations, contractual requirements, and WSP standards.
  • Maintain regular communications with the client including reporting on monthly status, safety incidents, and major issues together with scope and budget impacts.
  • Participate in and oversee problem project reviews, providing input about root cause issues and potential solutions. Assist with developing project recovery plans.
  • Ensure regular project reporting and updates are provided to clients, technical areas, and business unit managers, identifying any emergent issues with scope, risk, and/or budget.
  • Develop, maintain, and communicate integrated project schedules, cost forecasts, performance metrics, and executive-level reporting to support transparent decision-making and portfolio visibility.
  • Manage project financial performance, including budgeting, forecasting, earned value analysis, change management, invoice review, cost control, and margin protection.
  • Lead client engagement and relationship development through proactive communication, issue resolution, strategic alignment, and consistent delivery of high-quality project outcomes.
  • Direct and coordinate multidisciplinary teams, including engineering, project controls, procurement, construction, environmental, permitting, vendors, contractors, and client stakeholders.
  • Establish and maintain project governance practices, including risk registers, decision logs, action tracking, change control, contract compliance, quality reviews, and audit-ready documentation.
  • Guide technical review requirements, resource planning, staffing assignments, and QA/QC expectations to ensure deliverables are complete, accurate, timely, and aligned with project objectives.
  • Mentor project managers, assistant project managers, and project team members by sharing best practices, reinforcing accountability, and supporting consistent project delivery across the program.
  • Collaborate with professionals from a variety of disciplines to provide “trusted advisor” service and future ready solutions for clients.
  • Exercise sound judgment and ethical decision-making regarding company funds, resources, client commitments, and project conduct while adhering to WSP’s Code of Conduct and related policies and procedures.
  • Perform additional responsibilities as required by business and client needs.

Who You Are

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Construction Management, Project Management, Business, or a related field within the Power & Energy market; equivalent combination of education and directly relevant experience may be considered.
  • 12+ years of relevant post-education experience, including significant project management responsibility within the Power Delivery, transmission, substation, utility, or related infrastructure industry.
  • Demonstrated experience managing medium to large, complex transmission line and/or substation projects for electric utility clients, including investor-owned utilities, cooperatives, municipal utilities, independent power producers, or similar organizations.
  • Proven ability to lead multiple concurrent projects or a portfolio of related projects with accountability for scope, schedule, budget, quality, safety, risk, client satisfaction, and overall delivery performance.
  • Advanced understanding of utility project delivery, including engineering, procurement, permitting, environmental coordination, construction readiness, outage coordination, commissioning, closeout, and client reporting requirements.
  • Strong working knowledge of project controls practices, including CPM schedule management, cost forecasting, earned value management, change management, risk management, invoice review, and financial performance tracking.
  • Experience developing and maintaining project governance tools and documentation, including project execution plans, risk registers, decision logs, action item trackers, change logs, QA/QC records, and audit-ready project files.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage client relationships at a senior project level, communicate effectively with client representatives and leadership, resolve issues proactively, and support long-term account and program objectives.
  • Experience leading, coordinating, and influencing multidisciplinary teams, including engineering, project controls, procurement, construction, environmental, permitting, subcontractors, vendors, consultants, and client stakeholders.
  • Ability to provide direction, coaching, and mentorship to project managers, assistant project managers, and project team members while reinforcing accountability, consistency, and adherence to project management best practices.
  • Advanced analytical, organizational, critical thinking, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to assess project performance, anticipate risks, evaluate alternatives, and recommend practical solutions aligned with project and business objectives.
  • Strong business acumen with demonstrated ability to manage project financials, protect margin, support change recovery, evaluate commercial impacts, and make sound decisions involving company funds and client commitments.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to prepare clear project reports, executive summaries, client communications, meeting materials, and presentations for internal and external stakeholders.
  • Advanced proficiency with Microsoft Office applications and project management tools such as Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Project, SharePoint, Primavera P6 or equivalent scheduling tools, and related project controls or reporting systems.
  • Demonstrated ability to work independently, manage competing priorities, adapt to changing project needs, and maintain accountability in a fast-paced utility project environment.
  • Proven commitment to workplace safety, quality, ethics, and compliance, including adherence to WSP’s health, safety, drug/alcohol, harassment, Code of Conduct, and related policies and procedures.
  • Ability to travel periodically to WSP offices, client offices, project sites, or other locations as required by project and business needs.

title: Security Analyst, NHI (Non-Human Identity)
description:
GuidePoint Security provides trusted cybersecurity expertise, solutions and services that help organizations make better decisions and minimize risk. By taking a three-tiered, holistic approach for evaluating security posture and ecosystems, GuidePoint enables some of the nation’s top organizations, such as Fortune 500 companies and U.S. government agencies, to identify threats, optimize resources and integrate best-fit solutions that mitigate risk.

General Description

We are looking for a skilled Security Analyst, NHI to support the discovery, governance, and security of non-human identities — service accounts, application and machine identities, workload identities, secrets, tokens, and certificates — across enterprise, cloud, and DevOps environments. This role will engage in the development of NHI discovery and inventory, risk scoring and prioritization, and lifecycle and remediation programs while providing "Wow Them" service to clients and/or internal customers or co-workers.

The Security Analyst, NHI will be required to demonstrate strong identity security, cloud security, and secrets management skills, lead by influence, and strong business/financial acumen to drive the use of progressive non-human identity security and Zero Trust programs that will align the delivery business objectives and priorities.

About the Non-Human Identity (NHI) Security Practice

The Non-Human Identity (NHI) Security practice is responsible for securing the rapidly growing population of machine and workload identities that power modern enterprise, cloud, and automation environments. We discover, classify, govern, monitor, and remediate non-human identities and their credentials across the organization.

Our team of NHI security analysts, identity architects, and consultants focuses on service and application accounts, workload and machine identities, API identities, secrets, tokens, certificates, and cloud-native credentials — applying Zero Trust, least privilege, and secrets management principles with modern NHI platforms such as Oasis Security, Clutch Security, and Entro. We partner with application owners, DevOps, cloud engineering, infrastructure, and security teams to reduce credential sprawl, eliminate excessive privilege, and deliver measurable, lasting identity security outcomes.

  • Establishing enterprise-wide NHI discovery, inventory, ownership, and lifecycle governance across cloud, on-premises, SaaS, and DevOps environments.
  • Reducing non-human identity risk through risk scoring, remediation of orphaned, stale, and over-privileged identities, and secrets protection.
  • Integrating NHI security with IAM, PAM, CIEM, CSPM, SIEM, and DevSecOps platforms to secure machine-to-machine and emerging AI agent identities.

Roles and Responsibilities:

  • Serve as a senior subject matter expert for Non-Human Identity (NHI) security, including service accounts, application identities, machine identities, workload identities, API identities, secrets, tokens, certificates, and other machine-to-machine credentials.
  • Develop and implement NHI discovery, inventory, classification, ownership, lifecycle management, and governance processes across enterprise environments.
  • Conduct assessments to identify unknown, orphaned, excessive, over-privileged, stale, and high-risk non-human identities.
  • Define and implement NHI security controls aligned with Zero Trust, least privilege, identity security, and secrets management principles.
  • Leverage modern NHI security platforms, preferably Oasis Security, Clutch Security, and Entro, to discover, analyze, monitor, and remediate non-human identities.
  • Develop NHI risk scoring and prioritization models based on privileges, exposure, usage, ownership, credential type, business criticality, and potential blast radius.
  • Analyze NHI relationships and dependencies across applications, infrastructure, cloud environments, APIs, databases, DevOps pipelines, and third-party platforms.
  • Identify and remediate credential sprawl, hardcoded secrets, excessive privileges, unused credentials, unmanaged identities, and insecure authentication mechanisms.
  • Establish NHI ownership and accountability by working with application owners, development teams, infrastructure teams, DevOps, cloud engineering, and security teams.
  • Develop and maintain NHI lifecycle processes covering creation, onboarding, authentication, authorization, rotation, monitoring, certification, suspension, and retirement.
  • Integrate NHI security capabilities with enterprise IAM, PAM, CIEM, CSPM, SIEM, ITSM, secrets management, and DevSecOps platforms.
  • Analyze authentication and activity data to identify anomalous or suspicious behavior involving non-human identities.
  • Support implementation of least privilege and just-in-time access for workloads, applications, APIs, and machine identities.
  • Develop automation to improve NHI discovery, remediation, credential rotation, ownership assignment, and policy enforcement.
  • Define and maintain NHI security standards, procedures, control requirements, and operating processes.
  • Conduct periodic NHI reviews and support access certification, audit, compliance, and risk assessments.
  • Develop dashboards and metrics to track NHI security posture, including inventory coverage, ownership, risk, privilege levels, credential age, remediation status, and policy compliance.
  • Collaborate with PAM and IAM teams to establish clear boundaries and integration between human identity, privileged identity, and non-human identity management.
  • Support NHI strategy, architecture, proof-of-concepts, technology evaluations, and implementation initiatives.
  • Stay current on emerging NHI threats, attack techniques, industry standards, and technologies related to machine identities, workload identities, secrets, APIs, and AI agents.
  • Mentor junior analysts and contribute to the development of NHI security playbooks, standards, and reusable analytical processes.

Required Experience and Education:

  • 5+ years of experience in cybersecurity, IAM, PAM, cloud security, application security, or a related security discipline.
  • 2+ years of experience working with non-human identities, service accounts, application identities, machine identities, workload identities, or secrets management.
  • Strong understanding of the Non-Human Identity security lifecycle, including discovery, classification, ownership, risk assessment, governance, monitoring, remediation, and retirement.
  • Strong understanding of different NHI types, including:
    • Service and application accounts
    • Workload and machine identities
    • API identities and API keys
    • Service principals
    • Access tokens and OAuth credentials
    • SSH keys
    • Certificates
    • Secrets and credentials
    • CI/CD identities
    • Cloud workload identities
    • Containers and Kubernetes identities
    • Robotic/process automation identities
  • Hands-on experience with NHI security, secrets management, PAM, IAM, or identity security platforms.
  • Preferred experience with Oasis Security, Clutch Security, and Entro or comparable NHI security platforms.
  • Experience discovering and analyzing NHIs across cloud, on-premises, SaaS, application, DevOps, and infrastructure environments.
  • Strong understanding of AWS, Azure, and/or GCP identity and access management, including service principals, IAM roles, workload identities, and cloud-native credentials.
  • Understanding of DevOps and CI/CD environments, including GitHub/GitLab, Jenkins, Terraform, Kubernetes, containers, and other automation platforms.
  • Strong understanding of secrets management and credential security, including vaulting, rotation, expiration, and detection of exposed or hardcoded credentials.
  • Experience analyzing identity relationships and access paths to identify excessive privilege, lateral movement opportunities, toxic combinations, and potential attack paths.
  • Strong understanding of Zero Trust, least privilege, identity security, and defense-in-depth principles.
  • Experience integrating security and identity platforms with SIEM, SOAR, ITSM, PAM, IAM, CSPM, CIEM, and DevSecOps tools.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to investigate complex identity relationships and security findings.
  • Ability to work effectively with application owners, developers, DevOps engineers, cloud engineers, infrastructure teams, security architects, and risk/compliance teams.
  • Strong documentation and communication skills, including the ability to translate technical NHI risks into business and security impact.
  • Experience developing security controls, procedures, remediation plans, dashboards, and operational playbooks.
  • Embraces emerging technologies, including AI tools, to work smarter, solve problems, and drive better business outcomes.

Preferred Experience and Education

  • Exposure to NHIM platforms like Oasis Security, Clutch Security, Entro Security.
  • Experience implementing or operating an NHI security program within a large enterprise environment.
  • Experience with CyberArk, Delinea, or BeyondTrust and understanding of how PAM integrates with NHI security.
  • Experience with cloud-native identity technologies such as:
    • AWS IAM Roles and Service Roles
    • Azure Managed Identities and Service Principals
    • GCP Workload Identity
    • Kubernetes Service Accounts
  • Experience with HashiCorp Vault or other enterprise secrets-management platforms.
  • Experience with OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect, SAML, JWTs, API authentication, PKI, certificates, and SSH.
  • Familiarity with NHI attack paths, identity-based attack techniques, credential theft, secret leakage, and machine-to-machine authentication risks.
  • Experience with scripting and automation using Python, PowerShell, REST APIs, or similar technologies.
  • Experience creating NHI risk models, security metrics, dashboards, and executive reporting.
  • Relevant certifications such as CISSP, CCSP, Security+, cloud security certifications, or IAM/PAM certifications.
  • Experience with emerging AI agent identities and AI workload security, including governance of credentials and permissions used by AI agents and autonomous workloads.

Travel Requirements:

  • Up to 10% travel

Physical Requirements:

  • Sedentary work
  • Substantial movement of the wrists, hands, and/or fingers for a minimum of 8 hours a day
  • Required to have close visual acuity to view computer terminal and/or extensive reading for a minimum of 8 hours a day

title: Cyber Engineer IV
description:
The Cyber Engineer IV applies working knowledge of cyber security fundamentals to ensure data security for underwater vehicles. The candidate guides engineering efforts across the Systems Engineering V to deploy intelligent Risk Management Frameworks (RMF) to achieve Authority to Operate (ATO) accreditation. The ideal candidate will have cyber security experience in the Department of War (DoW) world. The candidate should possess a tenacious personality that displays excellent technical judgement, attention to detail, and ability to understand “the big picture”.

OTECH produces and maintains unique underwater systems – typically for US Navy and other US Government Department of Defense customers. Our projects are all one-of-a-kind. Projects range from quick burn to lifecycle management of fielded systems. The ideal candidate for this position is a self-starter who is an effective communicator with excellent critical thinking skills.

  • Identify, analyze and mitigate cyber vulnerabilities for complete underwater systems in accordance with required government specifications.
  • Implement the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) RMF in compliance with program requirements such as DoD standards.
  • Implement Security Technical Implementation Guide (STIG) on various operating systems.
  • Advise on STIG’s applied on customer supplied products.
  • Produce letters of volatility and clearing procedures for in house products, as well as analyzing those produced by vendors.
  • Function as Cyber Engineering Subject Matter Expert (SME) between engineering, project management and the customer.
  • Introduce innovative design concepts to achieve optimal cyber system security.
  • Participate in government audits.
  • Some travel may be required.

Experienced engineers are also expected to take a leadership role within the software group. This includes helping craft and enforce policies and procedures for software development, and mentorship of junior team members.

Essential Qualifications

  • BS degree in Electrical, Computer, Mechanical or Systems Engineering. Commensurate experience will be considered.
  • 10+ years of practical experience in Systems, Software, Cyber Engineering or related field.
  • Work experience with US Department of Defense (DoD) or similarly regulated field.
  • Forward leaning personality that is a strong and effective communicator.
  • Ability to obtain and maintain a US Government Department of Defense Security Clearance.
  • Must be a US citizen.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Familiarity with STIG and NIST policies, guidelines, and procedures.
  • Experience hardening embedded systems (including Linux variants and bare metal) and network devices.
  • Experience utilizing cyber methodologies to both derive and fulfill system level requirements.
  • Experience with the RMF lifecycle and creation of ATO artifacts such as clearing procedures and letters of volatility.
  • Experience designing and implementing security architectures.
  • Experience segregating classified and unclassified data via system design.
  • Experience with Anti Tamper (AT) technology.
  • Experience with AUV’s, ROV’s, the ocean engineering field or robotic systems.

Additional

  • Additional duties as assigned.

We offer a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Employee benefits vary by role, however, may include Health and Wellness, Mental Health, Retirement Savings, Life and Disability, Paid Maternity and Parental Leave, Paid Time Off, Tuition Reimbursement, and an Employee Assistance Program.

Compensation $138,000.00 - $207,500.00

description:

We're looking for a Director of Implementations to own and scale our customer onboarding function. You'll lead a team of TPMs, own the methodology that gets customers live on Casap quickly, and serve as the connective tissue between Sales, Product, Engineering, and Customer Experience.

title: EMT - ice! Seasonal
description:

title: Psychiatric Technician, 6 Ridgeway, Full Time, 12 Hour PM-AFSCME
description:
UC Health is hiring a Psych Tech-Psychiatric Therapeutic Program Worker (TPW) for the 6 Ridgeway Psychiatry for the varies shift at UC Medical Center.

This is a 20 bed, mixed Geriatric/Psychiatric co-ed unit which focuses on the treatment of older adults, many of whom are 55 and older, with primary psychiatric diagnoses.

About University of Cincinnati Medical Center

As part of the Clifton Campus of UC Health, Greater Cincinnati’s academic health system, University of Cincinnati Medical Center has served Greater Cincinnati and Northern Kentucky for nearly 200 years. Each year, hundreds of thousands of patients receive care from our world-renowned clinicians and care team. Our experts utilize the most advanced medical knowledge and technology available, providing a level of specialty and subspecialty medical care that is not available anywhere else in Greater Cincinnati.

UC Medical Center is also home to medical breakthroughs- our physician experts conduct basic, translational and clinical research, leading to new therapies and care protocols, and connecting patients to the latest and most advanced treatments. UC Medical Center houses Greater Cincinnati’s only Level I adult trauma center, which includes the right mix of specialist and medical resources available at a moment’s notice for a wide variety of the most complex medical conditions and injuries.

Become part of the only Psychiatric Unit in Southwest Ohio where you can gain exposure to a variety of diagnosis in behavioral health. You will also have the opportunity to see things you won’t see anywhere else and the chance to treat patients that other institutions don’t accept.

The Psychiatric Therapeutic Program Worker (TPW), in collaboration with other members of the healthcare team, is responsible for maintaining a therapeutic milieu and a safe environment for all psychiatric patients on the unit. As a member of the patient care team, the TPW performs selected duties under the direction of the Registered Nurse, to ensure quality patient care.

  • Engages in population appropriate communication.
  • Has knowledge of growth and development milestones and tasks.
  • Gives clear instructions to patients/family regarding treatment.
  • Involves family/guardian in the assessment, initial treatment and continuing care of the patient.
  • Identifies any physical limitations of the patient and deploys intervention when necessary.
  • Recognizes and responds appropriately to patients/families with behavioral health problems.
  • Interprets population related data and plans care appropriately.
  • Identifies and responds appropriately to different needs resulting from, unique psychological needs or those associated with religious / cultural norms. Performs treatments, administers medication or operates equipment safely.
  • Recognizes and responds to signs/symptoms of abuse or neglect.
  • Establish a therapeutic milieu and provide a safe environment for all psychiatric patients. The Psychiatric Therapeutic Program Worker (TPW), in collaboration with other members of the healthcare team, is responsible for maintaining a therapeutic milieu and a safe environment for all psychiatric patients on the unit. As a member of the patient care team, the TPW performs selected duties under the direction of the Registered Nurse, to ensure quality patient care and staff. This includes monitoring the unit for safety at all times, maintaining a quiet and peaceful atmosphere, managing patient's behavior, preparing room for patient's arrival, orienting patients to the unit, checking belongings for hazardous objects or weapons, securing all belongings in designated areas, provide routine bed checks and secure areas.
  • Provide clinical duties as directed by Registered Nurse. These assignments may include but are not limited to: NIPPAS for vital signs and daily weights, phlebotomy, EKG, finger sticks, assistance with feedings, personal hygiene/grooming, ADL's, collecting meal trays and returning to dietary, clean dining area, provide clean linen and dispose of soiled linen, and assist with inventory control and distribution of supplies and equipment in the clinical areas and hallways.
  • Co-lead treatment groups, i.e., Goals Group, Exercise Group, etc. Participate, organize and direct social and therapeutic leisure time activities, i.e., Bingo, card playing, chess and activities in the Recreation Room. Observe individual behaviors and group interactions and report any major change in patient's behavior and/or medical condition to the RN.
  • Initiate basic psychiatric interventions and provide appropriate redirection as needed. Uses age appropriate communication skills. Provide non-punitive limit setting, appropriate modeling and reinforcement as needed to meet the patient's emotional needs. Assist in physical crisis management as needed and/or assigned.
  • Participate in quality improvement activities. Attend staff meetings, in-service sessions, and crisis intervention programs. Performs other duties as delegated or directed by RN, Clinical Manager or Nursing Supervisor.
  • Transport patients to X-ray, EEG, MRI, clinic appointments, etc.

  • Minimum Required: High School diploma/GED. Preferred: Relevant college coursework.
  • STNA certification preferred or college-level coursework in nursing/psychiatry/social work.
  • Minimum Required: Six months direct patient care experience in psychiatric setting or equivalent college-level coursework in nursing/psychology/social work.
  • Preferred: Specialized training in phlebotomy, vitals signs, and assistance with activities of daily living experience.
  • For employees working in UCMC Psychiatric Services, NCI-APS (Nonviolent Crisis Intervention with Advanced Physical Skills) Certification must be obtained within 90 days of hire.

Join our team as a psychiatric technician in our Psychiatric Emergency department. and work alongside the best and brightest clinical teams collaborating toward our common purpose: to advance healing and reduce suffering.

Join our team to BE UC Health. Be Extraordinary. Be Supported. Be Hope. Apply Today!

About UC Health

UC Health is an integrated academic health system serving Greater Cincinnati and Northern Kentucky. In partnership with the University of Cincinnati, UC Health combines clinical expertise and compassion with research and teaching—a combination that provides patients with options for even the most complex situations. Members of UC Health include: UC Medical Center, West Chester Hospital, University of Cincinnati Physicians and UC Health Ambulatory Services (with more than 900 board-certified clinicians and surgeons), Lindner Center of HOPE and several specialized institutes including: UC Gardner Neuroscience Institute and the University of Cincinnati Cancer Center. Many UC Health locations have received national recognition for outstanding quality and patient satisfaction. Learn more at uchealth.com.

At UC Health, we're proud to have the best and brightest teams and clinicians collaborating toward our common purpose: to advance healing and reduce suffering.

As the region's adult academic health system, we strive for innovation and provide world-class care for not only our community, but patients from all over the world. Join our team and you'll be able to develop your skills, grow your career, build relationships with your peers and patients, and help us be a source of hope for our friends and neighbors.

UC Health is an EEO employer.

title: Business Energy Efficiency Engineer
description:
DNV – Energy Systems is seeking a Business Energy Efficiency Engineer to join our New Mexico team supporting the PNM Business Energy Efficiency Programs (BEEP).

This is a high-accountability, results-driven position focused on engaging commercial, industrial, governmental, and multifamily customers; supporting trade allies.

The ideal candidate will have experience with building energy performance (e.g., lighting, HVAC and their control systems, and building envelop components) to perform building audits (or assessments) and provide expert advice for customers while recommending specific upgrades to electric systems through exemplary customer service. You will also advise customers on the improved efficiency that the upgrades will bring. This position will provide excellent customer service and help customers implement, improve and demonstrate their commitment to improved energy management in their building.

This position will be in our Albuquerque New Mexico or Phoenix, AZ, presenting a dynamic hybrid schedule where employees will typically spend three (3) days per week working from either a DNV office or client location/site.

Further details regarding role-specific requirements will be shared during the interview process.



What You’ll Do

  • Conduct customer site audits and assessments, virtual and in-person, to verify existing equipment and operating conditions, and recommend energy-saving equipment installations and operational changes.
  • Recognize, identify, and catalog energy-saving equipment types, consulting with customers, facility managers, and contractors as needed. Identify and document opportunities for installing energy efficiency products.
  • Build rapport with customers on site. Educate customers about the energy efficiency program and advise them on energy-consuming equipment, such as lighting, HVAC, building envelope, and controls, in their facility.
  • Interpret customer billing data, meter data, rate information, and similar technical information, and communicate findings to customers in layperson terms.
  • Enter and analyze energy savings opportunity and customer building data using spreadsheets, report templates, and web-based tools. Author and edit weekly and monthly reports in accordance with client requirements and standards.
  • Review and verify energy savings calculations, and guide other staff on best practices across energy-saving technologies, including lighting, HVAC, fans, pumps, air compression, and industrial process applications.
  • Perform site-specific engineering analysis and evaluation of energy efficiency projects involving industrial process equipment such as pumps, fans, and compressed air systems, complex central plant systems, and advanced HVAC equipment. Assess existing and emerging measures, incorporating performance trends and operational data to support updates.
  • Complete technical and financial analyses for program applicants.
  • Perform building energy use assessments and building simulations using software packages such as eQuest, DOE2.2, EnergyPro, and Trace.
  • Communicate technical and program-related information through presentations, trainings, and stakeholder engagement events.
  • Generous paid time off (vacation, sick days, company holidays, personal days)
  • Multiple Medical and Dental benefit plans to choose from, Vision benefits
  • Spending accounts – FSA, Dependent Care, Commuter Benefits, company-seeded HSA
  • Employer-paid, therapist-led, virtual care services through Talkspace
  • 401(k) with company match
  • Company provided life insurance, short-term, and long-term disability benefits
  • Education reimbursement program
  • Flexible work schedule with hybrid opportunities
  • Charitable Matched Giving and Volunteer Rewards through our Impact Program
  • Volunteer time off (VTO) paid by the company
  • Career advancement opportunities

title: Assembler II
description:
Powell is an engineered manufacturer of switchgear and electrical equipment for the power generation industry. An Assembler II is responsible for putting together components or parts to create finished products. Four 10s Schedule: Monday-Thursday 4:30am-3:00pm.

Position Summary

An Assembler II is responsible for putting together components or parts to create finished products. They follow blueprints, work instructions, or diagrams to assemble products using various tools and equipment. Assemblers may work in manufacturing or production environments and may be required to perform quality checks and ensure that products meet specifications. They may also be responsible for maintaining a clean and organized work area and reporting any issues or defects to supervisors. Attention to detail, manual dexterity, and the ability to work as part of a team are important skills for an Assembler.

Supervision

None

Essential Responsibilities

•Build and assemble mechanical components for Switchgear and/or Breaker units according to engineering drawings and customer specifications using master copy, spec sheet, front elevation and WO files

•Perform maintenance and proper use of tools.

•Perform in process inspections; ensure quality by following standard work instructions and identifying any potential risks to product quality.

•Perform all ship prep functions including splitting gear.

•Assist in Root Cause Analysis on engineering changes and correct discrepancies

•Assist a small team of employees to complete a specific task assigned as assigned by lead assembler and/or supervisor

•Perform mechanical adjustments for switchgear

•Promote a safety culture as well as attend all safety meetings.

•Ensure that work areas remain clean and well organized.

Minimum Qualifications

•Minimum education level of a High School Diploma or General Education Equivalent Diploma is preferred.

•2-4 years of experience in assembling medium to large sized metal boxes/enclosures or electrical switchgear

•Ability to read a tape measure (including conversions from fraction to decimal and conversely from decimal to fraction and metric to imperial).

•Must have a basic command of the English language, both written and verbal.

•Basic knowledge of operating desktop computer.

•Safely use variety of hand/power tools.

•Lift up to 50lbs using proper lifting techniques.

Preferred Qualifications

•Basic MES system knowledge, Oracle preferred.

Skills, Abilities & Other Requirements

•Read and understand spec sheets and follow proper use of hardware by spec requirements.

•Able to read and understand single and three-line drawings, including symbols

•Able to interpret and execute change orders

•Able to identify part discrepancies and properly write HFDs for corrections

•Knowledge of mechanical drawings and designs

•Ability to follow direction from Senior Assemblers and Lead Assemblers.

•Effectively demonstrates on-time delivery and the ability to stay focused on goals and responsibilities.

•Self-starter with ability to take on multiple tasks with a drive to succeed.

•Challenges the status quo; looks for better or more efficient ways to get results.

•Ability to adapt to new ideas, technology, processes or product changes.

•Believes and displays through actions that our customers represent our current success and remain vital to our future growth.

•Demonstrates integrity and ethical decision making.

•Conscientious, thorough, accurate, and reliable when performing and completing job tasks.

•Able to work effectively within your team and around other departments and their activities.

•Ability to learn and adhere to all manufacturing policies and practices to ensure adherence to ISO requirements.

Working & Environmental Conditions

Working Conditions

· Safety sensitive position in a temperature-controlled manufacturing or industrial environment with occasional outside activities.

· Required to wear personal protective equipment (PPE) (i.e., safety shoes, hard hats, bump caps, safety glasses, hearing protection, safety harnesses as required) and respirators when required.

· Must be able to work from all type of ladders (step ladders, "A" frame ladders, etc.)

· Working at heights usually no higher than 20 feet in the air on an elevated structure using proper lift equipment and Fall Protection Equipment.

Physical Requirements

· Able to maintain body equilibrium and agility to prevent falling when walking, standing, crouching, ascending or descending stairs or step ladders

· Bending the body at the waist, the legs at the knees, and extending arms and hands in any direction

· Continuous standing and walking

· Able to use upper extremities frequently, work with both arms above shoulders and use both arms at full length frequently.

· Must be able to meet physical lifting demand up to 50lbs.

· Frequent use of hand tools and power tools

More Information

Mycronic is a global high-tech company whose innovative solutions have been advancing electronics technology for over 50 years. Overview

We are looking for an experienced Project Manager to join Mycronic’s Global Technologies division working within our Die Bonding business line. It is an exciting time to join our team!

In the world of microelectronics and optoelectronics, precision is everything. Our market-leading position has been built over decades by delivering flexible, ultra-precise die bonding systems that improve our customers’ performance each and every day. Innovation has been key to our success and continues today with new products and derivatives of our products being launched each year. We don’t sit still! title: Library Director
description:
WAGE: $61.76 - $95.73
DEPARTMENT: Library
BENEFITS: Health, Dental, Vision, Retirement, 401k match, Life Insurance, Short-term Disability, Accident, Critical Illness
PERSONNEL STATUS: Full Time FLSA & Merit Exempt

IMPORTANT NOTE:

Please submit a current resume and a thoughtful cover letter showing your leadership philosophy and vision for public library service. Also include in your submittal three current professional references who can speak to your leadership experience and qualifications for this position. References should include current library supervisor, governing authority, elected official, board chair, or other individual to whom you currently directly report. References will be contacted only if you are being seriously considered for appointment.

JOB OVERVIEW:

Weber County Library System is seeking an experienced, innovative, and community-minded professional to serve as its next Library Director. This is an exceptional opportunity to lead a highly regarded public library system serving approximately 278,000 Weber County residents through five library locations and a workforce of more than 170 employees.

The Library Director is the chief executive and senior professional librarian of the Weber County Library System. Reporting to the Library Board of Trustees and county officials, the Director provides executive leadership for library services, personnel, finances, facilities, collections, technology, programs, and community relations.

The ideal candidate will bring strong public library experience, sound administrative judgment, excellent communication skills, and the ability to lead a complex organization while maintaining a clear focus on public service and measurable results.

We are looking for a director who balances a deep passion for librarianship with the mindset of an executive, someone who sees budgets, modern facilities, and evolving technologies as creative tools to empower our community.

You will oversee:

Exceptional "Third Space" Facilities: Our five unique locations are designed for hands-on experimentation and community gathering. They feature incredible public amenities including black box theaters, modern makerspaces, tech labs, art galleries, cafes, and outdoor amphitheaters.

A Talented, Passionate Workforce: You will lead a dedicated team of more than 170 professionals and support staff spanning public service, technical processing—including cataloging and acquisitions—IT, operations, marketing, and administration. Together, this collaborative workforce is excited to partner with you to continually rethink and elevate what public service can achieve.

Rich Collections & Intellectual Freedom: We steward more than 757,000 physical items alongside a rapidly growing digital catalog. Our collections directly reflect our core commitment to education, intellectual freedom, equity, and diverse perspectives.

A Natural Culture of Innovation: From being early automation pioneers to deploying our custom BrAIny artificial intelligence services in 2026, our library is an evolving learning platform that shapes how our community works, creates, and communicates.

Strong, Stable Fiscal Foundation: Backed securely by property taxes, our 2026 operating budget is $17.2 million, complemented by a Capital Improvement Fund of more than $3,000,000. As the Library’s fiscal officer, you will have the financial runway to maintain excellence and plan meaningfully for the future.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:

The Director provides executive leadership and strategic direction for a dynamic, five-location county library system, working closely with the Library Board of Trustees, county leadership, employees, and the community to advance the Library’s mission and long-term success. The position leads systemwide planning, policy implementation, budgeting, collections, facilities, technology, public services, communications, and organizational development while ensuring responsible stewardship of public resources and compliance with applicable laws and professional standards. As the Library’s chief executive and public representative, the Director builds strong community and governmental partnerships, champions intellectual freedom, identifies opportunities for innovation and funding, and positions the Library to meet the evolving needs of Weber County residents.

Any one position may not include all of the duties listed, nor do the listed examples include all duties which may be found in positions of this class. Applicants must be prepared to demonstrate the ability to perform the essential functions of the job with or without reasonable accommodation.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES:

Oversight of the county library system and its 170+ employees

Recruit, hire, train, evaluate, discipline, and act to dismiss, retain, or promote a competent professional workforce for the achievement and delivery of superior library service

Analyze workflow, scheduling, and use of leave

EDUCATION/EXPERIENCE:

Education: A Master's degree in Library and Information Science (MLIS) from an American Library Association-accredited program is required.

Experience: A proven record of progressive leadership in a public library system of significant size and complexity, with a minimum of 10 years of professional library experience, including at least eight years of administrative experience overseeing personnel, budgets, services, and, preferably, multi-site facilities.

Preferred Education and Experience: A second Master's degree in Public Administration (MPA) or an equivalent degree is highly valued, particularly with preparation in organizational leadership, finance, and operations. Executive leadership experience, including demonstrated experience working with elected officials and governing boards, may also be considered.

Please submit a current resume and a thoughtful cover letter showing your leadership philosophy and vision for public library service. Also include in your submittal three current professional references who can speak to your leadership experience and qualifications for this position. References should include current library supervisor, governing authority, elected official, board chair, or other individual to whom you currently directly report. References will be contacted only if you are being seriously considered for appointment.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES (KSA):

Knowledge of:

Substantial working knowledge of public library trends, theories, and major services and programs

Substantial working knowledge of the principles and practices of library science including reference services, collection development, readers’ advisory service, cataloging, and technology services

Substantial demonstrated experience with the provision of library services to all demographics, including the elderly, children, students, adult learners, and those living in poverty

Substantial working knowledge of public service management theory and practice, including customer satisfaction, strategic planning for results, staff development and supervision, time management, organizational skills, community relations, and publicity and promotion techniques

Thorough knowledge of and ability to develop and interpret library board policies and administrative procedures

Understanding of the relationships and responsibilities of library divisions and buildings

Understanding of library vision, mission, and roles (guiding principles), and the general role of public libraries within a community

Understanding of librarianship and its foundational documents, including the Library Bill of Rights, Code of Ethics, and the Freedom to Read Statement

Skills and Abilities:

Demonstrated ability to employ management techniques effectively in directing, planning, organizing, staffing, coordinating, budgeting, and evaluating the library's operation

Excellent interpersonal skills with the demonstrated ability to facilitate discussion and build consensus

Excellent communication skills, including public speaking ability

Excellent business and problem-solving skills

Ability to supervise employees and delegate responsibility, fairly and in accordance with board policies and state and federal laws

Ability to work productively within lines of authority and to accept decisions made by the board

Ability to function effectively in a political environment, where real-world compromises are sometimes necessary for the health of the organization

Ability to think abstractly, understand complex ideas, and see the whole picture

Ability to think analytically and to manipulate statistical data

Ability to handle complaints and controversy with objectivity

Desire to meet and serve the library's user community

Ability to organize job duties and work independently, handling multiple, competing priorities and accommodating deadlines

Creativity to envision and communicate directives for library programs and services

Ability to employ management techniques effectively in directing, planning, organizing, staffing, coordinating, budgeting, and evaluating the library's operation

Ability to exhibit good judgment according to a formalist system of ethics and establish a cordial and effective working relationship with the public, support employees, colleagues, board members, and county officials

YOUR SPECIAL QUALIFICATIONS:

Availability for morning, afternoon, evening, weekend, and some holiday shifts

Ability and willingness to engage effectively with individuals from all segments of the community, including those who may be experiencing significant social, economic, or personal challenges.

Preference given for fluency in more than one language

Pre-employment drug screening and criminal background check are required

Remote work not authorized

PHYSICAL DEMANDS:

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to walk, stand, sit, talk, hear, balance, and reach. Must use hands and fingers to operate a computer. The employee is required to lift up to fifteen pounds, and occasionally up to fifty pounds. Must be able to move about the work area, talk clearly with customers and employees, and hear responses. Must have excellent close vision and good distance vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and ability to adjust focus.

WORK ENVIRONMENT:

The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

The Library Director works primarily in an office environment but regularly visits Library facilities and interacts with employees, Library users, community members, county officials, Board members, and community organizations.

The position requires flexibility to work morning, afternoon, evening, weekend, and holiday hours as necessary to fulfill the responsibilities of a system-wide executive.

Local, regional, and national travel may be required for internal and external meetings, professional conferences, and other Library business.

Professional employees may be required to adjust their responsibilities to address emergencies, special projects, and other organizational needs.

title: Software Engineer - CommBank iQ
description:
Who is Quantium?

Quantium is a world leader in data science and artificial intelligence. Established in Australia in 2002, Quantium is a global team of more than 1,200 people across 14 locations with a unique blend of capabilities across product and consulting services to help businesses unlock value from data and analytics. Quantium partners with the world's largest corporations to forge a better, more intelligent world.

CommBank iQ (CBAiQ) is a joint venture between Quantium and CommBank. It brings together Quantium's data science and AI expertise with CommBank's scale to deliver products and insights that drive better outcomes for customers and businesses.

We have an opportunity for a Software Engineer to join the CBAiQ engineering team in Sydney. This is a hands-on, full-stack role in a small team of around seven engineers, where you will work across the back end, front end and cloud, and use AI every day to build, learn and solve problems. You will get real exposure to the product, with plenty of room to learn and grow.

How will you make an impact?

  • Full-stack delivery: Design, build and maintain features across the stack, from Python services and databases through to React front ends and AWS infrastructure
  • AI-assisted engineering: Use AI tools day to day to explore unfamiliar areas, move faster and lift the quality of your work
  • Agent development: Help build AI agents using CommBank's governed agent framework, as the business moves towards AI and agents
  • Working within a bank: Learn how to build well within the governance, security and risk requirements of a major bank, balancing pace with care
  • Team contribution: Join in on problem solving, share ideas openly and help lift team culture as part of a close-knit engineering group

The superpowers you’ll be bringing to the team:

  • Full-stack foundations: Experience or strong interest across back end, front end and cloud, with Python and React as your main tools and a working knowledge of databases
  • AWS knowledge: An understanding of AWS services and environments, with the curiosity to deepen it as you go
  • Data awareness: Exposure to working with data teams or data-related projects is valued
  • AI fluency: Comfort using AI to navigate new problems and unfamiliar technology
  • Curious and collaborative: An eagerness to learn, a habit of taking initiative and the confidence to contribute ideas to solve problems as a team

Remember – you might not tick all the boxes, but don’t let that from stopping you applying. We’re more interested in how you work, your ability to solve problems and think big.

What could your Quantium Experience look like?

Working at Quantium will allow you to challenge your imagination. You will get to solve complex problems using rigor, precision and by asking great questions – but it also means you can think big, outside the box and push your problem-solving skills to the max.

By joining the Quantium team, you’ll get to:

  • Forge your path: So many of our team have moved around different teams or offices. You’ll be in the driver’s seat, and we empower you to make your career your own.
  • Find your kind: Embrace diversity and connect with your tribe (think foodies, dog lovers, readers, or runners).
  • Make an impact: Leave your mark. Your contributions resonate, regardless of your role or rank.

But wait, there’s more!

We’ve got some pretty sweet perks:

  • Flexible work arrangements: Achieve work life balance at your own pace with hybrid and flexible work arrangements.
  • Continuous learning: Our vision is empowering analytics talent to thrive. The Analytics Community fosters the development of individuals, thought leadership and technical excellence at Quantium through building strong connections, fostering collaboration, and co-creation of best practice.
  • Remote working: Embrace the opportunity to work outside of your assigned home location for up to 2 months every year.

Apply now and let's forge a better, more intelligent world together!

This provides information on how we collect, use & store your personal information, including potential disclosure to our majority shareholder, Woolworths Group Limited.

title: Nattevagt til plejehjem i Odense.
description:
Nattevagt til plejehjem i Odense.

Vi søger social- og sundhedsassistenter eller social- og sundhedshjælpere til Natgruppens plejehjem. Brænder du for at arbejde nat? Så er det dig, vi søger.

I Natgruppen er vi inddelt i 3 områder, og vi søger lige nu personale til Natgruppen, område 1 og 2, som dækker plejehjem, hvor der en eller to på arbejde om natten.

Vi søger uddannede social- og sundhedsassistenter eller social- og sundhedshjælpere, der har lige så meget fokus på faglighed, ansvar og godt kollegaskab som os. Vi kan tilbyde dig en fast stilling på 28 timer om ugen fra kl. 23.00 - kl. 7.00 - med en 7/7 fordeling samt weekendvagt hver anden uge. Ønsker du at arbejde mindre timer eller blive timelønnet afløser er dette også en mulighed.



Vi har pt. Stillinger på Herluf Trolle og Sanderum.

Hos os får du spændende opgaver, dygtige kollegaer og stor mulighed for at bruge din faglighed. Lyder det som noget for dig? Så send os endelig din ansøgning!

Om vores arbejdsplads – Natgruppen
Vores personalegruppe består af dygtige social- og sundhedshjælpere, social- og
sundhedsassistenter, pædagoger og pædagogiske assistenter, som hver nat gør deres bedste for at skabe et trygt og professionelt miljø for borgerne enten i deres eget hjem, eller på de forskellige plejehjem i Odense Kommune. Arbejdsområderne er mange og opgaverne ofte komplekse, hvorfor hver nat giver nye spændende udfordringer og mulighed for at udvikle sig.

Komplekse borgerforløb og rehabilitering i fokus
Vi dækker hele Odense Kommune. I vores arbejde møder vi nemlig mange forskellige borgere i alle aldre med forskellige diagnoser og livsomstændigheder. Det giver en spændende og afvekslende hverdag med fuld fart på og mange nye opgaver og problemstillinger, der dagligt skal håndteres. Vi ved aldrig, hvordan natten har været, før vi lukker døren efter endt vagt.

Højt til loftet, høj faglighed og godt kollegaskab
Vi er en hyggelig, social og tæt personale- og ledergruppe med meget fokus på faglighed, ansvarlighed og tillid til hinanden. Særligt sidstnævnte betyder meget, da opgaverne på nattevagterne ofte er selvstændige og derfor kræver handlekraftige medarbejdere, der hviler i egen faglighed. Dog er der altid mulighed for at få god faglig sparring med dine kollegaer eller tovholderen på den respektive nattevagt, så hjælpen er altid kun et telefonopkald væk, hvis du ikke har nære kollegaer i huset.

Det gode sammenhold er ekstremt vigtigt for os i Natgruppen, og vi forsøger derfor, hvis
muligt, at mødes til diverse arrangementer og aktiviteter. Vi forsøger på samme måde at fylde hverdagen med humor, god stemning og omsorg for hinanden, hvilket vi håber, at du også vil prioritere, som en del af vores team.

Om dig
Vi leder efter dig, der har hjertet på det rette sted, og der:

  • Er færdiguddannet social- og sundhedsassistent eller social- og sundhedshjælper
  • Arbejder ud fra en rehabiliterende tankegang og har fokus på, hvilke faglige tiltag, der kan understøtte borgeren og dine kollegaers arbejde
  • Kan håndtere en kompleks og foranderlig hverdag, som aldrig er ens
  • Besidder et fagligt fundamentet og engagement samt går nysgerrigt og handlekraftigt til både udvikling og udfordring
  • Har kendskab til IT og er mundtligt velfunderet
  • Møder stabilt op på alle vagter med gå-på-mod og smil, klar til at møde vores dejlige borgergruppe og dine kompetente kollegaer
Vi tilbyder
Hvad får du som medarbejder hos Natgruppen:

  • En grundig introduktion til dine arbejdsopgaver og vores omsorgssystemer, som er individuelt planlagt ud fra erfaring og kompetencer, så du er klædt godt på fra start
  • Et alsidigt og udfordrende arbejde med almen, kompleks og specialiseret sygepleje
  • En dedikeret, samarbejdsfokuseret, løsningsorienteret og social medarbejder- og ledergruppe
  • Mulighed for at bruge og udvikle din sundhedsfaglige viden og erfaringer, samt en god faglig sparring med dine dygtige kollegaer
  • Medindflydelse og medansvar i forhold til din rolle, opgaver og varetagelsen af disse
Løn- og ansættelsesvilkår
Løn- og ansættelsesvilkår i henhold til gældende overenskomst mellem KL og den forhandlingsberettigede organisation. Tiltrædelse den 1. december 2026 eller efter aftale.

Vil du vide mere?
Du er velkommen til at kontakte assisterende rehabiliteringsleder Michelle Raahauge, Louise-Amalie Henriksen eller rehabiliteringsleder Camilla Hedegaard på 65 51 39 37.

Det praktiske
Ansøgningsfristen er den 26.10.26. Vi indkalder til samtale med kort varsel.

title: NGM - Water Resources Specialist
description:
Water Resources Specialist

Department: Water Resources

Supervisor: Erica Gallegos

Job Level: Specialist I

Work Hours: Full-Time Regular

Position Description:

Would you like to have a career with a collaborative, diverse, and dynamic mining company? We have an exciting opportunity for you!

Our people division is growing, and we are looking for a Water Resources Specialist with our Water Resources department. The successful candidate is responsible for assisting with the administration, protection, and management of Nevada Gold Mines’ (NGM) water rights, water use data, and regulatory obligations. Provide technical, administrative, and field-based support to ensure water rights remain in good standing, reporting obligations are met, and NGM’s water assets are accurately documented and protected.

At Nevada Gold Mines, our vision is to be the world’s most valued gold mining business by finding, developing, and operating the best assets with the best people. We are committed to a safe work environment, sending every person home safe and healthy every day and leaving a sustainable legacy on our host communities.

Responsibilities:

  • Compile, organize, and maintain data and supporting documentation for Nevada Division of Water Resources (NDWR) filings, including proofs, extensions of time, pumpage reports, reports of conveyance, and change applications.

  • Draft administrative forms for management review; track permit deadlines and obligations to help ensure water rights remain in good standing and regulatory requirements are met.

  • Collect, compile, validate, and maintain pumpage, totalizer, water-level, and related water-use data; prepare monthly summaries and support basin inventories and monitoring-plan reporting.

  • Maintain accurate databases and organized records for water rights, wells and well logs, pumpage, regulatory correspondence, permits, orders, agreements, invoices, and other supporting documentation.

  • Perform routine field work, including meter readings, water-level measurements, and site investigations at wells, springs, surface-water features, pipelines, and storage facilities. This includes collecting and documenting photographs, GPS coordinates, field observations, and other information needed to verify and support filings.

  • Identify data gaps, inconsistencies, malfunctioning equipment, access issues, or discrepancies between records and field conditions and elevate issues as appropriate.

  • Collaborate with Environmental, Operations, Legal, consultants, ranching teams, and other stakeholders

  • Support special projects related to water-right strategy and policy, database improvements, process improvements, consultant coordination, and development of standard operating procedures for data collection, filings, and tracking.

  • Independently review assigned data, filings, and reports for accuracy, completeness, and reasonableness prior to management review; prioritize and sequence work to meet regulatory deadlines.

Qualifications:

  • Technical education is preferred, or commensurate years of industry experience.

  • Experience with Microsoft Word, Excel, and PowerPoint is required.

  • Experience with GIS and various database platforms is preferred.

  • Experience in a mining or industrial environment is preferred.

  • Valid driver’s license with a clean driving record.

  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail, with the ability to manage priorities, meet regulatory deadlines, and maintain accurate records.

  • Ability to review data and documentation for accuracy and reasonableness, identify anomalies or missing information, and seek clarification or escalate issues when needed.

  • Ability to communicate effectively and work collaboratively with internal teams, consultants, and other stakeholders.

  • Ability to perform occasional field work at remote sites and walk on wet, slick, icy, uneven, or obstructed ground.

What We Can Offer You

title: Director of Product, Provider Software
description:
About Us

At Office Ally, we’ve been revolutionizing healthcare administration since our inception. What started as a clearinghouse focused on simplifying insurance claims processing for healthcare providers has grown into a full-suite healthcare technology company. We offer a range of affordable, cloud-based revenue cycle management solutions –from eligibility verification and claims management to revenue recovery and payment processing –that help healthcare organizations of all sizes streamline operations and reduce administrative burdens so they can focus on what matters most: patient care.

In April 2026, Office Ally acquired Jopari Solutions, Inc, a leader in straight-through electronic claims processing for Property & Casualty (P&C), Commercial, and Government healthcare. Jopari brings deep industry expertise and innovative enterprise payment solutions that are transforming how disbursements are handled across the insurance ecosystem. Together, we are expanding our capabilities across the full healthcare transaction lifecycle, connecting claims, payments, and data exchange to deliver a more seamless and efficient experience for providers, payers, and partners.

At the core of our company are four key values that guide our mission and work:

  • Ownership: We take pride in our responsibilities, driving results and taking accountability for the success of our projects.
  • Empowerment: We believe in giving our team the autonomy and support to make decisions that lead to innovative solutions.
  • Innovation: We continuously seek new and better ways to improve healthcare administration, embracing creativity and forward-thinking technology.
  • Transparent Communication: Open, honest communication is at the heart of our collaborations, internally and with our clients, ensuring alignment and trust.

About the Role

We're looking for a Director of Product to own our product portfolio and lead a team of Product Owners. In this people-leading role, you'll coach and develop your team while setting the direction for the products they manage. You'll allocate budgets, headcount, and capacity, and lead annual planning with full integration of vision, strategy, and roadmap frameworks, ensuring your team delivers products that meet customer needs and company goals.

What You'll Do

  • Translate business strategy into an executable product portfolio with a 1–3 year horizon
  • Own outcomes for the product line and manage budget, staffing, and vendor contracts
  • Run quarterly and annual planning cycles using Pragmatic Framework artifacts
  • Champion scalable processes such as Lean Portfolio Management and Product Ops
  • Build and maintain senior stakeholder relationships and customer advisory boards
  • Lead, coach, and develop a team of Senior Managers and Product Owners, including performance management and career development

What You'll Need

  • Bachelor's degree from a four-year college or university
  • 10+ years of product leadership experience with budget responsibility
  • Proven experience leading, mentoring, and developing teams of product managers or product owners
  • Strong strategic thinking and business acumen
  • Expertise in Pragmatic Framework
  • Ability to read, analyze, and interpret complex documents; write clear reports and business correspondence; and effectively present information to senior leadership and external stakeholders
  • Ability to define problems, collect data, establish facts, and draw valid conclusions, including working with concepts such as probability, statistical inference, ratios, and percentages
  • Proficiency with MS Office or Google Workspace, collaborative platforms (e.g., JIRA, Confluence), and product analytics tools, with the ability to learn new systems quickly

Nice to Have

  • Experience in healthcare technology
  • Experience with practice management systems (PMS), such as leading product strategy for, or working closely with, software used by provider practices to run their day-to-day operations
  • Pragmatic Institute certification
  • Masters of Business Administration

Travel Requirements

  • This role requires up to 25% travel, which may include client meetings, team gatherings, or company events.
  • Travel will typically be scheduled in advance and supported by the company.

Pay Transparency

Office Ally is committed to fair and equitable compensation practices in alignment with pay transparency laws. Compensation for this position may vary based on individual skills, experience, and location. In addition to base pay, employees may be eligible for performance-based bonuses and a comprehensive benefits package, including medical, dental, and vision coverage, 401(k) with company match, paid time off, and other benefits. Actual compensation will be determined considering the candidate’s qualifications, relevant experience, and internal equity.

Office Ally Pay Transparency
$150,000—$160,000 USD

Why You’ll Love Working at Office Ally

At Office Ally, your work has a direct impact on healthcare providers and their ability to deliver exceptional care. We’re driven by a mission to simplify healthcare administration, making it easier for providers to focus on what they do best—helping patients. As an Office Ally employee, you’ll be at the heart of our efforts to deliver exceptional service and software solutions to our clients in the healthcare space.

title: Acme Assistant Store Director-Ph
description:
