title: Psychiatric Technician, Psychiatry-Electroconvulsive Therapy, Part Time,  AM-AFSCME
description:
UC Health is hiring a Psych Tech (Therapeutic Program Worker) for the Psychiatry-Electroconvulsive Therapy for the first shift at UC Medical Center.

About University of Cincinnati Medical Center

As part of the Clifton Campus of UC Health, Greater Cincinnati’s academic health system, University of Cincinnati Medical Center has served Greater Cincinnati and Northern Kentucky for nearly 200 years. Each year, hundreds of thousands of patients receive care from our world-renowned clinicians and care team. Our experts utilize the most advanced medical knowledge and technology available, providing a level of specialty and subspecialty medical care that is not available anywhere else in Greater Cincinnati.

UC Medical Center is also home to medical breakthroughs- our physician experts conduct basic, translational and clinical research, leading to new therapies and care protocols, and connecting patients to the latest and most advanced treatments. UC Medical Center houses Greater Cincinnati’s only Level I adult trauma center, which includes the right mix of specialist and medical resources available at a moment’s notice for a wide variety of the most complex medical conditions and injuries.

Become part of the only Psychiatric Unit in Southwest Ohio where you can gain exposure to a variety of diagnosis in behavioral health. You will also have the opportunity to see things you won’t see anywhere else and the chance to treat patients that other institutions don’t accept.

The Psychiatric Therapeutic Program Worker (TPW), in collaboration with other members of the healthcare team, is responsible for maintaining a therapeutic milieu and a safe environment for all psychiatric patients on the unit. As a member of the patient care team, the TPW performs selected duties under the direction of the Registered Nurse, to ensure quality patient care.

  • Engages in population appropriate communication.
  • Has knowledge of growth and development milestones and tasks.
  • Gives clear instructions to patients/family regarding treatment.
  • Involves family/guardian in the assessment, initial treatment and continuing care of the patient.
  • Identifies any physical limitations of the patient and deploys intervention when necessary.
  • Recognizes and responds appropriately to patients/families with behavioral health problems.
  • Interprets population related data and plans care appropriately.
  • Identifies and responds appropriately to different needs resulting from, unique psychological needs or those associated with religious / cultural norms. Performs treatments, administers medication or operates equipment safely.
  • Recognizes and responds to signs/symptoms of abuse or neglect.
  • Establish a therapeutic milieu and provide a safe environment for all psychiatric patients. The Psychiatric Therapeutic Program Worker (TPW), in collaboration with other members of the healthcare team, is responsible for maintaining a therapeutic milieu and a safe environment for all psychiatric patients on the unit. As a member of the patient care team, the TPW performs selected duties under the direction of the Registered Nurse, to ensure quality patient care and staff. This includes monitoring the unit for safety at all times, maintaining a quiet and peaceful atmosphere, managing patient's behavior, preparing room for patient's arrival, orienting patients to the unit, checking belongings for hazardous objects or weapons, securing all belongings in designated areas, provide routine bed checks and secure areas.
  • Provide clinical duties as directed by Registered Nurse. These assignments may include but are not limited to: NIPPAS for vital signs and daily weights, phlebotomy, EKG, finger sticks, assistance with feedings, personal hygiene/grooming, ADL's, collecting meal trays and returning to dietary, clean dining area, provide clean linen and dispose of soiled linen, and assist with inventory control and distribution of supplies and equipment in the clinical areas and hallways.
  • Co-lead treatment groups, i.e., Goals Group, Exercise Group, etc. Participate, organize and direct social and therapeutic leisure time activities, i.e., Bingo, card playing, chess and activities in the Recreation Room. Observe individual behaviors and group interactions and report any major change in patient's behavior and/or medical condition to the RN.
  • Initiate basic psychiatric interventions and provide appropriate redirection as needed. Uses age appropriate communication skills. Provide non-punitive limit setting, appropriate modeling and reinforcement as needed to meet the patient's emotional needs. Assist in physical crisis management as needed and/or assigned.
  • Participate in quality improvement activities. Attend staff meetings, in-service sessions, and crisis intervention programs. Performs other duties as delegated or directed by RN, Clinical Manager or Nursing Supervisor.
  • Transport patients to X-ray, EEG, MRI, clinic appointments, etc.

  • Minimum Required: High School diploma/GED. Preferred: Relevant college coursework.
  • STNA certification preferred or college-level coursework in nursing/psychiatry/social work.
  • Minimum Required: Six months direct patient care experience in psychiatric setting or equivalent college-level coursework in nursing/psychology/social work.
  • Preferred: Specialized training in phlebotomy, vitals signs, and assistance with activities of daily living experience.
  • For employees working in UCMC Psychiatric Services, NCI-APS (Nonviolent Crisis Intervention with Advanced Physical Skills) Certification must be obtained within 90 days of hire.

Join our team as a psychiatric technician in our Psychiatric Emergency department. and work alongside the best and brightest clinical teams collaborating toward our common purpose: to advance healing and reduce suffering.

Join our team to BE UC Health. Be Extraordinary. Be Supported. Be Hope. Apply Today!

About UC Health

UC Health is an integrated academic health system serving Greater Cincinnati and Northern Kentucky. In partnership with the University of Cincinnati, UC Health combines clinical expertise and compassion with research and teaching—a combination that provides patients with options for even the most complex situations. Members of UC Health include: UC Medical Center, West Chester Hospital, University of Cincinnati Physicians and UC Health Ambulatory Services (with more than 900 board-certified clinicians and surgeons), Lindner Center of HOPE and several specialized institutes including: UC Gardner Neuroscience Institute and the University of Cincinnati Cancer Center. Many UC Health locations have received national recognition for outstanding quality and patient satisfaction. Learn more at uchealth.com.

At UC Health, we're proud to have the best and brightest teams and clinicians collaborating toward our common purpose: to advance healing and reduce suffering.

As the region's adult academic health system, we strive for innovation and provide world-class care for not only our community, but patients from all over the world. Join our team and you'll be able to develop your skills, grow your career, build relationships with your peers and patients, and help us be a source of hope for our friends and neighbors.

UC Health is an EEO employer.

title: Executive Vice President, Operating Model & Product
description:
Executive Vice President, Operating Model & Product

Global | Permanent

About Citco

Citco is a global leader in fund services, corporate governance and related asset services with staff across 50 office locations worldwide. With more than $1.8 trillion in assets under administration, we deliver end-to-end solutions and exceptional service to meet our clients’ needs.

For more information about Citco, please visit www.citco.com

About the Team & Business Line

Fund Administration is Citco’s core business, and our alternative asset and accounting service is one of the industry’s most respected. Our continuous investment in learning and technology solutions means our people are equipped to deliver a seamless client experience.

Strategic Operations is a dedicated function within Private Assets. It brings transformation delivery, project execution, business analysis, operational initiatives and implementation support into one team, reducing the delivery burden on BAU Operations and maintaining ownership from design through adoption.

The group will be split across three distinct focus areas, aligned under two individual leaders:

Operating Model, Product & Client Solutions: led by the Operating Model & Product leader, this area will define how services should run end to end, shape scalable products and solutions, support complex client implementations, and ensure client commitments are operationally deliverable.

Data, Reporting & Platform Enablement: led by the Technology, Data & Delivery leader, this area will define Operations requirements for data, reporting and platforms, strengthen data quality and lineage, and carry solutions through testing, deployment and adoption.

Digital Workflow, Automation & AI: also led by the Technology, Data & Delivery leader, this area will identify and deliver workflow, automation and AI opportunities, establish appropriate controls, and measure whether the expected benefits are realised.

The group works in close partnership with Operations, the Transformation Office, IT, Tactical Operations and Marquee Client teams. Roles may be permanent or approximately 12-month rotational assignments anchored in strategic locations. Rotational colleagues will join from the business, help shape and deliver change, and return to the line with broader project experience.

Your Role

You will own how our service should run and what we commit to clients, with accountability for the design and adoption of the Private Assets operating model.

  • Set the direction for the Private Assets operating model — defining how services should run end to end, and building the case for change with senior stakeholders.

  • Lead the Operating Model, Product & Client Solutions focus area, balancing long-term transformation priorities with near-term business and client demand.

  • Act as the senior Operations voice in client pitches, POCs and strategic direction setting, ensuring what we sell is something we can genuinely run.

  • Own the marquee solution reuse agenda — identifying where a solution built for one client can be applied across the wider book, and driving that rollout.

  • Partner at senior level with Operations, Tactical Operations, Marquee Client teams, the Transformation Office and IT to align change activity and remove duplication.

  • Govern the transformation portfolio, including prioritisation, resourcing, budget, risk, dependencies and executive reporting.

  • Establish plans for new client setup, transitions and complex implementations, coordinating across Operations, Financial Statements, Tax and Investor Relations.

  • Build and develop the team, including the rotational model, and actively participate in recruitment.

  • Maintain alignment with Tactical Operations and Marquee Operations, routing work to the right group and handing back anything better delivered tactically.

  • Represent Strategic Operations at Private Assets and CFS leadership forums.

About You

You have 12–15 years’ experience in fund administration, alternative asset management or a related financial services environment, predominantly in private assets.

  • A demonstrable record of delivering large-scale operating model or product re-engineering initiatives, with change that was genuinely adopted by the business.

  • Deep knowledge of private assets operating models, fund structures and the end-to-end service model.

  • Strong executive stakeholder management, with credibility in front of clients and senior leadership.

  • Commercial judgement — able to assess what we can genuinely deliver and price, and to hold that line in a client conversation.

  • Portfolio and programme governance experience, with proven ability to manage competing priorities across multiple focus areas.

  • Strong leadership skills and supervisory experience of other professionals, including rotational colleagues joining from the business.

  • Skilled in business planning, budgeting and stakeholder negotiation.

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.

  • Advanced computer skills (Microsoft Excel, Word, PowerPoint and SharePoint).

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Accounting, Finance, Economics or a related field; professional accounting designation a plus.

What We Expect of the Strategic Operations Team

Regardless of role or focus area, everyone in Strategic Operations is expected to demonstrate the following:

  • Deep technical and operational knowledge — genuine depth in how our processes, data and platforms actually work — the detail that only comes from having run the work.

  • Curiosity — the instinct to ask why a process looks the way it does, to challenge the answer, and to keep asking whether there is a better way.

  • A transformational mindset — comfortable redesigning end to end rather than patching, and prepared to see change through past go-live to the point where it is genuinely adopted.

  • Ownership through to adoption — accountability does not end at delivery; success is measured by whether the change sticks in the business.

  • Commercial and client awareness — an understanding of what we can genuinely run, so that what we commit to a client is deliverable.

  • Global mindset — working across regions, jurisdictions and time zones, and designing solutions that scale beyond a single desk, client or location.

  • Ambition to shape Citco’s future — an appetite to help build the operating model we will run for years, and to be measured on whether it works.

Our Benefits

Your well-being is of paramount importance to us, and central to our success. We provide a range of benefits, training and education support, and flexible working arrangements to help you achieve success in your career while balancing personal needs. Ask us about specific benefits in your location.

We embrace diversity, prioritizing the hiring of people from diverse backgrounds. Our inclusive culture is a source of pride and strength, fostering innovation and mutual respect.

Citco welcomes and encourages applications from people with disabilities. Accommodations are available upon request for candidates taking part in all aspects of the selection process.

title: Development Engineer Technician I
description:

title: Finance Specialist- Rotational Role
description:
As a Finance Rotational Specialist at Solstice, you will participate in a structured rotational program consisting of approximately three 18-month assignments, providing broad exposure to Finance, Analytics, Audit, Risk Management, and Business Operations. Through a series of rotational assignments, including an expected plant/site rotation, you will gain hands-on experience supporting business performance, operational excellence, compliance, and strategic initiatives across the organization.

This role offers hands-on experience partnering with cross-functional teams to analyze business performance, support audit and compliance initiatives, identify process improvement opportunities, and deliver actionable insights that drive business results. Participants will gain exposure to multiple areas of the Finance organization and contribute to high-impact projects that support Solstice's strategic objectives.

Key Responsibilities

Throughout the rotational program, you will:

  • Analyze complex data sets and provide actionable insights to improve business performance and operational effectiveness
  • Support financial reporting, planning, forecasting, and business analytics activities
  • Identify trends, risks, and opportunities to support strategic decision-making and business planning
  • Partner with cross-functional teams on key initiatives
  • Develop and maintain performance metrics, dashboards, and reporting tools that enable data-driven decisions
  • Present findings, recommendations, and project results to business leaders and stakeholders
  • Participate in process improvement initiatives designed to enhance efficiency, controls, and business outcomes

  • Complete rotational assignments across multiple functional areas to broaden business acumen and organizational knowledge

Manufacturing/Plant Rotation Expectations

As part of the rotational program, participants are expected to complete a rotation to a plant/site assignment to gain a firsthand understanding of manufacturing operations and operational finance. Rotation may change based on business needs.

During this rotation, participants will:

  • Partner with plant leadership and operations teams to understand key manufacturing processes and performance drivers
  • Support plant finance activities, including cost analysis, productivity initiatives, budgeting, forecasting, and inventory management
  • Analyze operational and financial data to identify opportunities for improved efficiency and cost savings
  • Gain exposure to supply chain, production planning, quality, and operational excellence initiatives
  • Build relationships across manufacturing and business functions to strengthen collaboration and business acumen
  • Develop an understanding of how operational decisions impact financial performance and organizational results

Must Have

  • Bachelor's degree
  • Openness to a rotation to a plant/site assignment
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and critical-thinking skills
  • Ability to analyze data and translate findings into meaningful business recommendations
  • Strong communication and presentation skills
  • Demonstrated learning agility and ability to adapt to new business environments

We Value

  • Bachelors’ degree in Finance, Accounting, Business, Economics, Statistics, Data Analytics, or a related field
  • Internship or prior experience in Finance, Audit, Accounting, Analytics, Risk Management, or Business Operations
  • Familiarity with data visualization and analytics tools
  • Knowledge of financial reporting, internal controls, or risk management concepts
  • Experience working in cross-functional team environments

BENEFITS OF WORKING FOR SOLSTICE ADVANCED MATERIALS

In addition to a competitive salary, leading-edge work, and developing solutions side-by-side with dedicated experts in their fields, Solstice Advanced Materials employees are eligible for a comprehensive benefits package. This package includes employer-subsidized Medical, Dental, Vision, and Life Insurance; Short-Term and Long-Term Disability; 401(k) match, Flexible Spending Accounts, Health Savings Accounts, EAP, and Educational Assistance; Parental Leave, Paid Time Off (for vacation, personal business, sick time, and parental leave), and 12 Paid Holidays.

The annual base salary range for this position is $66,551-$83,129. Please note that this salary information serves as a general guideline. Solstice considers various factors when extending an offer, including but not limited to the scope and responsibilities of the position, the candidate's work experience, education and training, key skills, as well as market and business considerations.

Solstice Advanced Materials is an equal opportunity employer. Qualified applicants will be considered without regard to age, race, creed, color, national origin, ancestry, marital status, affectional or sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, disability, nationality, sex, religion, or veteran status.

About Solstice Advanced Materials

Solstice Advanced Materials is a leading global specialty materials company that advances science for smarter outcomes. Solstice offers high-performance solutions that enable critical industries and applications, including refrigerants, semiconductor manufacturing, data center cooling, nuclear power, protective fibers, healthcare packaging and more. Solstice is recognized for developing next-generation materials through some of the industry's most renowned brands such as Solstice®, Genetron®, Aclar®, Spectra®, Fluka™ and Hydranal™. Partnering with over 3,000 customers across more than 120 countries and territories and supported by a robust portfolio of over 5,700 patents and pending applications, Solstice’s approximately 4,100 employees worldwide drive innovation in materials science. title: Director of Finance, Constellation Real Estate Group
description:
Director of Finance

Overview:

Constellation Real Estate Group, a division of Constellation Software (TSX:CSU), is seeking a Director of Finance to manage the production of management accounts, accounting compliance, financial reporting and financial analysis. The individual will manage across the entire Real Estate portfolio of companies, manage an offshore team, align the business with our standard best practices and systems. This role is perfect for someone who is looking for a fast paced, growth orientated environment that will allow for rewarding challenges and a trajectory for long-term growth. If you are a strong performer working with a company that has a complex matrixed structure, we would love to talk to you about this unique opportunity.

Constellation is a publicly-traded company that acquires, manages and grows business software companies all over the world.

Key Responsibilities

  • Manage the overall business P&L and full cycle accounting processes including customer invoicing and collections, bi-weekly forecasting, financial reporting and analysis and corporate accounting compliance.
  • Work alongside the Corporate accounting and finance integration team to build a team, processes and align the new business with our standard best practices and systems
  • Analyze monthly results to provide insights into forecast variances, key performance indicators/ratios and financial performance trends.
  • Analyze monthly results to provide insights into forecast variances, key performance indicators/ratios, AR risk, customer MRR and financial statement trends. Provide management team with clear and actionable insights and ensure updates are communicated in a timely manner.
  • Partner closely with the Senior Leadership Team and key functional group leaders within the business unit to support them in developing their strategic plans and be a trusted finance advisor.
  • Take ownership of the credit agreement management and debt covenant reporting as part of the acquisition process.
  • Take ownership of forecasting cycle and proactively update based on business changes discussed during weekly management calls.
  • Run a disciplined AR management process and ensure collection risk is minimized. Management team expectations will include weekly calls, timely escalation of troubled accounts and assessment of collection trends on monthly revenue.
  • Support the President and management team in preparing material for quarterly strategic reviews and actively participate in the review.
  • Participate in weekly management calls and provide the team strategic financial advice and insights on key financial trends.
  • Collaborate with business units in the same portfolio to learn and share best practices, opportunities for synergies and streamlining.
  • Lead and develop a team of offshore resources. Regularly meet to provide coaching, feedback, and goal setting.
  • With curiosity, proactively identify new areas of investigation or opportunities for improvement.
  • Ad hoc projects as desired or requested by senior management.

Technical and Educational Qualifications:

  • Minimum 5 years of F&PA experience
  • Minimum 2 years of people management and team leadership experience
  • Experience with managing or supervising offshore teams.
  • Experience with credit agreement management and debt covenant reporting
  • Ability to manage and prioritize competing deliverables in a fast-paced environment.
  • Strong written and communication skills.
  • Proficient knowledge of Microsoft Office suite including advanced use of Excel workbooks and PowerPoint.
  • Experience with Great Plains or other similar programs is a plus.
  • Financial knowledge in the software / IT field, specifically with financial operations and accounting guidelines.
  • A strong understanding of accounting guidelines, particularly IFRS-15 revenue recognition guidelines is strongly preferred, and acquisition accounting is a plus.
  • University Degree in Accounting, CPA strongly preferred, but not required.
  • Will require travel to the US ad offshore locations occasionally.

The City of Greeley is proud to partner with Weld County School District 6 to offer high school students and young professionals the opportunity to gain hands-on experience in local government. title: Software Engineer, Lab Platform
description:
About Arc Institute

Arc Institute is an independent nonprofit research organization at the interface of artificial intelligence and biology, working to accelerate scientific progress and understand the root causes of complex diseases. Founded in 2021 and based in Palo Alto, Arc partners with Stanford University, UC Berkeley, and UC San Francisco.

Unlike academia, our scientists have long-term funding and industry-like resources. Unlike industry, they're free to pursue high-risk, long-term research without commercial pressures. Arc's Technology Centers and Core Investigator labs work side by side, integrating experimental and computational biology under one roof to tackle problems neither could solve alone.

Our two Institute Initiatives reflect this model in action:

  • Virtual Cell Initiative: Building a full-stack virtual cell model to identify disease mechanisms and nominate drug targets, accelerating the path from biological insight to clinical trials.
  • Alzheimer's Disease Initiative: Mapping the genes, pathways, and environmental factors behind Alzheimer's disease to develop drug candidates that address root causes.

More than 300 Arconauts work together at our Palo Alto headquarters, backed by substantial long-term philanthropic funding.

About the position

You'll join Arc's Infrastructure Engineering team and own support and operations for our laboratory information management system (LIMS). Arc's scientists record their samples and experiments there, including the variables they change from one experiment to the next. That record is business intelligence for the lab: it's how scientists learn which conditions improve an assay, and it also feeds the pipelines that process lab data automatically. You'll run the request queue, make schema changes, train users and maintain the checks on data as it's entered, and you'll turn the requests that keep coming back into automation. You don't need LIMS experience: strong Python and SQL and an interest in lab data matter more, and we'll teach you the platform. You'll start under our lab platform Tech Lead, who will review your work and mentor you.

Why this position could be the best job you’ve ever had

  • Your work reaches the lab within a week, and it shows up in results: the experiment records you keep accurate are how labs find what makes their assays perform better.
  • You'll learn how a research institute turns lab work into data, with a Tech Lead whose goal is to hand you more of the system as you grow.

About you

  • You finish what you own, and you fix what's broken without being asked.
  • You're curious about the biology and the mission. You want to know what a guide or a 10x Flex run is.
  • You go to the scientists. You sit down with them, learn how they run and record their experiments, and understand what they need before you propose a fix.
  • You're careful and thoughtful. You want more scope and you'll take it on before you have every skill it needs, and you double-check changes other teams depend on.
  • You see which requests need a general solution, and you balance that work with the rest of the queue.

In this position you will

  • Run the request queue for Arc's lab data systems, from questions and fixes to schema changes, which you'll ship through our change workflow so other teams' pipelines don't break.
  • Support the templates scientists record experiments with, and the command-line tools that pull their data for analysis.
  • Run training sessions for scientists, and write the docs they come back to.
  • Build and maintain the checks that catch errors in data as scientists enter it, so bad records don't reach analysis or pipelines.
  • Help carry out the refactor of the team and permission structure in our LIMS, which decides who can see and edit what.
  • Turn the requests that keep coming back into automation, and choose the approach that fits the problem: a script, a scheduled job, a template change or an AI agent. Write the runbook, add the checks and retire the manual step; changes go through the team's code review.
  • By the end of your first year you will
  • Build tools that make screen and experiment metadata queryable across systems for computational biologists and lab teams.
  • Run the request queue and ship schema changes on your own, with the Tech Lead reviewing designs instead of each change.
  • Own a part of the lab platform from design through support.

Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree with 0-2 years of relevant experience, or an advanced degree.
  • You write solid Python and SQL, and you're comfortable working with REST APIs.
  • You debug problems in systems you didn't build, working from the code, logs and data.
  • You use AI coding tools day to day or are ready to learn, you check what they produce, and you're careful with sensitive research data.
  • You explain technical things clearly to scientists, and you write docs and training that people use.
  • You ask for help early and take feedback well.
  • You've owned a piece of work from start to finish, in school, an internship or a job, and you stayed responsible for it after it shipped.
  • Work onsite in our Palo Alto office at least 3 days a week.

Preferred Qualifications

  • You've used a LIMS or ELN, such as Benchling, or you've worked with lab data like samples and sequencing metadata.
  • You've automated a repeated manual task with scripts, bots or agents.
  • You've worked on CI pipelines, tests or repo templates.
  • You've supported the users of a tool, on a help desk, as a TA or on an on-call rotation.

The base salary range for this position is $118,000 to $146,000. These amounts reflect the range of base salary that the Institute reasonably would expect to pay a new hire or internal candidate for this position. The actual base compensation paid to any individual for this position may vary depending on factors such as experience, market conditions, education/training, skill level, and whether the compensation is internally equitable, and does not include bonuses, commissions, differential pay, other forms of compensation, or benefits. This position is also eligible to receive an annual discretionary bonus, with the amount dependent on individual and institute performance factors.

In addition to the Base Salary and Annual Bonus above, you will be eligible to participate in the Institute’s Compound Cash Grant Program (the “CCGP”). title: Mechanical Reliability Engineer
description:
Mechanical Reliability Engineer

Valliant Mill

Salary Range ($89,000-$118,600)-Multiple factors, including Individual experience, skills, and abilities, will determine where an employee is ultimately placed in the pay range. Variable pay may provide additional opportunities for financial awards. This job is eligible to participate in IP’s short–term incentive plan.

The Mechanical Reliability Engineer reports to the Mechanical Reliability Engineering Manager at the Valliant Mill. The Valliant mill is a 5,000+ ton per day containerboard mill with 3 paper machines, 3 continuous digesters, 3 secondary fiber plants and a utilities/chemical recovery complex. It currently operates with over 400+ mill employees, 170+ contract maintenance employees, and 150+ other contractors in a results-oriented environment.

Responsibilities (include but are not limited to):

  • Process Management

title: Scaffold Builder II
description:
Position Summary

A Journeyman Scaffold Builder I will assist and support the safe, quality, and efficient completion of various tasks related to scaffold maintenance work being performed at a petrochemical processing plant, including but not limited to:

Craft specific scaffold labor

Preparation, transportation, erection, modification, disassembly, and storing of various scaffolding types (systems) in and around industrial equipment such as piping, boilers, towers, vessels, tanks, exchangers, reactors, pumps, etc.

Providing support services such but not limited to firewatch, holewatch, bottlewatch, light equipment/vehicle operation, material kitting/delivery, general housekeeping, etc. as needed.

Qualification Highlights

Must be able to meet all physical requirements – see below.

Must have reliable transportation

Must be willing and able to work:

Up to 7 days per week

Overtime, call-out, etc. as required

Must be capable of working under the direction of a skilled Leadman and under the supervision of an experienced Foreman.

Must possess proven qualifications, experience, and tested knowledge on the safe design, erection, and disassembly (in adherence with applicable OSHA standards) of various scaffolding systems (types) and materials.

Must be well versed on safe work practices while performing scaffolding services in and around operating units located within a petrochemical facility.

Must be capable of leading and mentoring other crew members such as helpers, apprentices, and Journeymen II.

Must possess skills and ability to preplan, coordinate, and order material for specific jobs/activities/tasks.

Must have an aptitude for scaffold equipment/materials/techniques and have effective computing, literacy, and numeracy skills.

Must possess all required tools to perform scaffold related activities.

Will be expected to assist other crafts when not actively performing scaffolding activities.

Must be experienced with and/or capable of successfully completing all required training/qualifications necessary to oversee safety-sensitive work which includes but is not limited to the preparation, set-up, and execution of hot work, confined space entry, and fresh air work.

Must be experienced with and/or capable of successfully completing all required training/qualifications necessary to utilize all related tools, apparatuses, equipment, etc. to execute safety-sensitive work which includes but is not limited to the preparation, set-up, and execution of hot work and confined space entry work.

Must be capable of reading, understanding, and adhering to restrictions and/or requirements of various types of work permits and/or JSAs.

Must successfully complete Short Service Employee (SSE) program, if applicable.

Must successfully complete a 90-day probationary period. Any disciplinary and/or attendance issues during this time will be grounds for termination.

Must maintain satisfactory bi-annual evaluation scores of no less than 3.0. Unsatisfactory bi-annual evaluation scores of less than 3.0 for two consecutive cycles will result in disciplinary action, up to termination, for poor performance.

Position Responsibilities

Must have a strong approach, understanding, and commitment to safety, quality, and efficiency in an industrial environment.

Must be capable of and will be expected to perform pre-task hazard assessments to identify potential risks and implement pro-active elimination and/or mitigation techniques.

Must be capable of reading and comprehending industrial/engineered drawings such as but not limited to blueprints, sketches, plans, P&ID, etc. to determine scope of work, locations, required tools/equipment, and bill of materials to execute activities.

Must actively participate and support site programs such as (at a minimum):

Safe Catch/Quality Catch/Stop Work Authority

Continuous Improvement (SMART Focus)

Applicable customer initiatives/programs

General craft specific scaffold knowledge

Preparation, transportation, erection, modification, disassembly, storing of various scaffolding types (systems) in and around industrial equipment such as piping, boilers, towers, vessels, tanks, exchangers, reactors, pumps, etc.

Providing support services such as but not limited to firewatch, holewatch, bottlewatch, light equipment/vehicle operation, material kitting/delivery, general housekeeping, etc. as needed.

Preferred Qualifications

Current or Former Zachry Employee with acceptable ESR rating only.

Reports to Position

This position does not have any direct reports; however, candidates will be expected to work closely with and mentor helper, apprentice, and/or Journeyman II positions.

Required Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

National Center for Construction Education and Research (NCCER) Performance Verified (PV) certification for Scaffold Builder.

Must have a minimum score of 85% on the Zachry Craft Assessment test pre-employment.

Must have a minimum of 4 years applicable experience in the Scaffold Builder trade in an industrial and/or construction project.

Acceptable Motor Vehicle Report (MVR) and valid Driver’s License.

Must be capable of successfully completing all required training/qualifications necessary to operate Ariel Work Platforms (AWP) such as but not limited to manlifts, scissor lifts, etc. as well as material handling equipment such as forklifts.

Must be capable of successfully completing all required training/qualifications of Person Leading Work (PLW).

Must have experience using industrial hand and power tools in an industrial work environment.

Must possess good problem-solving abilities and an agile mindset.

Must possess general aptitude for mechanical equipment, have effective computing, literacy, and numeracy skills, and manual dexterity.

Must possess the ability to work effectively with others in a team environment.

Must possess effective communication skills (written and/or verbal) with co-workers, supervisors, and customer.

Must possess a strong commitment/understanding of Zachry and customer core values, safety rules, and regulations.

Must possess and maintain a valid TWIC card for the duration of employment.

Must successfully complete and maintain applicable Safety Council and/or Site-Specific credentials for the duration of employment.

Physical Requirements

Employee will be required to adhere to large amounts of standing, walking, cycling, bending, squatting, lifting, and physically demanding work.

Must have good dexterity with hands and fingers to perform the precision adjustments of machinery parts and controls.

Will use arms and hands to signal, grab, hold, turn, push, and pull objects, materials, controls, and tools.

Must be capable of lifting, carrying, and moving up to 50lbs.

Must be capable and comfortable working at extreme heights on fixed, temporary, and/or mobile platforms.

Must be capable and comfortable working within confined spaces to include but not limited to tanks, vessels, pits, excavations, etc.

Will use vision abilities to focus, see short and long distances, colors, depth perception and peripheral vision.

Must be capable of working outside in the elements including but not limited to the heat, cold, rain, snow, and wind; and must be able to work for long period of times up to 12 hours a day.

Will be required to wear personal protective equipment (PPE) including but not limited to: hard hat, safety glasses/goggles, ear plugs/muffs, masks/respirators, safety vests, gloves, chemical suits, and steel-toe boots.

description:
Zscaler (NASDAQ: ZS) accelerates digital transformation so customers can be more agile, efficient, resilient, and secure. The Zscaler Zero Trust Exchange platform protects thousands of customers from cyberattacks and data loss by securely connecting users, devices, and applications in any location. We are looking for an AI Solutions Engineer, People & Culture to join our team. This is a hybrid role (in office Tuesday-Thursday) in our Santa Clara, CA HQ or Bellevue, WA office, reporting to the AI Transformation Director in the Global People & Culture Organization. Human Resources is being transformed around Human + AI optimization, and you will be the driving force behind this transformation. Part builder, part co-builder, and part teacher, you will spearhead our transition to an AI-native HR function by encoding the judgment of our best practitioners into safe, governed agents that seamlessly integrate with human ingenuity to unlock unprecedented outcomes.

  • Pair deeply with subject matter experts—from compensation analysts to recruiters—to build domain-specific agents, transferring your technical craft so they can independently maintain and evolve their own tools
  • Redesign workflows from the inside out to ensure we solve fundamental process issues rather than simply automating a broken system

  • Partner closely with the AI Center of Excellence and Forward Deployed Engineering team to solve the hardest technical integration challenges on shared rails, as well as co-create mature governance standards

Who You Are (Success Profile)

  • You are a “Figure-it-out” person who navigates ambiguity with ease and addresses fundamental process issues rather than bolting AI onto the current state
  • You are technically fluent and a proven builder with a portfolio of shipped, adopted GenAI agents, hands-on with skills, MCPs, data, automations, prompt design, and evals

What We’re Looking for (Minimum Qualifications)

  • Demonstrated hands-on experience building AI agents, automations, or tools that changed how real work gets done

description:

Are you ready to take the next step in your career? Join us for an exciting opportunity at Albertsons Companies, where innovation and customer service go hand-in-hand!

At Albertsons Companies, we are looking for someone who’s not just seeking a job, but someone who wants to make an impact. In this role, you’ll have the opportunity to lead, innovate, and contribute to the growth of a company that values great service and lasting customer relationships. This position offers the chance to work in a fast-paced, dynamic environment that’s constantly evolving.

The Assistant Store Director (ASD) is actively involved in and provides friendly, courteous, and helpful customer service daily. The ASD is also responsible for assisting the Store Director (SD) with the total operations of the store and performs various duties personally or through supervision of store employees (100+ bargaining unit and non-contract employees).

Pay Transparency: The salary range is $68k to $94k annually with quarterly bonus potential. Starting salary will vary based on criteria such as location, experience, and qualifications. There may be flexibility for exceptional candidates. The total comp package yearly can include 12 days PTO, 40 hrs of sick time, 6 recognized holidays, 401k match of up to 7%, Pet insurance, EPA benefits, and so much more!

The ASD manages the entire store with the authority to operate the store at maximum efficiency during the absence of the SD. The ASD is responsible for the supervision of all store employees. This includes orienting new employees, training and developing, scheduling and payroll, performance evaluation, and personnel actions (e.g., hiring, promoting, disciplining, etc.). Our ASD’s also performs or delegates security and cash control procedures, the handling of customer complaints, the reporting of accidents/injuries, the maintenance of sanitation standards, office and accounting functions, the maintenance of in-stock conditions, and ensuring communication between departments and among store personnel.

Key Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

  • Overall management responsibility for operation of retail grocery store during absence of the Store Director, including store performance, control of cash, inventory and security, customer services, and management of staff.
  • Track, analyze and take action to improve store performance by forecasting weekly/daily sales goals and meeting or exceeding established goals.

  • Select, train, develop, and manage job performance of store employees, with assistance of other management personnel.
  • Provide constructive suggestions and encouragement, set performance expectations, provide honest feedback, and identify assignments to provide others with developmental opportunities.
  • Maintain appropriate professional relationships with union officials and ensure compliance with collective bargaining agreement provisions if applicable.
  • Preserve positive working relationships with direct reports, peers, supervisors, suppliers, and customers effectively handling complex or difficult situations involving others.
  • Motivate others to perform the job and work towards common objectives. Serve as a role model to others instilling a positive attitude in his/her employees.

title: Controller
description:

title: On Call Field Archaeologist

title: Senior Vice President, Data, Reporting & Platform Enablement
description:
Senior Vice President, Data, Reporting & Platform Enablement

Global | Permanent

About Citco

Citco is a global leader in fund services, corporate governance and related asset services with staff across 50 office locations worldwide. With more than $1.8 trillion in assets under administration, we deliver end-to-end solutions and exceptional service to meet our clients’ needs.

For more information about Citco, please visit www.citco.com

About the Team & Business Line

Fund Administration is Citco’s core business, and our alternative asset and accounting service is one of the industry’s most respected. Our continuous investment in learning and technology solutions means our people are equipped to deliver a seamless client experience.

Strategic Operations is a dedicated function within Private Assets. It brings transformation delivery, project execution, business analysis, operational initiatives and implementation support into one team, reducing the delivery burden on BAU Operations and maintaining ownership from design through adoption.

The group will be split across three distinct focus areas, aligned under two individual leaders:

Operating Model, Product & Client Solutions: led by the Operating Model & Product leader, this area will define how services should run end to end, shape scalable products and solutions, support complex client implementations, and ensure client commitments are operationally deliverable.

Data, Reporting & Platform Enablement: led by the Technology, Data & Delivery leader, this area will define Operations requirements for data, reporting and platforms, strengthen data quality and lineage, and carry solutions through testing, deployment and adoption.

Digital Workflow, Automation & AI: also led by the Technology, Data & Delivery leader, this area will identify and deliver workflow, automation and AI opportunities, establish appropriate controls, and measure whether the expected benefits are realised.

The group works in close partnership with Operations, the Transformation Office, IT, Tactical Operations and Marquee Client teams. Roles may be permanent or approximately 12-month rotational assignments anchored in strategic locations. Rotational colleagues will join from the business, help shape and deliver change, and return to the line with broader project experience.

Your Role

You will lead the Operations data, reporting and platform agenda for Private Assets — setting requirements with IT and the Transformation Office, and delivering alongside them.

  • Own the Operations view of the data and reporting roadmap, including data quality, lineage, ownership and reporting capability.

  • Set out Operations’ requirements with IT and the Transformation Office, then deliver alongside them rather than handing over.

  • Lead platform enablement work — ensuring platform change is specified, tested and adopted with Operations in the room throughout.

  • Establish reporting standards and reusable data products rather than one-off extracts.

  • Provide the data and evidence base that other focus areas rely on to quantify a problem and measure a benefit.

title: Mental Health Group Facilitator - PA
description:
Why Charlie Health?

Millions of people across the country are navigating mental health conditions, substance use disorders, and eating disorders, but too often, they’re met with barriers to care. From limited local options and long wait times to treatment that lacks personalization, behavioral healthcare can leave people feeling unseen and unsupported.

Charlie Health exists to change that. Our mission is to connect the world to life-saving behavioral health treatment. We deliver personalized, virtual care rooted in connection—between clients and clinicians, care teams, loved ones, and the communities that support them. By focusing on people with complex needs, we’re expanding access to meaningful care and driving better outcomes from the comfort of home.

As a rapidly growing organization, we're reaching more communities every day and building a team that’s redefining what behavioral health treatment can look like. If you're ready to use your skills to drive lasting change and help more people access the care they deserve, we’d love to meet you.

About the Role

Charlie Health is hiring exceptional candidates with a Masters degree in mental health and previous work experience facilitating groups to provide remote, telehealth services to our adolescent and young adult clients. We’re eager to work with forward-thinking mental health professionals to enhance our programming and provide the best possible care to our clients.

People know Charlie Health for our warm and empathetic clinical team. While each individual clinician has their own interests, expertise, and style, we require all team members to be well versed in a variety of modalities. Our clients are struggling to cope with underlying mental health issues and benefit from therapists that are sophisticated and relational. Successful candidates are committed to bettering the mental health of their clients, along with being adept at self-care, ensuring they are prepared to give their best every day to address the youth mental health crisis.

Responsibilities

  • Complete all Onboarding requirements within 2 weeks of start date
  • Meet with your assigned Charlie Health Group Quality Supervisor or Group Quality Director at a minimum of 1x/month for required check-in
  • Respond to all email and Slack communication promptly (within 48 hours of receiving a communication)
  • Review the curriculum aligned to group assignment prior to group start time
  • Arrive ~10 minutes early to scheduled group time and facilitate all groups for the entirety of the hour
  • Facilitate groups following Charlie Health best practices and using assigned and most up to date Charlie Health curriculum
  • Facilitate groups across age groups and cohorts, including Integrative curriculum, Support Staffing and Wellness Hour as needed
  • Foster client engagement and group cohesion throughout the session, encouraging client participation and fostering camera-on culture
  • Following all operational policies and procedures as indicated by Charlie Health best practices
  • Participate in collaborative Treatment Team (Tuesdays) and Group Supervision (every other Friday) with your assigned Charlie Health Group Quality Supervisor or Group Quality Director, peers and other Clinical Leadership team members
  • Work collaboratively and respectfully across the care team including with Primary Therapists, Care Experience Specialists and Care Coaches
  • Communicate clearly, professionally, and promptly with all clients, staff, families, agencies, and referents
  • Monitor your treatment documentation to ensure all of your notes are completed within required 24 hour timeframe and meet agency and professional standards per DHCS and The Joint Commission standards
  • Maintain and model professional ethics, including appropriate boundaries and confidentiality
  • Other duties as assigned

Requirements

  • Must be available during late afternoons and evenings on weekdays (3-8pm MT on Monday to Thursday) and on Saturdays to meet the schedules of our adolescent and young adult clients
  • Master’s degree in mental health or related field required (see below for full list)
  • Experience working with youth and young adults
  • Well versed in a variety of modalities and feel confident integrating them into your treatment approach (DBT, CBT, EMDR, MI certification is a plus)
  • Passionate about the benefits of group treatment and skilled in conducting group treatment
  • Ability to work effectively in a team
  • Creative and engaging, especially over video!
  • The technical ability to run effective telehealth sessions
  • Reliable WIFI connection when meeting with clients
  • Familiarity with and willingness to use cloud-based communication software—Gmail, Slack, Zoom, Dropbox–in addition to EMR and outcomes survey software on a daily basis
  • Part time 1099 role

Benefits

  • Charlie Health is pleased to offer comprehensive benefits to all full-time, exempt employees. Read more about our benefits here.

Eligible Master's Degrees:

  • Master of Science (M.S.) in Mental Health Counseling
  • Master of Arts (M.A.) in Counseling Psychology
  • Master of Social Work (M.S.W.) with a concentration in Mental Health
  • Master of Science (M.S.) in Clinical Mental Health Counseling

title: Director of Fraud and Underwriting
description:
About Us

SimplePractice is headquartered in Los Angeles, California, but we have team members who work and live across the United States, Dominican Republic, Mexico City, and Ukraine.

At SimplePractice, we are improving access to quality care by equipping health and wellness clinicians with all the tools they need to thrive in private practice.

More than 250,000 providers trust SimplePractice to build their business through our industry-leading software with powerful tools that simplify every part of practice management. From admin work to clinical care, our suite of innovative solutions work together to reduce administrative burden—empowering solo and small group practitioners to thrive alongside their clients.

Award-winning and people-first, SimplePractice is shaping the future of health tech. In 2026, we were recognized by BuiltIn as a Best Remote Company to Work For, Software Guru's Best Places to Code, Becker Healthcare Telehealth Companies to Know, and we won a MedTech Breakthrough Award for Best Practice Management Solution Provider.

Role

You will manage the end-to-end operating model for fraud, payments underwriting, and platform abuse across the full customer lifecycle: pre-onboarding and KYB/KYC, payments underwriting and approval decisioning, transaction and payout monitoring, bank-change and account-takeover controls, disputes and chargeback strategy, reserves and holds, spam and platform abuse containment, and account decisions across approval, holds, re-enablement, termination, and deletion. You'll report to the Chief Legal Officer and work in close partnership with our CISO and Product/Engineering leadership. This is a strategy and program-ownership role: you'll set direction and represent our fraud posture to the executive team, while a team of analysts and leads runs the day-to-day operations you design.

What You'll Own

Strategy and risk appetite

  • Own SimplePractice's fraud and payments risk appetite — loss tolerance in basis points of payment volume, acceptable false-positive and review rates, review and verification requirements, approval-rate targets by segment. You propose it, you drive executive alignment on the tradeoffs those numbers encode, and you are the decision-maker on policy changes within it.

  • Build the roadmap for the function across policy, data, tooling, modeling, automation, and org design. Sequence it so early wins fund later investment.
  • Move policy from documented practice to governed artifact: versioned rules and thresholds, backtested before deployment, shadow-run or champion/challenger tested where exposure warrants it, with an auditable decision trail showing which policy version and which signals drove any given outcome.
  • Set the standard for how emerging attack patterns get from first detection to deployed control, and shrink that cycle time deliberately.

Underwriting and onboarding risk

  • Own payments underwriting and KYB/KYC decisioning end to end — policy, thresholds, data sources, verification requirements, escalation paths, and the conversion-versus-risk tradeoff at each gate.
  • Build risk-tiered onboarding: automated approval for the clean majority, proportionate friction for the ambiguous middle, real scrutiny reserved for genuine signal.
  • Own reserves, holds, and payout-timing policy as credit and exposure decisions, not just fraud decisions. Size them at portfolio level with a defensible methodology.
  • Maintain card network and ACH program compliance — Visa VAMP, Mastercard ECP, Nacha return-rate thresholds — and keep us well inside them, including the Nacha fraud-monitoring obligations that reached all originators in 2026.

Fraud operations and detection

  • Run fraud operations to explicit SLAs on throughput, accuracy, and time-to-contain, with capacity modeling and workforce planning rather than reactive hiring.
  • Drive automation and AI-assisted triage into the review pipeline to reduce manual touch volume, and hold yourself to a measurable cost-per-decision trend, not just a loss number.
  • Own the risk policy and configuration layer of the detection stack — rules, scoring thresholds, identity and device signals, case management, queue design — under a shared administration model with Product and Engineering, who own the underlying platform. Define the boundary clearly and make it work.
  • Own vendor strategy for the risk stack. Evaluate, select, and manage vendors against measured ROI, and be willing to consolidate or cut.
  • Partner with data science to build, validate, monitor, and retrain fraud models. You don't need to build them, but you need to know when one has drifted and be able to say why.

Platform abuse and account integrity

  • Co-own spam, scaled signup abuse, and platform-abuse controls, in partnership with Security, Product, Engineering, and Marketing.
  • Co-own account-compromise and account-takeover response with Security, with clear boundaries on who leads what.
  • Build controls for the current threat set: synthetic and stolen identity at onboarding, injection and deepfake attacks against identity verification, agentic and automated account takeover, first-party misuse where identity verifies cleanly and intent is the only signal, and payout redirection through bank-detail changes.

Influencing product and engineering

  • Establish a pre-launch risk review for anything that touches money movement, identity, account access, or payout — with fraud threat modeling done at design time, not launch week. Make it fast enough that teams want to use it rather than route around it.
  • Monitor shipped and in-flight product for builds that open new fraud surface, and raise them with enough specificity and evidence that they get fixed.
  • Translate risk needs into product and engineering requirements a team can actually build against: data and signal gaps, instrumentation, decisioning hooks, internal tooling for investigators, reason-code plumbing, latency budgets. Bring requirements, not complaints.
  • Earn standing roadmap influence. Build the case with loss data, exposure modeling, and customer-friction evidence, and get fixes prioritized against competing work — without formal authority over those teams.
  • Partner with Compliance, Legal, Security, Support, and Finance on the pieces they own, and be explicit about the seams.

Enabling the rest of the company

  • Own the escalation paths, SOPs, and training that let Support, Success, and Sales handle fraud-adjacent situations correctly without routing everything to your team.
  • Maintain the knowledge base and QA standards that keep decisions consistent as the team grows.

Incident command and reporting

  • Serve as domain lead for financial-fraud incidents: lead the response, make containment and account-action calls, coordinate cross-functionally, document incidents, and run honest postmortems that produce hardening work items.
  • Own the fraud metrics package to executives: loss rate in basis points of payment volume, chargeback and dispute performance, approval and decline rates, false-positive and review rates, time-to-detect and time-to-contain, recovery, and operational SLA adherence. Frame tradeoffs, not just results.
  • Represent fraud risk in executive forums, and with payment partners, sponsor banks, and networks alongside the accountable executive.

Team

  • Lead, coach, and grow the Fraud, Risk & Underwriting team, including senior individual contributors.
  • Design the org for where we're going: differentiate strategy and analytics work from operational disposition, and build the analytical capability the function currently lacks.
  • Set a high hiring bar and develop people into the next tier of leadership.

Required Skills and Experience

  • 10+ years in fraud, payments risk, underwriting, or financial crime, including 5+ years leading teams — with real experience managing managers.
  • Direct experience at a payment facilitator, PSP, acquirer, marketplace, fintech, or embedded-payments platform. You understand merchant-of-record liability, sub-merchant underwriting, reserves, and card network and ACH compliance programs from the inside.
  • A track record of building a function, not just running one: you have taken a fraud or risk team from operational and reactive to systematic and scaled, and can describe what you built, in what order, and what it moved.
  • Fluency across multiple risk surfaces — card-not-present payments, ACH and money movement, identity and onboarding, account takeover, disputes — and the judgment to tailor controls to each rather than applying one playbook.
  • Demonstrated ability to influence product and engineering roadmaps without owning them. You can point to fraud controls that shipped because you made the case.
  • You have defended a decision that traded approval rate against loss rate, and can walk through the total-cost math — including revenue lost to false declines — rather than optimizing for the lowest gross loss number.
  • You have presented fraud loss and risk tradeoffs directly to a C-level or board audience, and can turn a technical fraud trend into a specific ask.

Strongly preferred

  • Technical acumen sufficient to be a credible partner to engineering and data science: you understand how a decisioning system is put together — signals, features, rules, models, latency constraints, logging — and can write requirements at that level.
  • Hands-on data fluency. You query the data yourself in SQL rather than waiting on a dashboard, and you validate your own hypotheses.
  • Practical experience with the modern risk stack — decisioning and orchestration platforms, rules engines, case management, identity verification and KYB providers, device and behavioral intelligence — including vendor selection and integration.
  • Working literacy in model risk practice: validation, monitoring, drift, champion/challenger testing, and why the audit trail matters.
  • Experience operating risk controls under HIPAA, PHI-adjacent, or comparable regulatory constraints.
  • CFE, CAMS, or CFCS.

Benefits

We offer a competitive benefits program including:

  • Medical, dental, vision, life & disability insurance
  • 401(k) plan with company match
  • Flexible Time Off (FTO), wellbeing days, paid holidays, and summer Fridays
  • Mental health resources

title: Design Director - RS4
description:
Office location: Cambridgeshire, UK – This position offers flexible working options, including predominantly remote work. However, applicants should be based (or be willing to relocate) within a comfortable commuting distance of our office to attend onsite as required.

Are you an experienced MMO design leader who knows what it takes to build a world players will want to call home for thousands of hours?

As Design Director on our newly announced MMORPG, RS4 you'll work closely with our Creative Director to turn our vision into a coherent, scalable, and sustainable MMO design for an ambitious new project in the RuneScape universe. Bringing deep, hands-on experience of building and shipping MMOs, you'll own the game's overall design architecture across progression, economy, content, social systems, endgame, and live operations, making sure every system works together as a compelling long-term player experience.

This is an exciting senior leadership opportunity to lead and grow our Design team, partnering closely with the Creative Director, Design Leads, Production, and Engineering to create a game that can be built and operated at scale, and that honours what makes RuneScape so special to millions of players.

What you'll be doing:

  • Translate the Creative Director's vision and pillars into a coherent, scalable MMO experience.
  • Own the MMO design architecture, defining how progression, combat, economy, content, social systems, endgame, and retention work together.
  • Set the design strategy and standards, establishing design principles, frameworks, and quality bars across the project.
  • Lead the Design team, guiding and mentoring Design Leads and senior designers while establishing clear ownership and decision-making.
  • Design for longevity, ensuring systems and content can sustain years of player progression, engagement, and live development.
  • Partner closely with Creative, Production, Engineering, UX, Analytics, and other teams to make sure designs are achievable at scale.
  • Use playtesting, telemetry, and player feedback to identify problems, iterate, and evolve the experience.
  • Anticipate and proactively address MMO-specific risks, including economy health, progression balance, content consumption, exploits, and technical constraints.

What we're looking for:

  • A proven track-record of successful game design experience, with substantial experience on MMOs or persistent online worlds.
  • Senior design leadership experience (Design Director, Lead Designer, Principal Designer, Game Director, or equivalent) on at least one shipped MMO or major persistent online title, ideally from pre-production through to launch.
  • A proven ability to translate a Creative Director's vision, pillars, and player promise into a coherent MMO design framework, with strong creative partnership skills.
  • Deep MMO systems expertise across character progression, itemisation, economies, combat and encounters, social systems, and endgame, and an understanding of how they interact as one ecosystem.
  • Experience building or owning an MMO's content model, balancing content velocity against consumption and creating frameworks that let multiple teams build content consistently.
  • Significant experience on a live MMO or persistent online game, using telemetry and community feedback to understand retention, economy health, and player behaviour.
  • A strong understanding of the technical realities of MMO development, and experience working in Unreal Engine or similarly complex AAA environments.
  • Proven experience leading and mentoring a sizeable multidisciplinary design organisation, with the confidence to make difficult calls and protect the core game from uncontrolled complexity.
  • A passion for MMOs, a strong appreciation of what makes RuneScape distinctive, and the ability to modernise its principles without simply importing conventions from other games.

What we offer:

When you join Jagex you can look forward to a generous Perks & Benefits package including:

  • Private Healthcare, including Dental Plan.
  • Minimum 6% Pension contributions.
  • Employee Assistance Programme & onsite Counselling.
  • Life Insurance.
  • Discretionary annual performance bonus.
  • Enhanced family leave policies from day 1.
  • Flexible working hours.
  • 25 days annual leave + Bank holidays & the option to buy/sell holidays + so much more!


Inclusion & Accessibility Statement

We are committed to providing equal opportunities and creating an environment where everyone can thrive. We welcome applications from all backgrounds, and we recruit, develop, and promote based on merit and ability.

If you require any reasonable adjustments to support you during the recruitment process, please let us know when you’re invited to interview.

About Jagex:

We are Jagex: The RuneScape Company- home to one of gaming’s most enduring success stories. We create deep, community-powered games with worlds that evolve, inspire, and endure. Our flagship MMORPG franchise, RuneScape has welcomed over 300 million player accounts, inspiring generations of players across PC and mobile for 25 years.

As we begin our 26th year, we are accelerating our strategy to expand RuneScape into a broader ecosystem of forever games and connected experiences, grounded in a renewed commitment to integrity and fair play. This includes the reduction of monetisation mechanics, as well as the launch of RuneScape: DragonWilds into Steam Early Access in 2025 representing a major step in building a multi-genre future for the RuneScape universe. We remain focused on building enduring worlds, empowering player-led innovation, and laying the foundations for the boldest era in RuneScape’s history. For more information, visit .

Headquartered in Cambridgeshire, United Kingdom, We are home to passionate creators, storytellers, engineers, and even a few dreamers, all united by a single mission- to shape the future of online worlds and empower players to make them their own. We’re looking for people to join us who share our ambitions & values - We foster an inclusive workplace built on trust, autonomy, and a shared passion for creating experiences which inspire our communities. Our values guide everything we do: We Embrace Fellowship by collaborating and sharing openly. We Hone our Craft by always learning and improving; We Honour our Vows by being honest and transparent; We are our Customers’ Heroes by striving to understand our team & player needs, and We Seize The Day by making the most of every opportunity.

Join us. The next era of RuneScape - and the next chapter of Jagex: The RuneScape Company - starts now.

title: Business Analyst - Canadian Payments
description:
THE ROLE 📝

We’re looking for a Business Analyst with strong payments experience to join Form3’s Product team and play an important role in building out our new Canadian Real-Time Rail (RTR) payment gateway.

Working closely with the Product Manager, you’ll be involved from an early stage in the build, helping to understand payment scheme and business requirements and turn them into clear, actionable requirements that support the development and delivery of the product.

What you’ll be doing:

  • Work closely with the Product Manager to support the end-to-end build and delivery of Form3’s Canadian RTR payment gateway.
  • Understand and analyse payment scheme, product and business requirements, translating these into clear and actionable requirements.
  • Create high-quality user stories, acceptance criteria and functional and non-functional specifications.
  • Analyse the impact of product changes and enhancements and clearly document requirements to support delivery.
  • Use data and analysis to provide insights and support informed product decisions.
  • Collaborate with stakeholders across Product, Engineering and the wider business throughout the product development lifecycle.
  • Build deep knowledge of the Canadian payments ecosystem, becoming a trusted source of payments expertise for colleagues and stakeholders.
  • Take ownership of key Business Analyst activities and deliverables, helping the team move from requirements through to successful product delivery.

WE’RE LOOKING FOR 🔍

As RTR is a new payment scheme, we don’t expect you to have previous RTR experience. What’s much more important is a strong understanding of the Canadian payments landscape and infrastructure, with experience of payment rails such as Interac e-Transfer.

Knowledge of the wider North American payments landscape, including US schemes such as FedNow or RTP, would also be valuable.

Essential

  • Experience working as a Business Analyst within payments, banking or FinTech.
  • Strong knowledge of the Canadian payments ecosystem and infrastructure, ideally including experience with Interac e-Transfer or other Canadian payment rails.
  • Experience translating complex business, product or payment scheme requirements into clear user stories, acceptance criteria and functional specifications.
  • Strong technical understanding of APIs, cloud technologies and modern system architectures, with the ability to translate business requirements into clear technical requirements and collaborate effectively with Engineering teams.
  • A good understanding of the product development lifecycle and experience supporting products from requirements through to delivery.
  • Strong analytical skills, including experience using data to support decision-making.
  • Excellent stakeholder management and communication skills, with the ability to make complex payment concepts clear and actionable.
  • The ability to work autonomously, take ownership and operate effectively in a fast-paced environment.

Desirable

  • Knowledge or experience of the US payments landscape, particularly real-time payment schemes such as FedNow and RTP.
  • Experience working with real-time or instant payments.
  • Broader knowledge of payment schemes, payment infrastructure and how financial institutions move money.

Stage One: Screening Call with the Talent Team
Stage Two: Team Interview with a Senior Business Analyst and Senior Product Manager
Stage Three: Zoom Interview with two Heads of Product
