Global | Permanent

About Citco

Citco is a global leader in fund services, corporate governance and related asset services with staff across 50 office locations worldwide. With more than $1.8 trillion in assets under administration, we deliver end-to-end solutions and exceptional service to meet our clients’ needs.

For more information about Citco, please visit www.citco.com

About the Team & Business Line

Fund Administration is Citco’s core business, and our alternative asset and accounting service is one of the industry’s most respected. Our continuous investment in learning and technology solutions means our people are equipped to deliver a seamless client experience.

Strategic Operations is a dedicated function within Private Assets. It brings transformation delivery, project execution, business analysis, operational initiatives and implementation support into one team, reducing the delivery burden on BAU Operations and maintaining ownership from design through adoption.

The group will be split across three distinct focus areas, aligned under two individual leaders:

Operating Model, Product & Client Solutions: led by the Operating Model & Product leader, this area will define how services should run end to end, shape scalable products and solutions, support complex client implementations, and ensure client commitments are operationally deliverable.

Data, Reporting & Platform Enablement: led by the Technology, Data & Delivery leader, this area will define Operations requirements for data, reporting and platforms, strengthen data quality and lineage, and carry solutions through testing, deployment and adoption.

Digital Workflow, Automation & AI: also led by the Technology, Data & Delivery leader, this area will identify and deliver workflow, automation and AI opportunities, establish appropriate controls, and measure whether the expected benefits are realised.

The group works in close partnership with Operations, the Transformation Office, IT, Tactical Operations and Marquee Client teams. Roles may be permanent or approximately 12-month rotational assignments anchored in strategic locations. Rotational colleagues will join from the business, help shape and deliver change, and return to the line with broader project experience.

Your Role

You will own how we build it, prove it, and land it in the business — with accountability for delivery standards across the whole of Strategic Operations.

  • Lead the Data, Reporting & Platform Enablement and Digital Workflow, Automation & AI focus areas, setting priorities across the technology-enabled change agenda for Private Assets.

  • Own the business analysis and implementation discipline across all three focus areas, including requirements, testing standards, cutover and benefits tracking, so delivery quality is consistent across the group.

  • Set out Operations’ requirements with IT and the Transformation Office, and hold the relationship through build, test and deployment rather than handing over.

  • Sponsor automation and AI opportunities, from identification through to deployment and measured benefit.

  • Own the data, reporting and platform roadmap from an Operations perspective, including data quality, lineage and reporting capability.

  • Govern delivery: release planning, UAT, defect management, deployment readiness and post-implementation review.

  • Partner with Operations to ensure change is understood, trained out and genuinely adopted.

  • Build and develop the team, including the rotational model, and actively participate in recruitment.

  • Maintain alignment with Tactical Operations and Marquee Operations, picking up solutions originating in either for wider reuse.

  • Represent Strategic Operations at Private Assets and CFS technology and delivery forums.

About You

You have 12–15 years’ experience in fund administration, alternative asset management or a related financial services environment, with substantial exposure to technology-enabled change.

  • A demonstrable record of delivering large-scale technology, data or platform initiatives in a financial services setting, with change that was genuinely adopted.

  • Strong understanding of private assets processes and the platform estate that supports them.

  • Credibility with technology partners — able to translate operational need into technical requirement and to challenge a solution design.

  • Practical knowledge of automation, digital workflow and AI, and sound judgement on what is worth automating.

  • Delivery governance experience including testing strategy, cutover planning and benefits realisation.

  • Strong leadership skills and supervisory experience of other professionals, including rotational colleagues joining from the business.

  • Skilled in business planning, budgeting and stakeholder negotiation.

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.

  • Advanced computer skills (Microsoft Excel, Word, PowerPoint and SharePoint).

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Accounting, Finance, Economics or a related field; professional accounting designation a plus.

What We Expect of the Strategic Operations Team

Regardless of role or focus area, everyone in Strategic Operations is expected to demonstrate the following:

  • Deep technical and operational knowledge — genuine depth in how our processes, data and platforms actually work — the detail that only comes from having run the work.

  • Curiosity — the instinct to ask why a process looks the way it does, to challenge the answer, and to keep asking whether there is a better way.

  • A transformational mindset — comfortable redesigning end to end rather than patching, and prepared to see change through past go-live to the point where it is genuinely adopted.

  • Ownership through to adoption — accountability does not end at delivery; success is measured by whether the change sticks in the business.

  • Commercial and client awareness — an understanding of what we can genuinely run, so that what we commit to a client is deliverable.

  • Global mindset — working across regions, jurisdictions and time zones, and designing solutions that scale beyond a single desk, client or location.

  • Ambition to shape Citco’s future — an appetite to help build the operating model we will run for years, and to be measured on whether it works.

Our Benefits

Your well-being is of paramount importance to us, and central to our success. We provide a range of benefits, training and education support, and flexible working arrangements to help you achieve success in your career while balancing personal needs. Ask us about specific benefits in your location.

We embrace diversity, prioritizing the hiring of people from diverse backgrounds. Our inclusive culture is a source of pride and strength, fostering innovation and mutual respect.

Citco welcomes and encourages applications from people with disabilities. Accommodations are available upon request for candidates taking part in all aspects of the selection process.

title: Quality Inspector
description:
Position Summary

A Quality Inspector is responsible for ensuring that products or services meet established quality standards and specifications. They perform visual, mechanical and electrical inspections, tests, and audits to identify any defects or deviations from quality requirements. Quality Inspectors use various tools and techniques to measure and evaluate the quality of materials, components, and finished products. They document and report any non-conformities and work closely with production teams to address quality issues and implement corrective actions. Additionally, they may participate in the development and improvement of quality control processes and procedures.

Supervision:

Essential Responsibilities

  • Perform visual, mechanical and electrical inspections, and testing of all equipment manufactured at Powell facilities according to Powell Standards.
  • Program and operate electronic equipment such as microprocessor-based relays.
  • Energize Powell electrical products and other buyout equipment such as service Panels, HVAC, Battery Chargers, UPS System, etc.
  • Perform equipment failure investigations and root cause analysis.
  • Complete and maintain all test Quality Control documentation as required.
  • Perform maintenance on test equipment as needed.
  • Perform tests using equipment such as multi meter, clamp-on-meter, voltage detector, Hi-Pot, etc.
  • Interaction with all departments (shop, engineering, sales, shipping, fabrication, PCR, switchgear) including customers to work to resolve quality related issues.
  • Interaction with all departments during production, final inspection and final release to shipping is required.
  • External relationships may include regular interaction with other Powell subsidiaries, suppliers and customers.
  • Record Engineering and Shop discrepancies, non-conformities and material shortages utilizing Powell systems.
  • Participates in continuous improvement projects.
  • Promote a safety culture as well as attend all safety meetings.
  • Ensure quality by following standard work instructions and identifying any potential risks to product quality.
  • Ensure that work areas remain clean and well organized.
  • Learn and understand basic electrical principals and relevant Mechanical experience.

Minimum Qualifications

  • High School Diploma or General Education Diploma, or a Trade School diploma or certificate
  • Minimum 1-3 years’ experience in manufacturing environment.
  • Ability to read prints including specification sheets, wiring diagrams, schematics, three-line drawings, wiring lists and part drawings.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in Quality inspection for electrical or electronic equipment or components preferred
  • Intermediate experience working with industry codes and standards and able to refer to applicable codes.

Skills, Abilities & Other Requirements

  • Ability to apply industry standards as applicable to job and product.
  • Actively seeks out self-development through internal or external programs that contributes to knowledge, skill and abilities.
  • Demonstrates integrity and ethical decision making.
  • Conscientious, thorough, accurate, and reliable when performing and completing job tasks.
  • Able to work effectively within a team and around other departments and their activities.
  • Ability to learn and adhere to all manufacturing policies and practices to ensure adherence to ISO requirements.
  • Must be proficient in the English language, both written and verbal.

Working & Environmental Conditions

Working Conditions

Safety sensitive position in a temperature-controlled manufacturing or industrial environment with occasional outside activities.

Required to always wear personnel protective equipment (i.e., hard hats, safety glasses, hearing protection, safety harnesses and respirators) when required.

Working at a desk and computer in an office environment is required.

Must be able to work from all types of ladders (step ladders, "A" frame ladders and all size extension ladders) and scaffolding.

Working at heights usually no higher than 30 feet in the air or using proper lift equipment.

Physical Requirements

Able to maintain body equilibrium and agility to prevent falling when walking, standing, crouching, ascending or descending stairs.

Bending the body at the waist, the legs at the knees, and extending arms and hands in any direction in a repetitive manner continuously.

Continuous standing, walking 50–300-foot distances for long periods of time with only occasional sitting.

Must be able to climb stairs frequently throughout the shift.

Able to frequently look over shoulders, work with both arms above shoulders and use both arms at full length frequently.

Using upper extremities to apply or exert a force continuously up to 50lbs.

Ability to use hand tools such as tin snips, hammer, and power tools (some vibrating), for long periods of time with frequent repetition.

More Information

Headquartered in Akron, Ohio, FirstEnergy includes one of the nation's largest investor-owned electric systems, more than 24,000 miles of transmission lines that connect the Midwest and Mid-Atlantic regions, and a regulated generating fleet with a total capacity of more than 3,500 megawatts.

This position can be located any FE Headquarter locations

The selected candidate may be offered a position within the same job family, at a level that is lower than what was posted. The DPUC department’s responsibilities are as follows:

  • Oversee the current-year portfolio to ensure projects are delivered on time, on scope, and on budget while balancing tradeoffs and ensuring compliance with governance processes and emergent needs

  • Receive, evaluate, and process Joint Use attachment projects from beginning to end to meet FirstEnergy regulatory objectives, while maximizing cost recovery and measuring financial impacts

This role supports the forecasting and management of key portfolio and utility coordination components, including budgets, resources, materials, project schedules, regulatory timelines and work plans.

This position provides analytical and reporting support to the Distribution Portfolio and Utility Coordination team, helping ensure accurate insights into project performance, financials, benefits and risks.

Key Responsibilities

  • Reporting & Data Management

  • Develop and maintain accurate financial and operational reports using tools such as Power BI, QlikView, TOAD Data Point, and Microsoft Office.

  • Analyze data to identify trends, risks, and improvement opportunities.

  • Ensure data integrity through regular validation and updates.

  • Stakeholder Collaboration

  • Partner with internal and external stakeholders to align priorities and ensure consistent processes.

  • Serve as a liaison to facilitate clear communication across teams.

  • Executive Reporting

  • Translate complex financial and operational data into actionable insights.

  • Systems & Tools

  • Utilize systems such as SAP, Sage, Navigator, HVK, OPPM, Ecosys, and Unifier to generate reports.

  • Identify and implement process improvements and reporting automation.

  • Analytical Support

  • Assist in monitoring project scope, estimates, budget, and schedule performance.

Qualifications

title: Assembly Technician I
description:
At Thorlabs, we design and manufacture components, instruments, and systems that transform the world by identifying, enabling, and accelerating key photonics (i.e., light-based) technologies. Backed by a dedicated workforce of more than 3,000 employees worldwide, Thorlabs contributes to cutting-edge research and real-world innovation.

Whether you're early in your career or bringing years of experience, you’ll find opportunities to grow, take ownership, and make meaningful contributions from day one. We know every employee brings unique talents and perspectives that fuel our success, and we seek driven individuals who are excited to make an impact in a fun, fast-moving culture.

The Assembly Technician Level I is responsible for the assembly of laser systems and accessories.. Core responsibilities include electrical, mechanical, and optical fiber assembly; generating production test data; preparing products for shipment; and maintaining accurate records within the ERP system. This role requires the ability to follow detailed assembly instructions, while properly using sensitive instruments and tools to perform precise assembly tasks and measurements.

• Build electrical, mechanical, and optical assemblies according to work instructions.

• Perform basic electronic soldering and crimping tasks in accordance with documented procedures and industry standards • Operate sensitive production equipment such as fiber splicers, optical test instruments, and alignment tools after training and according to documented procedures.

• Handle and assemble intricate opto-mechanical components and assemblies, including fragile optics and/or optical fibers. • Perform laser and accessory system alignments following documented procedures.

• Maintain data systems to record and report test results.

• Follow work instructions, engineering drawings, and other production documentation for complex systems involving electronics, mechanical assemblies, and fiber components.

• Follow cleanroom protocols and maintain a high standard of cleanliness in work areas.

• Provide continuous improvement feedback on procedures and processes.

• Meet output and quality goals.

Requirements

Experience:

• 0-3 years of experience in electronics, fiber optics, photonics or related industry, or specialized training in these fields

• Proficiency working with computers and Microsoft Office is required.

Education:

• High school diploma or equivalent (e.g, GED)

Specialized knowledge and skills that are desired but not required:

• Demonstrated ability to work with minimal supervision in a collaborative, team environment and comply with high-quality standards.

• Familiarity with soldering and crimping for electrical assembly is a plus.

• Experience with optical fibers and optical measurement instruments is a plus

• Knowledge of inventory management, shipping/receiving practices, and ERP systems preferred.

The estimated hourly rate for this role is $ 19.00 to $ 26.00 per hour

Thorlabs values its diverse environment and is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity/Affirmative Action employer. All qualified individuals will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identify or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age or veteran status. Job descriptions are not intended as and do not create employment contracts. The organization maintains its status as an at-will employer. Employees can be terminated for any reason not prohibited by law.

Benefits

Thorlabs offers a complete benefits package that includes medical, dental and vision insurance, company paid life insurance, a generous PTO package, a 401(k) plan, and tuition reimbursement just to name a few.

description:

title: Director of Restaurants
location: Half Moon Bay, CA, United States
description:
JOB SUMMARY

Manages all restaurant operations and staff on a daily basis. Areas of responsibility include Restaurants/Bars and Room Service. As a department head, directs and works with the food and beverage/culinary management team and employees to successfully execute all restaurant operations. Strives to continually improve guest and employee satisfaction and maximize the financial performance in areas of responsibility.

CANDIDATE PROFILE

Education and Experience

• High school diploma or GED; 6 years experience in the food and beverage, culinary, event management, or related professional area.

OR

• 2-year degree from an accredited university in Food Service Management, Hotel and Restaurant Management, Hospitality, Business Administration, or related major; 4 years experience in the food and beverage, culinary, event management, or related professional area.

Skills and Knowledge

• Customer and Personal Service - Knowledge of principles and processes for providing customer and personal services. This includes customer needs assessment, meeting quality standards for services, and evaluation of customer satisfaction.

• Economics and Accounting - Knowledge of economic and accounting principles and practices, P&L statements, operating budgets, forecasting and scheduling, and the reporting of financial data.

• Analytical/Critical Thinking - The ability to gather and organize information using a logical and systematic process; recognize patterns and relationships in complex data; examine data to identify implications, problems and draw appropriate conclusions; generate alternative solutions to problems; evaluate strengths, weaknesses and consequences of alternative solutions and approaches to solving problems.

• Management of Financial Resources - Determining how money will be spent to get the work done, and accounting for these expenditures.

• Administration and Management - Knowledge of business and management principles involved in strategic planning, resource allocation, human resources modeling, leadership technique, production methods, and coordination of people and resources.

• Applied Business Knowledge - Understanding market dynamics, enterprise level objectives and important aspects of the company’s business to accurately diagnose strengths and weaknesses, anticipate opportunities and risks, identify issues, and develop strategies and plans. Aligning individual and team actions with strategies and plans to drive business results.

• Food Production and Presentation - Knowledge of techniques and equipment for preparing and presenting food products (both plant and animal) for consumption, including storage/handling techniques and sanitation standards.

• Management of Material Resources - Obtaining and seeing to the appropriate use of equipment, facilities, and materials needed to do certain work.

CORE WORK ACTIVITIES

Managing Day-to-Day Operations

• Estimate food, liquor, wine, and other beverage consumption in order to anticipate amounts to be purchased or requisitioned.

• Facilitates pre-meal briefings with the Chef and Restaurant Managers to educate restaurant staff on menu items including ingredients, preparation methods and unique tastes.

• Maintains service and sanitation standards in restaurant, bar/lounge and room service areas.

• Order and purchase equipment and supplies.

• Oversees the booking and manages service of restaurant parties, special events and room service hospitality suites.

Developing and Maintaining Budgets

• Manages department's controllable expenses to achieve or exceed budgeted goals.

• Understands the impact of department's operation on the overall property financial goals.

Leading Food and Beverage Team

• Establishes challenging, realistic and obtainable goals to guide operation and performance.

• Utilizes interpersonal and communication skills to lead, influence, and encourage others; advocates sound financial/business decision making; demonstrates honesty/integrity; leads by example.

• Encourages and builds mutual trust, respect, and cooperation among team members.

• Achieves and exceeds goals including performance goals, budget goals, team goals, etc.

• Serves as a role model to demonstrate appropriate behaviors.

• Develops means to improve profit, including estimating cost and benefit, exploring new business opportunities, etc.

• Identifies the developmental needs of others and coaches, mentors, or otherwise helps others to improve their knowledge or skills.

• Acts as the guest service role model for the restaurants, sets a good example of excellent customer service, and creates a positive atmosphere for guest relations.

• Displays leadership in guest hospitality, exemplifies excellent customer service and creates a positive atmosphere for guest relations.

• Ensures cash control and liquor control procedures are followed by all Restaurant, Bar/Lounge and Room Service employees.

• Ensures compliance with all food & beverage policies, standards and procedures by training, supervising, follow-up and hands on management.

• Ensures compliance with food handling and sanitation standards.

• Ensures staff understands all applicable liquor laws.

• Establishes guidelines for customer service so employees understand expectations and parameters.

• Strives to improve service performance.

Ensuring Exceptional Customer Service

• Provides services that are above and beyond for customer satisfaction and retention.

• Improves service by communicating and assisting individuals to understand guest needs, providing guidance, feedback, and individual coaching when needed.

• Estimates cost and benefit ratio, maintaining balance between profit and service satisfaction.

• Empowers employees to provide excellent customer service.

• Incorporates guest satisfaction as a component of departmental meetings with a focus on continuous improvement.

• Interacts with guests to obtain feedback on product quality and service levels.

• Meets with guests on an informal basis during meals or upon departure to obtain feedback on quality of food and beverage, service levels and overall satisfaction.

• Responds effectively to guest problems and handles complaints.

• Reviews guest satisfaction feedback with employees to develop appropriate corrective action.

Managing and Conducting Human Resource Activities

• Provides guidance and direction to subordinates, including setting performance standards and monitoring performance.

• Ensures that expectations and objectives are clearly communicated to subordinates; subordinates are also open to raise questions and/or concerns.

• Administers the performance appraisal process for direct report managers.

• Communicates performance expectations in accordance with job descriptions for each position and monitors progress.

• Ensures employees are treated fairly and equitably.

• Ensures property policies are administered fairly and consistently.

• Interviews and hires management and hourly employees with the appropriate skills to meet the business needs of the operation.

• Observes service behaviors of employees and provides feedback to individuals and or managers.

Additional Responsibilities

• Informs and/or update the executives, the peers and the subordinates on relevant information in a timely manner.

• Provides information to supervisors, co-workers, and subordinates by telephone, in written form, e-mail, or in person.

• Analyzes information and evaluating results to choose the best solution and solve problems.

title: Research Associate -Neurological Disorders and Diseases
description:
We are looking for a highly self-motivated Research Associate with the ability to work both in vitro and in vivo collaboratively within a team. This role offers an exciting opportunity to investigate cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying the pathophysiology of neurological diseases and disorders such as stroke, Alzheimer’s disease, and Parkinson’s disease with a focus on the role of neuroinflammation, epigenetic regulation and microRNAs, and on protein regulation and degradation such as ubiquitination and autophagy. Our research aims to identify novel therapeutic targets for these challenging conditions.

The successful candidate will engage in discussions with the Principal Investigator (PI) and other scientists in the lab to design, execute, and troubleshoot experiments, as well as to analyze and interpret results. Opportunities for involvement in the preparation of manuscripts and scientific reports will be provided.

The position requires 8 working hours per day (40 hours per week). The schedule may be flexible depending on experimental needs, and working hours may occasionally extend into evenings or weekends.

  • Engage in discussions with the Principal Investigator (PI) and other scientists in the lab to design, execute, and troubleshoot experiments, as well as to analyze and interpret results.

  • Provide a wide variety of laboratory testing and technical lab support for projects in the laboratory.

  • Document experiments, maintain laboratory notebook, analyze data, and report using complex statistical computer software.

Qualifications:

• B.S./B.A. or M.S. in areas of biology, chemistry, or a related field of science.
• 3+ year’s research lab experience
• Strong background on neurological disorders and diseases preferred.
• Prior experience in rodent surgery and handling preferred.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:

• Excellent verbal and written communication skills, organizational skills, and analytical skills required.
• Requires knowledge of the processes/procedures in testing, documenting experiments, maintaining laboratory notebook, analyzing data, and reporting using complex statistical computer software.

title: Subcontract Field Coordinator II
description:
The Subcontract Field Coordinator II works in a team environment, leads a team of Subcontract Field Coordinators and will be assigned subcontracts or services packages to oversee the field execution of the subcontractor or service provider based on highest complexity on the project. The Subcontract Field Coordinator II understands commercial agreements, technical specifications and safe construction craft execution. The Subcontract Field Coordinator II leads the oversite of the subcontractors or service providers in the field to ensure the providers are cooperating with Zachry craft and other subcontractors/service providers while executing their work in a safe, quality way while following the defined schedule and technical requirements. The Subcontract Field Coordinator II works with the Subcontract Managers to ensure each subcontractor or service providers is following the commercial agreement they are bound to while coordinating and removing any limitations caused by direct craft or other providers that could hinder their completion of the work.

Position Responsibilities:

  • Assist in the development, preparation and award of subcontract/service bids along with the presentation of rational behind the recommended award.
  • Attend assign subcontract/services project meetings to ensure schedule, priorities and expectations are being met including kick off, pre-mobilization and on-site meetings.
  • Monitors contractor progress and performance, ensures work is performed in a safe and quality manner.
  • Assist with the project change and claim management procedures and processes including the identification of change orders, back charges, drawing revisions, etc.
  • Maintains daily work and manpower logs for each subcontractor/service provider assigned to them.
  • Assist in the reviews, evaluations and authorization of progress payments based upon actual work completed.
  • Provide updates to Subcontract Administrators on the progress of each subcontract/service providers assigned to them.
  • Oversees the field coordination with direct craft and other subcontract/service providers.
  • Leads weekly field reviews of subcontract/service providers.
  • Leads subcontract/service turnover and closeout.

Essential Skills, Knowledge, and Abilities (Include any training, licenses and certifications):

  • 5 years of experience in subcontract management or 1-3 years of craft experience as a Superintendent on an industrial construction or maintenance services projects.
  • Craft specific - such as Electrical & Instrumentation and Transportation Management.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS:

  • Employee will be required to adhere to large amounts of standing, walking, bending, squatting, sitting, and lifting.
  • Will talk and hear to communicate.
  • Will use arms and hands to signal, grab, hold, turn, push, and pull objects, materials, controls and tools.
  • May be required to pick up, lift, carry and move up to 50lbs.
  • Will work at heights, climb ladders and stairways, and may occasionally work off platforms/scaffolding using the appropriate fall protection requirements.
  • Must be able to work in all weather conditions (including heat, rain, cold and wind) while wearing appropriate PPE.
  • Will be required to wear personal protective equipment (PPE) including but not limited to; hard hat, safety glasses/goggles, ear plugs, masks/respirators, hi-vis safety vests, leather gloves and leather steel-toed work boots.

WORK ENVIRONMENT:

Will work in all weather conditions ranging from warm/hot – cool/cold. Occasional rain. Will work at different elevations. May be required to work in close, confined spaces for a long period of time. Noise levels will be moderate to high.

ZACHRY is dedicated to providing a Safe and Drug-Free work environment and is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

title: Quality Assurance Engineer
description:
The Quality Assurance Engineer IV finds bugs, defects, and regressions. This role will design, implement, execute, and debug test cases and/or automated test scripts. Validate and document completion of testing and development. Verify fixes and help ensure successful releases by planning and executing test activities for exploratory and regression testing.

This person will demonstrate and apply product, domain, or technical expertise to maximize the quality of testing for a development team. They will maintain a positive and professional attitude. While also indentifying opportunities for improving processes, training and tools and make appropriate recommendations to management.

Essential Tasks

  • Review requirements, specifications, and technical design documents to provide timely and meaningful feedback
  • Develop testing plans and testing scenarios in accordance with the functional requirements and detail technical specifications provided by the design team to ensure code generated by the development team conforms to the specified requirements
  • Estimate, prioritize, plan and coordinate testing activities within a cross-functional development team
  • Design, develop and execute test cases and/or automation scripts using provided tools
  • Identify, record, document, and track bugs
  • Perform regular regression, exploratory and system testing as required
  • Monitor and maintain bug backlogs for accuracy
  • Leverage AI-enabled tools and analytics to enhance decision-making, improve efficiency, and drive measurable business outcomes when appropriate.
  • Apply sound judgment and ethical standards when using AI, ensuring accuracy, data privacy, and responsible human-in-the-loop oversight.
  • Other duties as assigned

Preferred Skills & Experience

  • 6+ years professional experience
  • Must have strong diagnostic skills to properly test software and measure the quality of the product
  • Must have a technical background to be able to create proper testing scenarios from the functional requirements and detail specifications
  • Experience with Microsoft SQL Server Management Studio and writing SQL queries
  • Experience with QA testing on ERP type applications/systems
  • A thorough understanding administrative software for higher education and experience with automated testing tools are a plus
  • Proficiency with at least one programming or scripting language a plus

title: Structural Engineering Intern- Summer 2027
description:
This Opportunity

WSP USA hosts hundreds of internships across the United States to gain hands-on, meaningful work experience to enhance their education and professional aptitude. Our interns gain exposure to real projects while working side by side with senior staff. Through our Developing Professionals Network, interns gain mentorship, networking opportunities and lifelong career connections.

Our Structures Team is seeking a Full-Time Senior Intern (Structures) to work out of our Glastonbury, CT office. This temporary position is seeking individuals currently enrolled in an Undergraduate or Graduate degree program.

This internship will be part of the WSP Summer Internship Program. As a summer intern, you have the opportunity to participate in our 12-week program scheduled to start on May 17, 2027. The individual start date of the internship may be flexible.

The position is an exciting opportunity for exposure to multiple discipline civil engineering projects (structural, site/civil, highway, transportation, etc.) in support of heavy highway and rail design and construction projects. These include projects with the following agencies:

• Connecticut Department of Transportation

• Rhode Island Department of Transportation

• Rhode Island Turnpike and Bridge Authority

• & other New England and Northeast Transportation Agencies

Your Impact

  • Support a variety of engineering tasks with the goal to develop technical, social, and ethical skills.
  • Learn basic principles of Civil and Structural Engineering.
  • Assist with project research, field work, and preliminary design calculations and analysis.
  • Support preparation of final design plans (Bentley/MicroStation, AutoCAD and Revit), and cost estimates.
  • Assist in collecting and maintaining project documentation.
  • Complete training on assigned tasks.
  • Exercise responsible and ethical decision-making regarding company funds, resources and conduct, and adhere to WSP’s Code of Conduct and related policies and procedures.
  • Perform additional responsibilities as required by business needs.
  • Please note that there is no relocation or housing assistance associated with this internship.

Who You Are

Required Qualifications

  • Actively enrolled in an accredited Civil Engineering, or related, Undergraduate program with an anticipated graduation date of May 2028 or later.
  • Must be 18 or older.
  • Demonstrated interest in Structural and Civil Engineering, or related field, and have a strong desire to advance skills related to WSP’s work and projects.
  • Competent interpersonal and communication skills when interacting with others, expressing ideas effectively and professionally to an engineering and non-engineering audience.
  • Capable of taking direction from leadership, mentors, and managers to executive projects.
  • Basic proficiency with technical writing, office automation, software, spreadsheets, technology, and tools.
  • Proven track record of upholding workplace safety and ability to abide by WSP’s health, safety and drug/alcohol and harassment policies.
  • Authorization to work in the United States at the start of the internship

Preferred Qualifications

  • Actively enrolled in an accredited Civil Engineering Bachelors program, or related, Masters or PhD program with an anticipated graduation date of May 2028 or later.
  • Experience using AutoCAD, Bentley/MicroStation or Revit Cad platforms/programs.
  • Prior internship and leadership involvement on campus.

title: Senior Mainframe Developer
description:
About This Opportunity

We are seeking an experienced Senior Mainframe Developer to lead the remediation and modernization of a 50-year-old legacy COBOL system running on a Unisys mainframe platform. This role will be responsible for analyzing, modifying, and enhancing critical business applications to support integration with Workday Human Capital Management (HCM), Payroll, Finance, and related enterprise services.

This individual will work closely with enterprise architects, Workday integration developers, business analysts, infrastructure teams, and business stakeholders to enable reliable and secure data exchange between legacy applications and the Workday platform.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Legacy System Assessment & Remediation
    • Analyze and document existing Unisys-based COBOL applications, batch processes, databases, interfaces, and data flows.
    • Review and assess approximately 50 years of application code for technical debt, dependencies, and remediation requirements.
    • Identify and resolve code defects, performance bottlenecks, and system integration constraints.
    • Refactor, modify, and enhance COBOL programs to support modern integration patterns.
    • Maintain business continuity while implementing system changes.
  • Workday Integration Enablement
    • Design and implement integration solutions between legacy Unisys applications and Workday.
    • Create outbound interfaces for legacy data to Workday.
    • Develop inbound processes to consume Workday-generated data.
    • Support Workday APIs, web services, EIBs, and middleware-based integrations.
    • Design data transformation and validation processes to ensure data integrity.
  • Data Analysis & Conversion
    • Analyze existing master and transactional data structures.
    • Map legacy data elements to Workday objects.
    • Identify data quality issues and develop remediation plans.
    • Support migration and reconciliation activities.
    • Develop automated processes for data extraction and transformation.
  • Architecture & Modernization
    • Provide recommendations for modernization and technical roadmaps.
    • Identify opportunities to reduce technical debt and improve maintainability.
    • Implement best practices for application lifecycle management.
    • Document system architecture, interfaces, and operational procedures.
  • Testing & Quality Assurance
    • Develop and execute unit, system, integration, and regression testing strategies.
    • Support end-to-end testing with Workday and external systems.
    • Ensure all modifications comply with security, audit, and regulatory requirements.
  • Production Support
    • Provide support for production deployments.
    • Troubleshoot integration failures and batch processing issues.
    • Participate in on-call support during critical implementation periods.
    • Monitor system performance and recommend improvements.

Requirements

You have:

  • Education
    • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, or a related field.
    • Equivalent combination of education and relevant experience may be considered.
  • Experience
    • 10+ years of COBOL development experience.
    • 7+ years supporting enterprise mainframe environments.
    • 5+ years working with Unisys mainframe platforms.
    • Experience maintaining highly customized legacy applications over multiple decades.
    • Experience supporting large-scale modernization or digital transformation initiatives.
    • Experience integrating legacy systems with cloud-based SaaS platforms.
    • Experience with COBOL-74, COBOL-85, or Enterprise COBOL.
    • Experience with DMSII databases.
    • Experience with batch processing systems and JCL or equivalent job scheduling frameworks.
    • Experience with enterprise integration technologies, including REST APIs, SOAP web services, ETL processes, data mapping and transformation, middleware platforms, message queues, and secure file transfer solutions.
    • Experience with relational databases and SQL.
    • Experience with one or more of the following: Workday HCM, Workday Payroll, Workday Financials, Workday Studio, Workday Web Services (WWS), Enterprise Interface Builder (EIB), or Workday integration frameworks.

This job is for you if you possess:

  • Technical Leadership
    • Experience mentoring junior and mid-level developers.
  • Business Analysis Skills
    • Understanding of payroll, HR, finance, and workforce management business processes.
  • Strong Communication
    • Experience communicating with executives, architects, business stakeholders, and technical teams.
  • Legal Authorization
    • Eligible to work in the United States.

Benefits

About Us

AG Consulting Partners, Inc. is a Redmond-based boutique consulting firm. Our mission is to embrace the entrepreneurial spirit to relentlessly deliver an exceptional experience and results for our people and our clients.

We put our people first. Our excellent benefits to full-time employees include medical, dental, vision, PTO, 401K matching, education reimbursement, community and philanthropic events and flexible career paths.

We’re humbled to be consistently acknowledged by local and national organizations for our success, including Consulting Magazine, Puget Sound Business Journal, and Inc. 5000.

We strive to ensure that our compensation package is competitive and fair, taking into account various factors to provide a rewarding opportunity for our team members.

title: Vehicle Inspector

What Centria Offers:

  • Early Intervention, Big Impact – Help shape a child’s future during the years when ABA therapy can make the most significant developmental difference.

  • Purpose-Built Centers – Our LSAA centers are thoughtfully designed for children 5 and under, with low-distraction spaces, play-based learning areas, and a strong emphasis on routines and safety.

  • Clinical Quality First – We prioritize outcomes, not billables. Our proprietary CareConnect platform streamlines everything from treatment planning to data collection so you can stay focused on care, not paperwork.

  • Assent-Based and Play-Focused – We blend Practical Functional Assessment and Skills-Based Treatment into a compassionate, assent-based model, centered around joyful, meaningful learning.

  • Real Work-Life Balance – Small caseloads, manageable schedules, and dedicated support teams mean no last-minute chaos and no burnout.

  • You're Never Alone – With layered support from Clinical Directors, Area Clinical Directors, and our Clinical Excellence Team, you'll always have someone in your corner.

  • No Operational Headaches – We handle the logistics. From scheduling to onboarding of technicians, our operations team keeps everything running smoothly behind the scenes.

  • Career Growth on Your Terms – Whether you're mentoring the next generation of BCBAs, leading clinical training, or stepping into leadership, we support your growth.

  • We Invest in You – From CEU stipends and paid CEU days to exclusive internal training events, we’re serious about keeping you sharp—and helping you level up.

As part of the Clifton Campus of UC Health, Greater Cincinnati’s academic health system, University of Cincinnati Medical Center has served Greater Cincinnati and Northern Kentucky for nearly 200 years. Each year, hundreds of thousands of patients receive care from our world-renowned clinicians and care team. The Psychiatric Therapeutic Program Worker (TPW), in collaboration with other members of the healthcare team, is responsible for maintaining a therapeutic milieu and a safe environment for all psychiatric patients on the unit. As a member of the patient care team, the TPW performs selected duties under the direction of the Registered Nurse, to ensure quality patient care.

  • Engages in population appropriate communication.
  • Has knowledge of growth and development milestones and tasks.
  • Gives clear instructions to patients/family regarding treatment.
  • Involves family/guardian in the assessment, initial treatment and continuing care of the patient.
  • Identifies any physical limitations of the patient and deploys intervention when necessary.
  • Recognizes and responds appropriately to patients/families with behavioral health problems.
  • Interprets population related data and plans care appropriately.
  • Identifies and responds appropriately to different needs resulting from, unique psychological needs or those associated with religious / cultural norms. Performs treatments, administers medication or operates equipment safely.
  • Recognizes and responds to signs/symptoms of abuse or neglect.
  • Establish a therapeutic milieu and provide a safe environment for all psychiatric patients. The Psychiatric Therapeutic Program Worker (TPW), in collaboration with other members of the healthcare team, is responsible for maintaining a therapeutic milieu and a safe environment for all psychiatric patients on the unit. This includes monitoring the unit for safety at all times, maintaining a quiet and peaceful atmosphere, managing patient's behavior, preparing room for patient's arrival, orienting patients to the unit, checking belongings for hazardous objects or weapons, securing all belongings in designated areas, provide routine bed checks and secure areas.

These assignments may include but are not limited to: NIPPAS for vital signs and daily weights, phlebotomy, EKG, finger sticks, assistance with feedings, personal hygiene/grooming, ADL's, collecting meal trays and returning to dietary, clean dining area, provide clean linen and dispose of soiled linen, and assist with inventory control and distribution of supplies and equipment in the clinical areas and hallways.

Observe individual behaviors and group interactions and report any major change in patient's behavior and/or medical condition to the RN.
  • Initiate basic psychiatric interventions and provide appropriate redirection as needed. Uses age appropriate communication skills. Provide non-punitive limit setting, appropriate modeling and reinforcement as needed to meet the patient's emotional needs. Assist in physical crisis management as needed and/or assigned.
  • Participate in quality improvement activities. Attend staff meetings, in-service sessions, and crisis intervention programs. Performs other duties as delegated or directed by RN, Clinical Manager or Nursing Supervisor.
  • Transport patients to X-ray, EEG, MRI, clinic appointments, etc.

  • Minimum Required: High School diploma/GED. Preferred: Relevant college coursework.
  • STNA certification preferred or college-level coursework in nursing/psychiatry/social work.
  • Minimum Required: Six months direct patient care experience in psychiatric setting or equivalent college-level coursework in nursing/psychology/social work.
  • Preferred: Specialized training in phlebotomy, vitals signs, and assistance with activities of daily living experience.
  • For employees working in UCMC Psychiatric Services, NCI-APS (Nonviolent Crisis Intervention with Advanced Physical Skills) Certification must be obtained within 90 days of hire.

title: Staff Software Engineer - Search Platform
description:
About the role and team

Uber's Search Platform team builds and operates the foundational search infrastructure powering critical business applications and services. Our platform supports a diverse and rapidly evolving set of workloads, spanning lexical search, semantic and vector search, observability and emerging agentic AI applications.

We are looking for a passionate Staff Software Engineer to help us build the next generation of Search Platform—a highly scalable, reliable, cost-efficient, and intelligent retrieval infrastructure designed to meet the demands of both traditional search and AI-native workloads.

You will have the opportunity to solve challenging distributed systems problems at Uber scale, push the boundaries of modern search technologies, and shape the future of how data is indexed, retrieved, and consumed across Uber's ecosystem.

What you’ll do

  • Build next-generation search infrastructure: Design and develop highly scalable, low-latency, and reliable distributed search systems that power Uber's critical business applications.
  • Advance search and retrieval capabilities: Develop and optimize lexical, semantic, vector, and hybrid search capabilities to support increasingly complex retrieval workloads.
  • Enable AI-native and agentic applications: Evolve the search platform to support emerging AI and agentic workloads, including intelligent retrieval, contextual search, and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG).
  • Drive performance and efficiency: Optimize indexing throughput, query latency, resource utilization, and infrastructure costs across large-scale distributed systems.
  • Solve complex engineering challenges: Tackle problems involving distributed indexing, storage architecture, query execution, data freshness, scalability, and system reliability.
  • Shape platform architecture and strategy: Contribute to technical direction and architectural decisions that enable the platform to evolve with Uber's growing business and AI needs.
  • Collaborate across teams/organizations: Partner with engineering and product teams to understand diverse search requirements and deliver reusable, high-impact platform capabilities.

Basic Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • 8+ years of professional software engineering experience, including significant experience designing and building large-scale distributed systems.
  • Strong expertise in distributed systems architecture, concurrency, data structures, algorithms, and performance optimization.
  • Proficiency in one or more systems or backend programming languages, such as Java, Go, Rust or C++.
  • Proven track record of architecting and delivering complex, production-grade infrastructure systems with high availability and scalability requirements.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead technically ambiguous, cross-team initiatives from architecture and design through execution and production adoption.

Preferred Qualifications

title: Senior Vice President, Operating Model, Product & Client Solutions
description:
Senior Vice President, Operating Model, Product & Client Solutions

Global | Permanent

About Citco

Citco is a global leader in fund services, corporate governance and related asset services with staff across 50 office locations worldwide. With more than $1.8 trillion in assets under administration, we deliver end-to-end solutions and exceptional service to meet our clients’ needs.

For more information about Citco, please visit www.citco.com

About the Team & Business Line

Fund Administration is Citco’s core business, and our alternative asset and accounting service is one of the industry’s most respected. Our continuous investment in learning and technology solutions means our people are equipped to deliver a seamless client experience.

Strategic Operations is a dedicated function within Private Assets. It brings transformation delivery, project execution, business analysis, operational initiatives and implementation support into one team, reducing the delivery burden on BAU Operations and maintaining ownership from design through adoption.

The group will be split across three distinct focus areas, aligned under two individual leaders:

Operating Model, Product & Client Solutions: led by the Operating Model & Product leader, this area will define how services should run end to end, shape scalable products and solutions, support complex client implementations, and ensure client commitments are operationally deliverable.

Data, Reporting & Platform Enablement: led by the Technology, Data & Delivery leader, this area will define Operations requirements for data, reporting and platforms, strengthen data quality and lineage, and carry solutions through testing, deployment and adoption.

Digital Workflow, Automation & AI: also led by the Technology, Data & Delivery leader, this area will identify and deliver workflow, automation and AI opportunities, establish appropriate controls, and measure whether the expected benefits are realised.

The group works in close partnership with Operations, the Transformation Office, IT, Tactical Operations and Marquee Client teams. Roles may be permanent or approximately 12-month rotational assignments anchored in strategic locations. Rotational colleagues will join from the business, help shape and deliver change, and return to the line with broader project experience.

Your Role

You will lead end-to-end operating model and product redesign for a portfolio of Private Assets services, from problem definition through to adoption.

  • Lead the redesign of how a service runs end to end — not patching an existing process, but rebuilding it around what the business and clients actually need.

  • Translate operational pain points into a defined scope, business case and delivery plan.

  • Define the target operating model for a product or service, including roles, handoffs, controls and location strategy.

  • Develop and implement best practice standards across regions, driving consistency and efficiency.

  • Act as the Operations voice in client pitches, POCs and solution design, and hold the line on what is genuinely deliverable.

  • Lead operational solution design for our marquee clients, working alongside Client Services, Product and Client Integration.

  • Own the marquee solution reuse assessment — identifying where a client-specific build could be productised for the wider book, and leading that rollout.

  • Lead complex client transitions and implementations from an Operations standpoint, working alongside the integration team on new client setup.

  • Set out requirements with the Data, Reporting & Platform Enablement and Digital Workflow, Automation & AI focus areas where a redesign or client solution depends on data, platform or automation capability.

  • Coordinate across Operations, Tactical Operations, Marquee Client teams, Financial Statements, Tax, Investor Relations and Client Integration.

  • Lead and mentor focus area resources, including rotational colleagues joining from the business.

  • Report on progress, risks and benefits realisation to the relevant leader and senior stakeholders.

About You

You have 12–15 years’ experience in private assets, working at a fund administrator, fund manager or comparable environment.

  • Proven delivery of operating model redesign, process re-engineering or transformation initiatives in financial services.

  • Strong technical knowledge of private assets accounting and operations, including fund structures and complex calculations.

  • The ability to see a whole service end to end rather than a single desk, and to design for scale across jurisdictions.

  • Significant exposure to large or complex client relationships, with credibility in front of clients and the judgement to distinguish between a reasonable request and an unsustainable commitment.

  • The ability to recognise where a bespoke solution has wider application, and to make the case for productising it.

  • Comfortable working with data, reporting and platform teams and translating operational need into technical requirements.

  • Strong leadership skills and supervisory experience of other professionals, including rotational colleagues joining from the business.

  • Skilled in business planning, budgeting and stakeholder negotiation.

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.

  • Advanced computer skills (Microsoft Excel, Word, PowerPoint and SharePoint).

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Accounting, Finance, Economics or a related field; professional accounting designation a plus.

What We Expect of the Strategic Operations Team

Regardless of role or focus area, everyone in Strategic Operations is expected to demonstrate the following:

  • Deep technical and operational knowledge — genuine depth in how our processes, data and platforms actually work — the detail that only comes from having run the work.

  • Curiosity — the instinct to ask why a process looks the way it does, to challenge the answer, and to keep asking whether there is a better way.

  • A transformational mindset — comfortable redesigning end to end rather than patching, and prepared to see change through past go-live to the point where it is genuinely adopted.

  • Ownership through to adoption — accountability does not end at delivery; success is measured by whether the change sticks in the business.

  • Commercial and client awareness — an understanding of what we can genuinely run, so that what we commit to a client is deliverable.

  • Global mindset — working across regions, jurisdictions and time zones, and designing solutions that scale beyond a single desk, client or location.

  • Ambition to shape Citco’s future — an appetite to help build the operating model we will run for years, and to be measured on whether it works.

Our Benefits

Your well-being is of paramount importance to us, and central to our success. We provide a range of benefits, training and education support, and flexible working arrangements to help you achieve success in your career while balancing personal needs. Ask us about specific benefits in your location.

We embrace diversity, prioritizing the hiring of people from diverse backgrounds. Our inclusive culture is a source of pride and strength, fostering innovation and mutual respect.

Citco welcomes and encourages applications from people with disabilities. Accommodations are available upon request for candidates taking part in all aspects of the selection process.

title: Site Reliability Engineer (SRE)
description:
About Enformion

Enformion is a dynamic powerhouse in data intelligence and AI-powered identity verification. We deliver next-generation fraud prevention, risk management, and seamless onboarding solutions that foster ironclad trust between digital marketplaces, merchants, and consumers. By leveraging our massive data repositories and advanced behavioral analysis, we provide continuous monitoring for emerging risk indicators.

In a digital world where security and trust are everything, Enformion is at the forefront of the industry—and we are growing fast.

Job Purpose

Enformion provides identity and contact data to enterprise clients through APIs, and supports a network of consumer-facing websites built on that data. Enformion is seeking a Site Reliability Engineer to keep these sites and APIs available, fast, and protected from abusive traffic. This role sits where reliability and security meet.

The SRE will work closely with software engineering, information security, and legal/compliance to build and maintain reliable, scalable, and secure infrastructure. The role covers monitoring, resolving complex technical issues, and automating solutions to recurring problems, and it plays a central part in optimizing Enformion platforms and infrastructure.

Salary - $150K-$165K

Responsibilities

Reliability and monitoring

  • Monitor availability, latency, and error rates across Enformion APIs. Define service level objectives and alerting that catch problems before customers do.
  • Lead troubleshooting and resolution of production incidents. Run blameless post-incident reviews and track follow-up actions to completion.
  • Automate recurring operational work and remediation, reducing manual toil.
  • Plan capacity and tune performance across the CDN, application, and data tiers.

Traffic protection and abuse mitigation

  • Design solutions that automatically identify harmful or unwanted traffic, including scraping, malicious bots, credential stuffing, fake account creation, and API key abuse.
  • Configure and tune CDN, WAF, bot management, and rate-limiting controls to block abusive traffic without degrading the experience for legitimate users and clients.
  • Analyze traffic logs to understand how abusive actors behave, how they evade controls, and what they cost in infrastructure load and revenue.
  • Investigate new abuse patterns and trends, and work with the Data Abuse & Detection Engineer to turn findings into enforced edge and application controls.
  • Enforce acceptable-use and terms-of-service policies at the infrastructure level.

Infrastructure security

  • Manage infrastructure as code and apply security policy checks before changes reach production.
  • Apply least-privilege IAM, network segmentation, TLS management, and secrets handling across AWS environments.
  • Integrate security checks into CI/CD pipelines in partnership with the DevSecOps Lead, including dependency, container, and configuration scanning.
  • Detect and remediate configuration drift, and maintain centralized logging that supports both operations and security investigations.
  • Provide evidence from automated controls for audits and client security questionnaires.

Collaboration

  • Work with Engineering, Marketing, Product, and Legal/Compliance to update policies, close product loopholes, and protect site quality and data integrity.
  • Help marketing and product teams understand how traffic quality affects analytics, conversion metrics, and campaign reporting.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in computer science, a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • 3 years of experience with security attacks and mitigation methods, particularly bot, scraping, and application-layer threats.
  • Hands-on experience with CDN providers (Akamai, Cloudflare, Fastly) and their traffic management, WAF, and bot management features.
  • Experience with Elastic/OpenSearch or a comparable platform for log mining and analytics.
  • Solid understanding of TCP/IP, DNS, HTTP, and TLS, and how to manage traffic at each layer.
  • Proficiency in Linux administration and scripting (Python, Bash, or similar).
  • Experience operating production systems in a public cloud environment.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Infrastructure as code (e.g. Terraform).
  • Experience integrating security tooling into CI/CD pipelines.
  • Container and orchestration experience, including container security basics.
  • Observability tooling (e.g. Datadog).
  • Experience protecting high-traffic commercial APIs.
  • Familiarity with SLOs, error budgets, and incident management practices.
  • Exposure to SOC 2 or ISO 27001 control environments.

Benefits
- Flexible PTO
- 401k match
- Dental/Vision/Medical

title: Software Engineer II - Compute
description:
About the role and team

At Uber’s Infrastructure organization we are relentlessly raising the bar for reliability and availability, while designing a truly cloud native platform that seamlessly runs on multiple cloud providers. We are the Compute team at Uber, and are looking for a strong engineer to come shape the next version of our Compute platform. We own the foundational compute systems used by every product team at Uber - from control plane services such as node health monitoring to leveraging the latest kernel features to deliver graceful degradation at high utilization. Along the way, we get to present our work at leading conferences such as Linux Plumbers. Our company mission is to make transportation as reliable as running water, and we need technical powerhouses to build the dependable, high-performance foundation that supports that vision.

You will contribute to the complex infrastructures spanning global data centers and multiple cloud providers, supporting a diverse variety of workloads. You’ll need to make smart decisions with imperfect information and own the outcomes of global architectural choices. If you lead with clarity, build with heart, and are motivated by the challenge of peak efficiency at unparalleled scale - this is where you’ll make your mark.

What you’ll do

  • Design and build end-to-end systems for orchestration, monitoring, or frameworks that stand the test of massive global scale and high availability.
  • Build a world class, extensible multi-cloud compute platform. Collaborate closely with stakeholders in the big cloud providers to influence their roadmaps per Uber’s business needs.
  • Learn from, and often contribute to, the leading edge in Linux open source to enable graceful degradation when there is resource contention
  • Contribute to team charter by reviewing code and designs while fostering a culture of continuous learning and humility. You will balance being AI-first while ensuring the quality of our code does not drop.

Basic Qualifications

  • 3+ years of professional experience building scalable, fault-tolerant platforms, with a track record of delivering business critical services in the cloud.
  • Proficiency in Go, C/C++ or Java) and the ability to define organization-wide standards.
  • Proven experience leading large-scale engineering projects through the entire lifecycle from inception to global productionization.
  • Experience identifying architectural gaps and acting as a multiplier to reduce technical debt across the organization.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, or equivalent practical experience.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with operating a large fleet of Linux machines. Hands-on experience with Linux internals or container orchestration.
  • Experience building Compute platform in AWS/Azure/GCP/OCI. .
  • Experience in designing Linux features that boost fleet wide resource utilization.
  • Experience in driving cross-team projects.

For Seattle, WA-based roles: The base salary range for this role is USD $171,000 per year - USD $190,000 per year.

title: Project Manager
description:
Project Manager

Job Description

Exempt

title: Experienced P&C Field Services Technician
description:
WSP is currently initiating a search for a POWER Testing and Energization (PTE) Experienced P&C Field Services Technician based in Wisconsin or Minnesota. Successful applicants will be involved in projects with our PTE Team and be part of a growing organization that solves problems and supports client needs in electrical testing and commissioning for utility substations, industrial, and bulk electrical power systems.

This Opportunity

  • Supports a wide range of testing and commissioning activities through application of client testing standards, industry standards (IEEE, NETA, NFPA, NESC), and manufacturer recommendations
  • Works under limited supervision, independently executing moderately complex assignments, and contributing to regulatory compliance, safety adherence, and data integrity across active job sites
  • Provides day-to-day support to field teams, helps resolve challenges on-site, and mentors junior technicians to promote quality, efficiency, and safe work practices
  • As one of the world’s leading professional services firms, WSP now brings world-class expertise in power delivery, power generation, and project management with the recent acquisition of POWER Engineers, Inc. Our vision is to be the preeminent pure-play global consulting firm for the world’s energy transition—and we need your help.

Your Impact

  • Perform assigned testing and commissioning tasks for Protection and Control systems on high voltage substations
  • Perform on-site hands-on protective relay testing using relay test sets such as Omicron CMC 256/356 or Doble F6150. Examples of relays to be tested are SEL-311L, SEL-387, SEL-487, SEL-421, SEL-351S, GE L90, GE D60 among others
  • Use field forms, digital data tools, and mobile applications to document site activities
  • Perform equipment cleaning, inventory control, and calibration as directed

  • Perform additional responsibilities as required by business needs

Who You Are

Required Qualifications

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Minimum of 7 years of experience in the electrical testing industry, including experience in medium and high voltage circuit breakers, power transformers, instrument transformers, and substation protection and controls testing
  • Demonstrable expertise on transmission, generation, and distribution relays (SEL, Basler, Beckwith, and GE families) and protective schemes
  • Technical skills related to protective relays include relay calibration utilizing test sets/measuring devices such as Omicron CMC 256/356 and Doble F6150, control scheme testing, testing of the sensing CT/PT circuits, ability to upload settings to microprocessor relays, and static & dynamic testing of microprocessor-based protective relays
  • Proven experience with electrical field testing standards, practices, and procedures, such as NETA, IEEE, and NFPA applicable standards
  • Demonstrable knowledge of testing electrical distribution, generation, and transmission projects with voltage levels ranging from 15 kV to 500 kV, including protective relays and circuit breakers
  • Experience using technical software such as ProTesT, Protection Suite, ENOSERV RTS, Omicron Test Universe, and AcSELerator Quickset for testing purposes and data review
  • Experience with reading and understanding electrical drawings
  • Ability to identify routine field challenges and equipment issues, responding within established procedures and escalating atypical conditions
  • Skilled in preparing field logs, sketches, and digital reports
  • Physical stamina to work in outdoor and physically demanding conditions
  • Experience collaborating with contractors, technicians, and engineers
  • Demonstrated commitment to field safety, quality, and regulatory compliance
  • Good interpersonal and verbal communication skills for field team collaboration
  • Capable of critical thinking and problem-solving skills to apply technical knowledge to reach conclusions from inspection and testing results
  • Capability to support a wide variety of tasks in dynamic or changing environments
  • Ability to follow procedures, meet deadlines, and maintain accountability in the field
  • Commitment to continued learning and development in technical field services
  • Understanding of confidentiality and ethical behavior in technical environments
  • Competent self-leadership with attention to detail, multi-tasking, and prioritization of responsibilities in a dynamic work environment
  • Reliable, punctual, with the ability to work independently or with a team
  • Proven track record of upholding workplace safety and ability to abide by WSP’s health, safety, drug/alcohol, and harassment policies

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in testing and commissioning electrical equipment on high voltage substations such as CTs, CCVTs, PLC systems, and DC systems, including batteries and battery chargers
  • Current OSHA 30-hour or 40-hour HAZWOPER certification

title: Sterile Processing Technician II Certified
description:
Overview

Shift: Full-time; Monday - Friday, 12:30 pm - 9:00 pm, for 80 hours. There is a holiday and weekend rotation.

The Sterile Processing Technician II Certified is a skilled professional who plays a critical role in supporting safe, high-quality patient care. In addition to performing instrument decontamination, assembly, sterilization, and distribution, this position serves as a resource for the department by mentoring team members, supporting training efforts, and contributing to quality improvement initiatives. Through advanced technical expertise and a commitment to excellence, this role helps ensure regulatory compliance, operational efficiency, and the highest standards of patient safety.

Why UnityPoint Health?

At UnityPoint Health, you matter. We’re proud to be recognized as a Top 150 Place to Work in Healthcare by Becker's Healthcare several years in a row for our commitment to our team members.

Our competitive Total Rewards program offers benefits options that align with your needs and priorities, no matter what life stage you’re in. Here are just a few:

  • Expect paid time off, parental leave, 401K matching and an employee recognition program.
  • Dental and health insurance, paid holidays, short and long-term disability and more. We even offer pet insurance for your four-legged family members.
  • Early access to earned wages with Daily Pay, tuition reimbursement to help further your career and adoption assistance to help you grow your family.

With a collective goal to champion a culture of belonging where everyone feels valued and respected, we honor the ways people are unique and embrace what brings us together.

And, we believe equipping you with support and development opportunities is a vital part of delivering an exceptional employment experience.

Find a fulfilling career and make a difference with UnityPoint Health.

Responsibilities

  • Decontaminate, clean, inspect, and reprocess surgical instruments, equipment, and medical devices in accordance with manufacturer guidelines and infection prevention standards.
  • Operate automated washers, sterilizers, and high-level disinfection equipment to ensure safe, effective instrument processing.
  • Assemble and verify instrument trays with a high degree of accuracy to support surgical and procedural readiness.
  • Inspect instruments for cleanliness, functionality, and quality; coordinate repairs and remove defective items from service when needed.
  • Configure and monitor sterilization cycles, ensuring compliance with required time, temperature, and quality standards.
  • Maintain organized, compliant storage and work areas to support sterile processing best practices.
  • Complete detailed documentation to ensure regulatory compliance, traceability, and quality assurance.
  • Serve as a resource to clinical teams by communicating equipment needs and supporting operational efficiency.
  • Mentor and train new team members while contributing to quality improvement and infection prevention initiatives.
  • Escalate critical issues to leadership and support ongoing departmental operations.

Qualifications

Education:

  • High School Diploma or equivalent required.

Experience:

  • Minimum of two (2) years of sterile processing or surgical services experience required.

License(s)/Certification(s):

  • Certified through one of the following is required:
    • Certified Registered Central Service Technician - Healthcare Sterile Processing Association (HSPA)
    • Certified Sterile Processing and Distribution Technician - Certification Board for Sterile Processing & Distribution (CBSPD)
    • Certified Surgical Technologist - National Board of Surgical Technology and Surgical Assisting (NBSTSA)
    • Surgical Technician-Certified is acceptable in conjunction with CRCST or CSPDT - National Center for Competency Testing (NCCT)
  • IA & IL Child Abuse Mandatory Reporter Training in state(s) where providing care required within 90 days of hire.
  • IA & IL Adult Dependent Abuse Mandatory Reporter Training in state(s) where providing care required within 90 days of hire.

description:
You Matter

Perks and Benefits
